files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@
+\set ON_ERROR_STOP on
+
+-- Promotion records are shared by model digest and may move to a later evaluation.
+-- A committed crown permanently makes that specific winning submission public.
+BEGIN;
+SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s';
+
+CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW control_plane.dashboard_evaluation_history WITH (security_barrier='true') AS
+ SELECT c.netuid,
+    c.chain_generation,
+    c.name AS competition,
+    SUBSTRING(encode(public.digest((e.upload_id)::text, 'sha256'::text), 'hex'::text) FROM 1 FOR 16) AS challenge_id,
+    r.hotkey,
+    identity.coldkey,
+    r.uid,
+    baseline.hotkey AS baseline_hotkey,
+    COALESCE(baseline_identity.coldkey, baseline_identity_fallback.coldkey) AS baseline_coldkey,
+    baseline.uid AS baseline_uid,
+        CASE
+            WHEN ((e.state = 'terminal_failure'::text) OR (e.verdict = 'failed'::text)) THEN 'failed'::text
+            WHEN (e.verdict = 'accepted'::text) THEN 'accepted'::text
+            ELSE 'rejected'::text
+        END AS verdict,
+    (e.verdict_summary ->> 'mu_hat'::text) AS mu_hat,
+    (e.verdict_summary ->> 'lcb'::text) AS lcb,
+    COALESCE((e.verdict_summary ->> 'delta'::text), (e.verdict_summary ->> 'delta_threshold'::text)) AS delta,
+    (e.verdict_summary ->> 'avg_king_loss'::text) AS avg_king_loss,
+    (e.verdict_summary ->> 'avg_challenger_loss'::text) AS avg_challenger_loss,
+    (e.verdict_summary ->> 'wall_time_s'::text) AS wall_time_s,
+    (e.verdict_summary ->> 'n_sequences_evaluated'::text) AS n_sequences_evaluated,
+    (e.verdict_summary ->> 'n_sequences'::text) AS n_sequences,
+    (e.verdict_summary ->> 'early_stopped'::text) AS early_stopped,
+        CASE
+            WHEN (e.public_error_code = ANY (ARRAY['invalid_evaluation_input'::text, 'config_rejected'::text, 'model_copy'::text, 'evaluator_busy'::text, 'evaluator_job_lost'::text, 'evaluation_failed'::text, 'protocol_invalid'::text, 'retry_exhausted'::text, 'safetensors_reuse_limit'::text])) THEN e.public_error_code
+            WHEN (e.public_error_code IS NULL) THEN NULL::text
+            ELSE 'evaluation_failed'::text
+        END AS public_error_code,
+    e.policy_version,
+    e.dataset_version,
+    e.completed_at,
+        CASE
+            WHEN (published_reign.reign_id IS NOT NULL OR p.state = 'promoted'::text) THEN u.model_name
+            ELSE NULL::text
+        END AS public_model_name,
+        CASE
+            WHEN (published_reign.reign_id IS NOT NULL) THEN published_reign.model_digest
+            WHEN (p.state = 'promoted'::text) THEN p.model_digest
+            ELSE NULL::bpchar
+        END AS public_model_digest,
+        CASE
+            WHEN (published_reign.reign_id IS NOT NULL) THEN published_reign.public_prefix
+            WHEN (p.state = 'promoted'::text) THEN p.public_prefix
+            ELSE NULL::text
+        END AS public_model_reference,
+        CASE
+            WHEN (published_reign.reign_id IS NOT NULL) THEN 'winner'::text
+            WHEN (p.state = 'promoted'::text) THEN p.disposition
+            ELSE NULL::text
+        END AS publication_disposition,
+    COALESCE(( SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('source', COALESCE(NULLIF((shard_group.value ->> 'source'::text), ''::text), 'dataset'::text), 'names', COALESCE(( SELECT jsonb_agg(regexp_replace(split_part(split_part((shard_ref.value #>> '{}'::text[]), '?'::text, 1), '#'::text, 1), '^.*/'::text, ''::text) ORDER BY shard_ref.ordinality)
+                   FROM jsonb_array_elements(
+                        CASE
+                            WHEN (jsonb_typeof((shard_group.value -> 'refs'::text)) = 'array'::text) THEN (shard_group.value -> 'refs'::text)
+                            ELSE '[]'::jsonb
+                        END) WITH ORDINALITY shard_ref(value, ordinality)
+                  WHERE (jsonb_typeof(shard_ref.value) = 'string'::text)), '[]'::jsonb)) ORDER BY shard_group.ordinality)
+           FROM jsonb_array_elements(
+                CASE
+                    WHEN (jsonb_typeof(COALESCE((e.verdict_summary -> 'shards_used'::text), (e.verdict_summary #> '{dataset,shards_used}'::text[]), '[]'::jsonb)) = 'array'::text) THEN COALESCE((e.verdict_summary -> 'shards_used'::text), (e.verdict_summary #> '{dataset,shards_used}'::text[]), '[]'::jsonb)
+                    ELSE '[]'::jsonb
+                END) WITH ORDINALITY shard_group(value, ordinality)
+          WHERE (jsonb_typeof(shard_group.value) = 'object'::text)), '[]'::jsonb) AS shards_used
+   FROM ((((((((((((control_plane.evaluations e
+     JOIN control_plane.uploads u ON ((u.upload_id = e.upload_id)))
+     JOIN control_plane.registrations r ON ((r.registration_id = u.registration_id)))
+     JOIN control_plane.competitions c ON ((c.competition_id = e.competition_id)))
+     JOIN control_plane.king_reigns baseline ON ((baseline.reign_id = e.claimed_king_reign_id)))
+     LEFT JOIN control_plane.model_promotions p ON (((p.evaluation_id = e.evaluation_id) AND (p.state = 'promoted'::text) AND ((p.disposition = 'non_winner'::text) OR (EXISTS ( SELECT 1
+           FROM control_plane.king_reigns published_winner
+          WHERE ((published_winner.causing_evaluation_id = e.evaluation_id) AND (published_winner.accepted_upload_id = e.upload_id) AND (published_winner.model_digest = p.model_digest))))))))
+     LEFT JOIN control_plane.metagraph_snapshots identity_snapshot ON (((identity_snapshot.netuid = r.netuid) AND (identity_snapshot.chain_generation = r.chain_generation) AND (identity_snapshot.finalized_block = r.last_seen_finalized_block) AND identity_snapshot.is_complete)))
+     LEFT JOIN control_plane.metagraph_uid_assignments identity ON (((identity.snapshot_id = identity_snapshot.snapshot_id) AND (identity.uid = r.uid) AND (identity.hotkey = r.hotkey))))
+     LEFT JOIN control_plane.uploads baseline_upload ON ((baseline_upload.upload_id = baseline.accepted_upload_id)))
+     LEFT JOIN control_plane.registrations baseline_registration ON (((baseline_registration.registration_id = baseline_upload.registration_id) AND (baseline_registration.hotkey = baseline.hotkey))))
+     LEFT JOIN control_plane.metagraph_snapshots baseline_snapshot ON (((baseline_snapshot.netuid = c.netuid) AND (baseline_snapshot.chain_generation = c.chain_generation) AND (baseline_snapshot.finalized_block = baseline_registration.last_seen_finalized_block) AND baseline_snapshot.is_complete)))
+     LEFT JOIN control_plane.metagraph_uid_assignments baseline_identity ON (((baseline_identity.snapshot_id = baseline_snapshot.snapshot_id) AND (baseline_identity.uid = baseline_registration.uid) AND (baseline_identity.hotkey = baseline.hotkey))))
+     LEFT JOIN LATERAL ( SELECT assignment.coldkey
+           FROM (control_plane.metagraph_snapshots snapshot
+             JOIN control_plane.metagraph_uid_assignments assignment ON ((assignment.snapshot_id = snapshot.snapshot_id)))
+          WHERE ((baseline_identity.coldkey IS NULL) AND (snapshot.netuid = c.netuid) AND (snapshot.chain_generation = c.chain_generation) AND (assignment.hotkey = baseline.hotkey) AND snapshot.is_complete)
+          ORDER BY snapshot.finalized_block DESC
+         LIMIT 1) baseline_identity_fallback ON (true))
+     LEFT JOIN control_plane.king_reigns published_reign
+       ON published_reign.competition_id = e.competition_id
+      AND published_reign.model_digest = u.model_digest
+      AND published_reign.causing_evaluation_id = e.evaluation_id
+      AND published_reign.accepted_upload_id = e.upload_id
+  WHERE (e.state = ANY (ARRAY['completed'::text, 'terminal_failure'::text]));
+
+
+ALTER VIEW control_plane.dashboard_evaluation_history OWNER TO teutonic_schema_owner;
+GRANT SELECT ON TABLE control_plane.dashboard_evaluation_history TO teutonic_dashboard_view;
+
+COMMIT;

@@ -768,10 +768,35 @@ and MIX02 has no special sampling path. DCLM is the single category `dclm-baseli
 
 Keep `TEUTONIC_COMPETITION` set to the existing MAIN database name on every control
 plane service. One validator, promotion worker, and weight publisher serve all seven.
-MIXes start without kings. A kingless MIX challenges the **latest MAIN king** using
-that MIX's categories and threshold. If MAIN changes before coronation, the old
-comparison is requeued against the latest MAIN without consuming a failure retry.
-After its first win, a MIX uses its own latest king.
+MIXes start without kings. A kingless MIX challenges a **fixed starting MAIN king**
+using that MIX's categories and threshold. `starting_reign_id` is pinned once at
+initialization; later MAIN promotions do not change claims, retries, or coronation
+checks for that MIX. After its first win, a MIX uses its own current king.
+Configuration refreshes preserve the pin. `competitions.json` includes a
+`starting_king` object with the pinned reign ID, model digest, public model reference,
+name, UID, and hotkey; a starting king does not count as a MIX king or receive MIX rewards.
+
+For an existing deployment that follows the latest MAIN, use the following update.
+Let active evaluations finish and their promotions commit, then stop the validator
+and promotion worker before pulling the new code. This prevents a MAIN promotion
+between selecting the fixed starting point and switching the workers to the new rule.
+
+```bash
+pm2 stop teutonic-validator teutonic-promotion-worker
+git pull --ff-only
+docker compose exec -T postgres sh -c \
+  'psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" --no-psqlrc -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1' \
+  < scripts/db/pin_mix_starting_kings.sql

files.name: scripts/db/pin_mix_starting_kings.sql
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+\set ON_ERROR_STOP on
+
+-- Pin once to MAIN at application time. Re-running never moves an existing pin.
+BEGIN;
+SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s';
+ALTER TABLE control_plane.competitions
+    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS starting_reign_id uuid
+    REFERENCES control_plane.king_reigns(reign_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT;
+
+UPDATE control_plane.competitions c
+   SET starting_reign_id = main.current_reign_id
+  FROM control_plane.competitions main
+ WHERE c.main_competition_id = main.competition_id
+   AND c.competition_key ~ '^mix[0-9]{2}$' AND c.active
+   AND c.current_reign_id IS NULL AND c.starting_reign_id IS NULL
+   AND main.current_reign_id IS NOT NULL;
+
+DO $$
+BEGIN
+    IF EXISTS (
+        SELECT 1 FROM control_plane.competitions
+         WHERE active AND competition_key ~ '^mix[0-9]{2}$'
+           AND current_reign_id IS NULL AND starting_reign_id IS NULL
+    ) THEN
+        RAISE EXCEPTION 'cannot pin a kingless MIX without a current MAIN king';
+    END IF;
+END $$;
+
+CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW control_plane.dashboard_competitions WITH (security_barrier=true) AS
+SELECT c.netuid, c.chain_generation, c.name AS competition, c.competition_key,
+       main.name AS main_competition, c.current_reign_id IS NOT NULL AS has_king,
+       ec.config_version, ec.eval_n, ec.delta_threshold,
+       c.active, main.reward_transition,
+       COALESCE((ec.long_documents->>'token_budget')::bigint, 0) AS document_tokens,
+       CASE WHEN starting.reign_id IS NOT NULL THEN jsonb_build_object(
+           'reign_id', starting.reign_id, 'reign_number', starting.reign_number,
+           'model_digest', starting.model_digest, 'model_reference', starting.public_prefix,
+           'model_repo', starting_upload.model_name, 'uid', starting.uid, 'hotkey', starting.hotkey
+       ) END AS starting_king
+  FROM control_plane.competitions c
+  JOIN control_plane.competitions main ON main.competition_id=COALESCE(c.main_competition_id,c.competition_id)
+  JOIN control_plane.evaluation_configs ec ON ec.competition_id=c.competition_id AND ec.active
+  LEFT JOIN control_plane.king_reigns starting ON starting.reign_id=c.starting_reign_id
+  LEFT JOIN control_plane.uploads starting_upload ON starting_upload.upload_id=starting.accepted_upload_id;
+ALTER VIEW control_plane.dashboard_competitions OWNER TO teutonic_schema_owner;
+GRANT SELECT ON control_plane.dashboard_competitions TO teutonic_dashboard_view;
+
+SELECT c.name AS competition, starting.reign_id AS starting_reign_id,
+       starting.uid AS starting_uid, starting.model_digest AS starting_model_digest
+  FROM control_plane.competitions c
+  LEFT JOIN control_plane.king_reigns starting ON starting.reign_id=c.starting_reign_id
+ WHERE c.active AND c.competition_key ~ '^mix[0-9]{2}$' AND c.current_reign_id IS NULL
+ ORDER BY c.netuid, c.chain_generation, c.name;
+COMMIT;

 # DaniLabs Subnet
 
-Bittensor validator code for DaniLabs.
+DaniLabs is a Bittensor subnet for distributed AI inference. This repository is
+home to its validator software: the code that evaluates miner performance,
+calculates scores, and submits weights to Bittensor.
 
-Validators evaluate miner performance, calculate scores, and submit weights to the
-chain.
+The validator's role is to determine how miners are rewarded for the inference
+work they contribute. This repo is intended for validator operators and
+contributors developing the subnet's evaluation and incentive rules.
 
-Validator code and setup instructions will be added here.
+## Validator responsibilities
 
-**Miners:** use the ManagedVNetIR miner kit. Its repository link will be added when
-available.
+The validator is being developed to:
+
+- Track subnet state and associate registered miners with their on-chain
+  identities.
+- Check the source, format, and freshness of performance reports, rejecting
+  invalid or duplicate submissions.
+- Evaluate inference performance using latency, token throughput, completed
+  requests, and availability.
+- Calculate miner scores using consistent, documented evaluation rules.
+- Convert eligible miner scores into weights and submit them to Bittensor.
+
+## Scoring
+
+The goal is to reward useful, fast, reliable inference. Scoring needs to account
+for both performance and successful completion, so generation speed alone does
+not determine a miner's score.
+
+The scoring formula, eligibility requirements, and measurement definitions are
+still being developed. They will be documented and tested here before live
+weight submission is enabled. Validator reports should contain operational
+measurements, without customer prompts or generated responses.
+
+## Current status
+
+This repository currently contains documentation only. The validator
+implementation, tests, configuration, and operator setup instructions will be
+added as development progresses.

files.name: docs/operator-pilot.md
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,155 @@
+# Validator observer pilot
+
+This release reads finalized Finney state for an explicitly configured subnet. It opens no wallet,
+contains no transaction writer, and does not maintain burn weights. Keep the
+existing burn process running while this observer is tested. No deployment or
+chain configuration changes are part of installing the source.
+
+## Host
+
+Use a Linux CPU host with **4 vCPUs, 8 GB RAM and 50 GB SSD** as a practical
+starting allocation; **8 vCPUs and 16 GB RAM** leaves room for later report
+processing. These are DaniLabs planning estimates, not Bittensor protocol
+minimums or a measured capacity guarantee. This observer does not run inference
+and needs no GPU. GPU requirements for future verification are undecided.
+
+Use Python 3.11 or 3.12 in an isolated environment. The chain adapter follows the
+existing SDK 9.12.2 storage-query interface and pins that dependency. Verify its
+native dependencies on the selected Linux architecture during host acceptance;
+do not assume newer SDK APIs are drop-in replacements. The official generic
+[compute template](https://github.com/RaoFoundation/bittensor-subnet-template/blob/main/min_compute.yml)
+is a subnet-authoring example, not a universal GPU requirement for validators.
+
+The process needs outbound HTTPS/WSS access to a trusted Finney RPC, DNS and
+correct host time. Historical state is needed for settlement evidence. There is
+no inbound server, public axon or local chain node in this observer. A future
+challenge protocol may introduce additional network requirements. Keep private
+keys and wallet directories inaccessible to the observer user.
+
+## Local setup
+
+Run from the repository root:
+
+```sh
+python3 -m venv .venv
+.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e .
+cp config/observer.example.json config/observer.local.json
+```
+
+Set `netuid` to the subnet you operate before running the commands below. There
+is no default subnet identifier. The local configuration is ignored by Git.
+
+```sh
+.venv/bin/dani-validator --config config/observer.local.json status
+.venv/bin/dani-validator --config config/observer.local.json shadow
+.venv/bin/dani-validator --config config/observer.local.json watch --count 3
+```
+
+The commands above query public chain data. Only `watch` writes local observer
+state. Keep local configurations outside Git if they contain operational paths.
+If the Python installation lacks a working default CA bundle, point
+`SSL_CERT_FILE` to the installed certifi CA file; TLS verification stays enabled.
+The example deliberately leaves public identity pins empty. A missing pin blocks
+the burn guard; it does not silently trust the first owner or assume UID 0.
+
+After independently confirming the identities, fill `expected_owner_hotkey`,
+`expected_owner_coldkey`, `expected_owner_registration_block`,
+`validator_hotkey`, and `expected_validator_registration_block`. These are public
+addresses and registration blocks, never seeds or private keys. The chain's
+`Uids` and `Keys` mappings must agree at one finalized hash. The observer records
+the current owner UID, validator UID, permit, raw stake fields, weight row and
+source block/hash. `stake_weight_raw` is the chain's normalized u16 consensus
+weight, not a TAO balance; the separately named raw stake fields remain raw.
+
+`shadow` currently reports `pending_authenticated_reports` and emits no scores.
+There is no signed validator-report contract or approved scoring formula yet.
+An account token, miner telemetry or local JSON file is not accepted as trusted
+reward evidence. This is an executable observer, not a completed validator.
+
+## Reading the burn evidence
+
+Keep three questions separate:
+
+1. Does this validator's finalized weight row assign exactly 65,535 to the
+   current owner UID and nothing else?
+2. Was the latest epoch's withheld miner incentive destroyed under `Burn`, or
+   returned under `Recycle`?
+3. What proportion of the whole subnet's miner incentive was withheld?
+
+A validator controls its own row. Other validators and consensus affect the
+network result. Neither a fresh `LastUpdate` nor a submitted row proves that
+the subnet burned 100% of its miner incentive. Owner cut, validator dividends and
+liquidity injections are separate from miner incentive.
+
+The runtime's `MinerBurned` counter includes both burning and recycling. The
+observer keeps its raw encoding and source block. It queries the settlement's
+parent-state `RecycleOrBurn`, because epoch settlement occurs before that
+block's extrinsics. Missing archive data yields unavailable evidence.
+
+`miner_burned_semantics` is null by default: the field's metadata name alone does
+not establish its fixed-point scale. Only after reviewing the deployed runtime,
+configure an object with `spec_version`, `fractional_bits: 32`, and a `source`
+URL pinned to the exact 40-character Subtensor commit containing
+`pallets/subtensor/src/coinbase/run_coinbase.rs`. This acknowledges the reviewed
+U96F32 encoding; the observer cannot verify that review on your behalf. A runtime
+version mismatch, upgrade at settlement, malformed value, absent source,
+unverified registration or burn mode leaves full-burn verification unavailable.
+There is no automatic fallback to 100%.
+
+The guard also blocks unverified commit/reveal compatibility, extra mechanisms,
+identity changes and regressing finalized state. Passing its checks authorizes
+no transaction and is not a complete weight-writer preflight.
+
+## Process supervision
+
+The uninstalled template is in `deploy/danilabs-validator-observer.service`.
+For a later reviewed host deployment, use a dedicated `dani-validator` user,
+read-only source/virtualenv under `/opt/danilabs/subnet`, configuration under
+`/etc/danilabs/validator-observer.json`, and set `state_file` to
+`/var/lib/danilabs-validator/observer.json`. The systemd sandbox permits writes
+only to its state directory. It requires no wallet mounts or public ports.
+Observe JSON output in the journal; alerts for stalled polling and RPC failures
+remain an operator responsibility. Do not replace an existing burn service with
+this unit.
+
+## Before adding a burn writer
+
+Preserve and audit the existing writer first. Confirm the deployed runtime,
+owner/validator registration, effective stake, permit, mechanism count,
+commit/reveal path, version key, weight limits and rate limit at finalized state.
+Read all relevant validator rows and pending commits. Test any future writer on
+localnet or testnet, isolate the hotkey signer, and wait for finalization before
+reading back the exact row. Never load a coldkey private key into this process.
+
+Burn maintenance must run independently of inference reports so no GPU or
+missing report can stall it. Never disable commit/reveal or change network
+hyperparameters merely to fit an older writer. Do not set the newer subnet
+emission-vector burn slot to 100%: that slot is currently reserved at zero and
+is distinct from directing miner incentive to owner-associated burn UIDs.
+
+Only after stable observation and burn verification should a separate real
+miner be registered, served, challenged and scored in shadow. Check its owner
+association: miner incentive sent to owner-associated hotkeys is withheld. Live
+score weights and other validators require authenticated report/challenge
+evidence, documented scoring, replay protection, identity-at-epoch validation,
+and an explicit activation step in a later release.
+
+## Verification
+
+```sh
+PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
+```
+
+Tests use an injected fake substrate and never touch a wallet or chain. They
+cover finalized source hashes, network pins, recycled UIDs, changed owners,
+unknown burn evidence, archive failures and settlement-time mode. Native SDK
+installation and live RPC compatibility still need host acceptance.
+
+## Primary references
+
+- [Validating and permit rules](https://www.bittensor.com/docs/guides/validating)
+- [Mining and owner-associated hotkeys](https://www.bittensor.com/docs/guides/mining)
+- [Runtime miner-incentive settlement](https://github.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/blob/main/pallets/subtensor/src/coinbase/run_coinbase.rs)
+- [Runtime weight checks](https://github.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/blob/main/pallets/subtensor/src/subnets/weights.rs)
+- [Storage fields and MinerBurned semantics](https://guides.learnbittensor.org/subtensor-api/storage)
+- [Subnet emission-vector constraints](https://www.bittensor.com/docs/guides/etao)

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import time
+
+from .chain import ChainUnavailable, FinalizedChain
+from .config import load_settings
+from .monitor import assess, load_state, save_state
+
+
+def main(argv=None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Read-only DaniLabs finalized-chain observer; never signs transactions")
+    parser.add_argument("--config", required=True)
+    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+    sub.add_parser("status", help="Inspect one finalized snapshot")
+    sub.add_parser("shadow", help="Inspect identity; scoring is pending authenticated reports")
+    watch = sub.add_parser("watch", help="Poll and persist local observer state")
+    watch.add_argument("--count", type=int, default=0, help="Number of polls; 0 watches continuously")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    if args.command == "watch" and args.count < 0:
+        parser.error("--count must be non-negative")
+    try:
+        settings = load_settings(args.config)
+        chain = FinalizedChain(settings)
+        previous = load_state(settings.state_file)
+        count = 0
+        while True:
+            try:
+                snapshot = chain.snapshot()
+                result = assess(snapshot, settings, previous)
+                if args.command == "shadow":
+                    result["shadow"] = {"status": "pending", "reason": "No authenticated validator report contract or approved scoring formula exists yet", "scores": None, "weights_submitted": False}
+                print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True), flush=True)
+                if args.command == "watch":
+                    save_state(settings.state_file, snapshot)
+                previous = snapshot
+            except ChainUnavailable as exc:
+                print(json.dumps({"status": "unavailable", "error": str(exc), "chain_writes": False, "burn_guard": {"checks_passed": False}, "last_epoch_100_percent_miner_burn_verified": None}), flush=True)
+                if args.command != "watch":
+                    return 2
+            count += 1
+            if args.command != "watch" or (args.count > 0 and count >= args.count):
+                return 0
+            time.sleep(settings.poll_seconds)
+    except (OSError, ValueError, ImportError) as exc:
+        print(json.dumps({"status": "configuration_error", "error": str(exc), "chain_writes": False}), flush=True)
+        return 2
+    except KeyboardInterrupt:
+        return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,154 @@
+"""Read every snapshot at a single finalized block. No wallet or extrinsic API."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from typing import Any
+
+from .config import Settings
+
+
+class ChainUnavailable(RuntimeError):
+    pass
+
+
+def value(item: Any) -> Any:
+    return getattr(item, "value", item)
+
+
+def unsigned_newtype(raw):
+    """SDK9 decodes some unsigned newtypes as singleton lists."""
+    candidate = raw[0] if isinstance(raw, (list, tuple)) and len(raw) == 1 else raw
+    return candidate if type(candidate) is int and candidate >= 0 else None
+
+
+def create_subtensor(endpoint: str):
+    import bittensor as bt
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
+    bt.Subtensor.add_args(parser)
+    config = bt.Config(parser=parser, args=["--subtensor.chain_endpoint", endpoint])
+    return bt.Subtensor(network=endpoint, config=config)
+
+
+class FinalizedChain:
+    def __init__(self, settings: Settings, substrate=None):
+        self.settings = settings
+        self.settings.validate()
+        self.substrate = substrate
+
+    def snapshot(self) -> dict:
+        try:
+            if self.substrate is None:
+                self.substrate = create_subtensor(self.settings.chain_endpoint).substrate
+            s = self.substrate
+            genesis = s.get_block_hash(0)
+            if genesis != self.settings.expected_genesis:
+                raise ChainUnavailable("Chain genesis does not match the configured Finney pin")
+            block_hash = s.rpc_request("chain_getFinalizedHead", [])["result"]
+            header = s.rpc_request("chain_getHeader", [block_hash])["result"]
+            block = int(header["number"], 16)
+            runtime = s.rpc_request("state_getRuntimeVersion", [block_hash])["result"]
+            errors = {}
+
+            def query(name, params, *, required=False, at_hash=None):
+                try:
+                    return value(s.query("SubtensorModule", name, params, block_hash=at_hash or block_hash))
+                except Exception:
+                    if required:
+                        raise ChainUnavailable(f"Required finalized field unavailable: {name}")
+                    errors[f"{name}@{at_hash or block_hash}"] = "unavailable"
+                    return None
+
+            n = self.settings.netuid
+            if query("NetworksAdded", [n], required=True) is not True:
+                raise ChainUnavailable("Pinned subnet is not active")
+
+            def registration(hotkey):
+                if not hotkey:
+                    return None
+                uid = query("Uids", [n, hotkey])
+                if type(uid) is not int or uid < 0:
+                    return {"hotkey": hotkey, "registered": False}
+                mapped = query("Keys", [n, uid])
+                registered = query("BlockAtRegistration", [n, uid])
+                if mapped != hotkey or type(registered) is not int or not 0 <= registered <= block:
+                    return {"hotkey": hotkey, "uid": uid, "registered": False, "reason": "Finalized UID mapping is inconsistent"}
+                return {"hotkey": hotkey, "uid": uid, "registered": True, "registration_block": registered, "coldkey": query("Owner", [hotkey])}
+
+            owner_hotkey = query("SubnetOwnerHotkey", [n], required=True)
+            if not isinstance(owner_hotkey, str) or not owner_hotkey:
+                raise ChainUnavailable("Subnet owner hotkey is unavailable")
+            owner = registration(owner_hotkey)
+            validator = registration(self.settings.validator_hotkey)
+            owner_coldkey = query("SubnetOwner", [n], required=True)
+            permits = query("ValidatorPermit", [n])
+            stakes = query("StakeWeight", [n])
+            last_updates = query("LastUpdate", [n])
+            def validator_fields(registration):
+                if not registration or not registration.get("registered"):
+                    return
+                uid = registration["uid"]
+                for key, vector in (("validator_permit", permits), ("stake_weight_raw", stakes), ("last_update", last_updates)):
+                    registration[key] = vector[uid] if isinstance(vector, (list, tuple)) and uid < len(vector) else None
+                # Mechanism 0 uses the subnet's base storage index. Extra mechanisms
+                # are surfaced below and keep the burn guard blocked until supported.
+                registration["weights_raw"] = query("Weights", [n, uid])
+                registration["alpha_stake_rao_raw"] = query("TotalHotkeyAlpha", [registration["hotkey"], n])
+                registration["root_tao_stake_rao_raw"] = query("TotalHotkeyAlpha", [registration["hotkey"], 0])
+            # Inspect the owner's public row for operational reference without
+            # treating it as the configured validator or loading its wallet.
+            validator_fields(owner)
+            validator_fields(validator)
+            last_epoch = query("LastEpochBlock", [n])
+            epoch_source = "LastEpochBlock"
+            if type(last_epoch) is not int or last_epoch <= 0:
+                last_epoch = query("LastMechansimStepBlock", [n])
+                epoch_source = "LastMechansimStepBlock"
+            epoch_evidence = None
+            if type(last_epoch) is int and 0 < last_epoch <= block:
+                try:
+                    epoch_hash = s.get_block_hash(last_epoch)
+                    parent_hash = s.get_block_hash(last_epoch - 1)
+                    epoch_runtime = s.rpc_request("state_getRuntimeVersion", [epoch_hash])["result"]
+                    parent_runtime = s.rpc_request("state_getRuntimeVersion", [parent_hash])["result"]
+                    epoch_evidence = {
+                        "source_block": last_epoch, "source_hash": epoch_hash,
+                        "runtime_spec_version": epoch_runtime.get("specVersion"),
+                        # Settlement runs in on_initialize, before this block's
+                        # extrinsics. The prior block's mode governed that payout.
+                        "mode_source_block": last_epoch - 1, "mode_source_hash": parent_hash,
+                        "mode_runtime_spec_version": parent_runtime.get("specVersion"),
+                        "recycle_or_burn_raw": query("RecycleOrBurn", [n], at_hash=parent_hash),
+                        "miner_burned_raw": query("MinerBurned", [n], at_hash=epoch_hash),
+                    }
+                except Exception:
+                    errors["last_epoch_evidence"] = "unavailable; historical RPC may be required"
+            mechanism_count = query("MechanismCountCurrent", [n])
+            return {
+                "network": "finney", "genesis": genesis, "netuid": n,
+                "source_block": block, "source_hash": block_hash,
+                "observed_at_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
+                "runtime_spec_version": runtime.get("specVersion"),
+                "owner": owner, "subnet_owner_coldkey": owner_coldkey,
+                "owner_coldkey_matches": bool(owner and owner.get("registered") and isinstance(owner_coldkey, str) and owner.get("coldkey") == owner_coldkey),
+                "validator": validator,
+                "recycle_or_burn_raw": query("RecycleOrBurn", [n]),
+                "miner_burned_raw": query("MinerBurned", [n]),
+                "last_epoch_block": last_epoch, "last_epoch_source": epoch_source,
+                "last_epoch_evidence": epoch_evidence,
+                "tempo": query("Tempo", [n]),
+                "commit_reveal_enabled": query("CommitRevealWeightsEnabled", [n]),
+                "mechanism_count": unsigned_newtype(mechanism_count),
+                "mechanism_count_raw": mechanism_count,
+                "weights_version": query("WeightsVersionKey", [n]),
+                "weights_rate_limit": query("WeightsSetRateLimit", [n]),
+                "min_allowed_weights": query("MinAllowedWeights", [n]),
+                "max_weight_limit": query("MaxWeightsLimit", [n]),
+                "stake_threshold_raw": query("StakeThreshold", []),
+                "unavailable_fields": errors,
+            }
+        except ChainUnavailable:
+            raise
+        except Exception as exc:
+            self.substrate = None
+            raise ChainUnavailable("Finalized chain snapshot unavailable") from exc

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, fields
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+from urllib.parse import urlsplit
+
+FINNEY_GENESIS = "0x2f0555cc76fc2840a25a6ea3b9637146806f1f44b090c175ffde2a7e5ab36c03"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Settings:
+    chain_endpoint: str = "wss://entrypoint-finney.opentensor.ai:443"
+    expected_genesis: str = FINNEY_GENESIS
+    netuid: int | None = None
+    expected_owner_hotkey: str | None = None
+    expected_owner_coldkey: str | None = None
+    expected_owner_registration_block: int | None = None
+    validator_hotkey: str | None = None
+    expected_validator_registration_block: int | None = None
+    state_file: str = ".state/observer.json"
+    poll_seconds: int = 60
+    miner_burned_semantics: dict | None = None
+
+    def validate(self) -> None:
+        endpoint = urlsplit(self.chain_endpoint)
+        if endpoint.scheme != "wss" or not endpoint.hostname or endpoint.username or endpoint.password:
+            raise ValueError("A credential-free wss chain endpoint is required")
+        if self.expected_genesis != FINNEY_GENESIS:
+            raise ValueError("This pilot is pinned to the verified Finney genesis")
+        if type(self.netuid) is not int or not 1 <= self.netuid <= 65535:
+            raise ValueError("A non-root netuid must be explicitly configured")
+        if type(self.poll_seconds) is not int or self.poll_seconds < 15:
+            raise ValueError("poll_seconds must be an integer >= 15")
+        if not isinstance(self.state_file, str) or not self.state_file.strip():
+            raise ValueError("state_file must be a local filename")
+        for name in ("expected_owner_hotkey", "expected_owner_coldkey", "validator_hotkey"):
+            value = getattr(self, name)
+            if value is not None and (not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip()):
+                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a public hotkey address or null")
+        for name in ("expected_owner_registration_block", "expected_validator_registration_block"):
+            value = getattr(self, name)
+            if value is not None and (type(value) is not int or value < 0):
+                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-negative integer or null")
+        semantics = self.miner_burned_semantics
+        if semantics is not None:
+            if not isinstance(semantics, dict) or set(semantics) != {"spec_version", "fractional_bits", "source"}:
+                raise ValueError("miner_burned_semantics requires spec_version, fractional_bits and source")
+            if type(semantics["spec_version"]) is not int or semantics["fractional_bits"] != 32:
+                raise ValueError("Only explicitly reviewed U96F32 semantics are supported")
+            source = semantics["source"]
+            if not isinstance(source, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"https://github\.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/blob/[0-9a-f]{40}/pallets/subtensor/src/coinbase/run_coinbase\.rs", source):
+                raise ValueError("Pin semantics to a reviewed Subtensor commit URL, not a moving branch")
+
+
+def load_settings(path: str) -> Settings:
+    doc = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
+    if not isinstance(doc, dict):
+        raise ValueError("Config must be an object")
+    unknown = set(doc) - {field.name for field in fields(Settings)}
+    if unknown:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unknown config fields: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
+    result = Settings(**doc)
+    result.validate()
+    return result

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from decimal import Decimal
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from .config import Settings
+
+BURN_SOURCE = "https://github.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/blob/main/pallets/subtensor/src/coinbase/run_coinbase.rs"
+
+
+def normalized_miner_burned(raw, spec_version, semantics):
+    """Return a decimal only for an operator-reviewed runtime encoding.
+
+    FixedU128 is not enough to infer the denominator. Keep the raw value when
+    the deployed runtime has not been reviewed, rather than guessing a percent.
+    """
+    if not semantics or semantics["spec_version"] != spec_version:
+        return None
+    bits = raw.get("bits") if isinstance(raw, dict) and set(raw) == {"bits"} else raw
+    if type(bits) is not int or not 0 <= bits <= 1 << 32:
+        return None
+    return str(Decimal(bits) / Decimal(1 << 32))
+
+
+def registration_identity(registration):
+    if not registration or not registration.get("registered"):
+        return None
+    return [registration["hotkey"], registration["uid"], registration["registration_block"]]
+
+
+def assess(snapshot: dict, settings: Settings, previous: dict | None = None) -> dict:
+    reasons = []
+    if snapshot.get("genesis") != settings.expected_genesis or snapshot.get("netuid") != settings.netuid:
+        reasons.append("Snapshot does not match the configured chain/subnet pin")
+    owner = snapshot.get("owner") or {}
+    validator = snapshot.get("validator") or {}
+    if not settings.expected_owner_hotkey or owner.get("hotkey") != settings.expected_owner_hotkey:
+        reasons.append("Subnet owner hotkey is unpinned or changed")
+    if not owner.get("registered") or owner.get("registration_block") != settings.expected_owner_registration_block:
+        reasons.append("Owner registration is unpinned, unavailable or changed")
+    if snapshot.get("owner_coldkey_matches") is not True:
+        reasons.append("Owner hotkey/coldkey association is not verified")
+    if not settings.expected_owner_coldkey or snapshot.get("subnet_owner_coldkey") != settings.expected_owner_coldkey:
+        reasons.append("Subnet owner coldkey is unpinned or changed")
+    if not validator.get("registered"):
+        reasons.append("Validator public hotkey is unconfigured or unregistered")
+    if validator.get("registration_block") != settings.expected_validator_registration_block or settings.expected_validator_registration_block is None:
+        reasons.append("Validator registration is unpinned or changed")
+    if validator.get("validator_permit") is not True:
+        reasons.append("Validator permit is absent or unavailable")
+    if snapshot.get("recycle_or_burn_raw") not in ({"Burn": ()}, {"Burn": []}, "Burn"):
+        reasons.append("RecycleOrBurn is not verified as Burn")
+    if snapshot.get("commit_reveal_enabled") is not False:
+        reasons.append("Plain-weight burn writer compatibility not established: commit/reveal is enabled or unavailable")
+    if snapshot.get("mechanism_count") != 1:
+        reasons.append("Single-mechanism scope is unverified")
+    if previous:
+        if previous.get("genesis") != snapshot.get("genesis") or previous.get("netuid") != snapshot.get("netuid"):
+            reasons.append("Prior snapshot belongs to another chain or subnet")
+        if previous.get("source_block", -1) > snapshot["source_block"]:
+            reasons.append("Finalized source block regressed")
+        if previous.get("source_block") == snapshot["source_block"] and previous.get("source_hash") != snapshot.get("source_hash"):
+            reasons.append("Finalized block hash changed at the same height")
+        for role in ("owner", "validator"):
+            if registration_identity(previous.get(role)) != registration_identity(snapshot.get(role)):
+                reasons.append(f"{role.title()} registration changed since previous snapshot")
+    row = validator.get("weights_raw")
+    row_burn = None
+    if isinstance(row, (list, tuple)) and owner.get("registered"):
+        try:
+            entries = [(uid, weight) for uid, weight in row]
+            if any(type(uid) is not int or type(weight) is not int for uid, weight in entries):
+                raise ValueError("Weights must be raw integers")
+            if any(uid < 0 or not 0 <= weight <= 65535 for uid, weight in entries) or len({uid for uid, _ in entries}) != len(entries):
+                raise ValueError("Invalid weight row")
+            nonzero = [(uid, weight) for uid, weight in entries if weight > 0]
+            row_burn = bool(nonzero and len(nonzero) == 1 and nonzero[0] == (owner["uid"], 65535))
+        except (ValueError, TypeError):
+            row_burn = None
+    if row_burn is not True:
+        reasons.append("Finalized validator row is not verified as 100% to the current owner UID")
+    evidence = snapshot.get("last_epoch_evidence") or {}
+    same_runtime = evidence.get("runtime_spec_version") == evidence.get("mode_runtime_spec_version")
+    fraction = normalized_miner_burned(evidence.get("miner_burned_raw"), evidence.get("runtime_spec_version"), settings.miner_burned_semantics) if same_runtime else None
+    epoch = snapshot.get("last_epoch_block")
+    epoch_valid = type(epoch) is int and 0 < epoch <= snapshot["source_block"] and evidence.get("source_block") == epoch and bool(evidence.get("source_hash")) and evidence.get("mode_source_block") == epoch - 1 and bool(evidence.get("mode_source_hash"))
+    epoch_burn = evidence.get("recycle_or_burn_raw") in ({"Burn": ()}, {"Burn": []}, "Burn")
+    observed_full = None if fraction is None or not epoch_valid or not epoch_burn or reasons else fraction == "1"
+    return {
+        **snapshot,
+        "observer": {"chain_writes": False, "wallet_loaded": False, "scoring": "pending_authenticated_reports"},
+        "burn_guard": {"checks_passed": not reasons, "blocked_reasons": reasons, "validator_row_100_percent_to_owner": row_burn},
+        "miner_burned": {"fraction": fraction, "raw": snapshot.get("miner_burned_raw"), "settlement_evidence": evidence or None, "semantics": "Latest epoch miner incentive withheld from owner-associated hotkeys; includes burn and recycle", "encoding_review": settings.miner_burned_semantics, "source": BURN_SOURCE},
+        "last_epoch_100_percent_miner_burn_verified": observed_full,
+        "scope": "Miner incentive only. Validator dividends, owner cut and pool injections are separate. This observer maintains no burn process.",
+    }
+
+
+def load_state(path: str) -> dict | None:
+    try:
+        value = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
+        if not isinstance(value, dict):
+            raise ValueError("Observer state must be an object")
+        return value
+    except FileNotFoundError:
+        return None
+
+
+def save_state(path: str, snapshot: dict) -> None:
+    target = Path(path)
+    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    temporary = target.with_suffix(target.suffix + ".tmp")
+    with temporary.open("w") as stream:
+        os.chmod(temporary, 0o600)
+        json.dump(snapshot, stream, sort_keys=True)
+        stream.write("\n")
+    temporary.replace(target)

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from copy import deepcopy
+from dataclasses import replace
+import tempfile

+
+from danilabs_validator.chain import ChainUnavailable, FinalizedChain, unsigned_newtype
+from danilabs_validator.config import FINNEY_GENESIS, Settings

+    def query(self, module, name, params, *, block_hash):
+        self.reads.append((name, params, block_hash))
+        assert module == "SubtensorModule"
+        assert block_hash in ("hash-100", "hash-90", "hash-89")
+        if block_hash in ("hash-90", "hash-89") and not self.archive_available:
+            raise RuntimeError("No archive")
+        values = {

+            "MaxWeightsLimit": 65535, "StakeThreshold": 1000,
+            "TotalHotkeyAlpha": [10_000_000_000],
+        }
+        if name == "Uids":
+            return {"owner-hotkey": 1, "validator-hotkey": 2}.get(params[1])
+        if name == "Keys":
+            return {1: "owner-hotkey", 2: "replacement-hotkey" if self.recycled else "validator-hotkey"}[params[1]]
+        if name == "BlockAtRegistration":
+            return {1: 10, 2: 20}[params[1]]
+        if name == "Owner":
+            return "owner-coldkey" if params[0] == "owner-hotkey" else "validator-coldkey"
+        if name not in values:
+            raise AssertionError(f"Unexpected storage: {name}")
+        return deepcopy(values[name])
+
+
+class ObserverTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def snapshot(self):

+        return FinalizedChain(SETTINGS, substrate).snapshot(), substrate
+
+    def test_all_reads_use_explicit_finalized_or_settlement_hash(self):

+    def test_genesis_and_netuid_pins(self):

+    def test_recycled_uid_cannot_inherit_validator_row(self):

+
+    def test_owner_or_registration_change_blocks_guard(self):

+        self.assertFalse(assess(snapshot, SETTINGS)["burn_guard"]["checks_passed"])

+    def test_unavailable_or_unreviewed_burn_is_not_one_hundred_percent(self):
+        snapshot, _ = self.snapshot()

+            damaged = deepcopy(snapshot)
+            damaged["last_epoch_evidence"][field] = None
+            self.assertIsNone(assess(damaged, SETTINGS)["last_epoch_100_percent_miner_burn_verified"])
+        self.assertIsNone(assess(snapshot, replace(SETTINGS, miner_burned_semantics=None))["miner_burned"]["fraction"])
+        self.assertIsNone(normalized_miner_burned(1 << 32, 480, SEMANTICS))
+        self.assertIsNone(normalized_miner_burned(1.0, 481, SEMANTICS))

+    def test_archive_failure_and_recycle_at_settlement_are_not_burn(self):

+        fake.archive_available = False

+        self.assertIsNone(result["last_epoch_100_percent_miner_burn_verified"])

+        snapshot["last_epoch_evidence"]["recycle_or_burn_raw"] = {"Recycle": ()}
+        self.assertIsNone(assess(snapshot, SETTINGS)["last_epoch_100_percent_miner_burn_verified"])
+
+    def test_runtime_upgrade_at_settlement_requires_new_review(self):
+        snapshot, _ = self.snapshot()
+        snapshot["last_epoch_evidence"]["mode_runtime_spec_version"] = 480
+        result = assess(snapshot, SETTINGS)
+        self.assertIsNone(result["miner_burned"]["fraction"])
+        self.assertIsNone(result["last_epoch_100_percent_miner_burn_verified"])

+    def test_fresh_last_update_does_not_prove_burn_row(self):
+        snapshot, _ = self.snapshot()
+        snapshot["validator"]["last_update"] = 100
+        snapshot["validator"]["weights_raw"] = [(0, 65535)]
+        result = assess(snapshot, SETTINGS)
+        self.assertFalse(result["burn_guard"]["validator_row_100_percent_to_owner"])

+    def test_finalized_regression_and_missing_pins_block(self):
+        snapshot, _ = self.snapshot()
+        previous = deepcopy(snapshot)
+        previous["source_block"] = 101
+        self.assertFalse(assess(snapshot, SETTINGS, previous)["burn_guard"]["checks_passed"])
+        self.assertFalse(assess(snapshot, Settings())["burn_guard"]["checks_passed"])
+
+    def test_local_state_roundtrip_preserves_mapping(self):
+        snapshot, _ = self.snapshot()
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+            path = directory + "/state.json"
+            self.assertIsNone(load_state(path))
+            save_state(path, snapshot)
+            loaded = load_state(path)
+            self.assertEqual(registration_identity(loaded["owner"]), registration_identity(snapshot["owner"]))
+            self.assertEqual(loaded["source_hash"], snapshot["source_hash"])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

primaryCommitChecks.message:
Scale the miner pool by recent swap fees (#811)

* Scale the miner pool by recent swap fees

Each scoring round multiplies every lane pool by
miner_share = min(1, FEE_POOL_MULTIPLE x fees_24h / miner_emission_24h);
the undistributed remainder recycles to RECYCLE_UID as before.

fees_24h is the SwapCompleted fee over the trailing pool window, now stored
on clearing_rates (new fee column, old rows read 0). Lamport fees convert to
TAO at the median sol<->tao rate the validator cleared in the window, else
the last good rate. miner_emission_24h is the subnet's per-block alpha
emission x 0.41 x blocks in the window, valued at the subnet alpha price.
A failed input keeps the last persisted share; a new validator starts at 0.

* Convert lamport fees at a fixed-hour market rate; value emission at the moving price

Lamport swap fees convert to TAO at sol_usd / tao_usd from CoinGecko at one
fixed UTC hour (the last full hour at least 10 minutes old), so every
validator derives the same rate. The rate is fetched once per hour and kept
in relay_meta with its hour; a round makes up to 3 attempts within 10 s and
otherwise keeps the last rate (WARNING, or ERROR past 24 h). With no rate
yet, lamport fees are skipped and TAO fees still count.

A fee backing with no conversion is now skipped with a warning instead of
holding the whole round's share. The emission value uses the subnet's
moving alpha price.

* Trim the fee-scaled pool tests

Same coverage in 22 tests: related cases parametrized or merged, overlapping ones dropped. No behaviour change.

 # BURN_RATE of every round recycles to RECYCLE_UID before any shortfall.
 BURN_RATE = 0.0
 MINER_POOL_SHARE = 1.0 - BURN_RATE
+# Fee-scaled pool: every round, each lane pool is multiplied by
+# miner_share = min(1, FEE_POOL_MULTIPLE × fees / miner_emission) over POOL_VOLUME_WINDOW_SECS, so the
+# pools pay MINER_POOL_SHARE × miner_share and the rest recycles to RECYCLE_UID. fees = the 1% swap fee
+# (SwapCompleted.fee) in TAO; miner_emission = the miners' alpha emission over the same window in TAO.
+# A constant, not config: every validator must derive the same weights. Raise it to pay out more per fee.
+FEE_POOL_MULTIPLE = 2.0
+# Miners' cut of a subnet's alpha emission: the owner takes 18%, the other 82% splits evenly between

@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+"""The fee pool's SOL→TAO rate: CoinGecko USD prices for SOL and TAO at one fixed UTC hour.
+
+Every validator asks for the same hour (``rate_hour``), so every validator derives the same rate. One
+round tries ``SOL_TAO_FETCH_ATTEMPTS`` times inside ``SOL_TAO_FETCH_BUDGET_SECS`` and then gives up, so
+a slow or rate-limited feed never stalls scoring.
+"""
+
+import math
+import time
+from typing import Callable, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+import bittensor as bt
+import requests
+
+from allways.constants import (
+    SOL_TAO_FETCH_ATTEMPTS,
+    SOL_TAO_FETCH_BUDGET_SECS,
+    SOL_TAO_RATE_LAG_SECS,
+)
+from allways.miner.optimizer.market_price import COINGECKO_IDS
+
+COINGECKO_RANGE_URL = 'https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/{id}/market_chart/range'
+HOUR_SECS = 3600
+
+
+class RateLimited(Exception):
+    """A 429, carrying its Retry-After in seconds (None when absent or unparseable)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, retry_after: Optional[float]):
+        super().__init__(f'rate limited (retry-after={retry_after})')
+        self.retry_after = retry_after
+
+
+def rate_hour(now: int) -> int:
+    """The last full UTC hour at least ``SOL_TAO_RATE_LAG_SECS`` old, as unix seconds."""
+    return (int(now) - SOL_TAO_RATE_LAG_SECS) // HOUR_SECS * HOUR_SECS
+
+
+def valid_price(value: float) -> bool:
+    return math.isfinite(value) and value > 0
+
+
+def hour_price(points: List[Tuple[int, float]], hour: int) -> float:
+    """The price at ``hour`` from ``[(unix_secs, usd)]``: the point stamped exactly ``hour``, else the
+    latest point in ``[hour - 1h, hour]``. Raises if there is none or it is not a positive finite number."""
+    in_hour = [(ts, price) for ts, price in points if hour - HOUR_SECS <= ts <= hour]
+    exact = [price for ts, price in in_hour if ts == hour]
+    if exact:
+        price = exact[-1]
+    elif in_hour:
+        price = max(in_hour)[1]
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f'no price point in the hour ending {hour}')
+    if not valid_price(price):
+        raise ValueError(f'invalid price {price} for hour {hour}')
+    return price
+
+
+def _retry_after(header: Optional[str]) -> Optional[float]:
+    try:
+        return float(header) if header is not None else None
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def fetch_hour_usd(coin_id: str, hour: int, timeout: float) -> float:
+    """One CoinGecko range read for ``coin_id`` over the hour ending at ``hour``; USD at ``hour``."""
+    resp = requests.get(
+        COINGECKO_RANGE_URL.format(id=coin_id),
+        params={'vs_currency': 'usd', 'from': hour - HOUR_SECS, 'to': hour},
+        timeout=timeout,
+    )
+    if resp.status_code == 429:
+        raise RateLimited(_retry_after(resp.headers.get('Retry-After')))
+    resp.raise_for_status()
+    points = [(int(ts) // 1000, float(price)) for ts, price in resp.json()['prices']]
+    return hour_price(points, hour)
+
+
+def fetch_sol_tao_rate(
+    hour: int,
+    fetch: Callable[[str, int, float], float] = fetch_hour_usd,
+    sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep,
+    clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
+) -> Optional[float]:
+    """TAO per SOL at ``hour`` (``sol_usd / tao_usd``, both read for that same hour), or None once the
+    attempts or the time budget run out. Backs off 1s/2s/4s between attempts; a 429's Retry-After is
+    honoured when it fits the remaining budget, else the round gives up."""
+    deadline = clock() + SOL_TAO_FETCH_BUDGET_SECS
+    for attempt in range(SOL_TAO_FETCH_ATTEMPTS):
+        wait = float(2**attempt)
+        try:
+            sol_usd = fetch(COINGECKO_IDS['sol'], hour, max(0.1, deadline - clock()))
+            tao_usd = fetch(COINGECKO_IDS['tao'], hour, max(0.1, deadline - clock()))
+            rate = sol_usd / tao_usd
+            if valid_price(rate):
+                return rate
+            bt.logging.debug(f'sol/tao rate {rate} for hour {hour} rejected')
+        except RateLimited as e:
+            if e.retry_after is not None:
+                wait = e.retry_after
+            bt.logging.debug(f'sol/tao price fetch for hour {hour}: {e}')
+        except Exception as e:
+            bt.logging.debug(f'sol/tao price fetch for hour {hour} failed (attempt {attempt + 1}): {e}')
+        if attempt == SOL_TAO_FETCH_ATTEMPTS - 1 or clock() + wait > deadline:
+            break
+        sleep(wait)
+    return None

@@ -0,0 +1,478 @@
+"""Fee-scaled miner pool: each round scales every lane pool by
+``miner_share = min(1, FEE_POOL_MULTIPLE × fees / miner_emission)`` over the trailing pool window,
+and the remainder recycles to ``RECYCLE_UID``."""
+
+import sqlite3
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+
+from allways.constants import (
+    FEE_POOL_MULTIPLE,
+    MINER_EMISSION_FRACTION,
+    POOL_VOLUME_WINDOW_SECS,
+    RECYCLE_UID,
+    SECONDS_PER_BLOCK,
+)
+from allways.solana.events import EventRecord
+from allways.validator import scoring as scoring_mod
+from allways.validator.event_index import SolanaEventIndex
+from allways.validator.scoring import (
+    calculate_miner_rewards,
+    fee_pool_share,
+    hourly_sol_tao_rate,
+    round_miner_share,
+    score_and_reward_miners,
+    snapshot_current_miner_scores,
+    window_fees_tao,
+)
+from allways.validator.sol_tao_price import RateLimited, fetch_sol_tao_rate, hour_price, rate_hour
+from allways.validator.state_store import ValidatorStateStore
+from tests.test_scoring_v1 import (  # noqa: F401 — _identity_attribution is an autouse fixture
+    CROWN_SLICE,
+    POOL_BTC_SOL,
+    POOL_SOL_BTC,
+    _identity_attribution,
+    make_validator,
+    pad_hotkeys_to_cover_recycle,
+)
+
+TAO = 10**9
+SOL = 10**9
+ALPHA_PER_BLOCK = 1.0
+ALPHA_PRICE = 0.01  # TAO per alpha
+EMISSION_24H = ALPHA_PER_BLOCK * MINER_EMISSION_FRACTION * (POOL_VOLUME_WINDOW_SECS / SECONDS_PER_BLOCK) * ALPHA_PRICE
+
+
+HOUR = 3600
+NO_RATE = lambda: None  # noqa: E731
+
+
+def subnet_info(alpha_per_block: float = ALPHA_PER_BLOCK, price: float = ALPHA_PRICE) -> SimpleNamespace:
+    # The spot price is set far off the moving price: the emission value must read the moving one.
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        alpha_out_emission=SimpleNamespace(tao=alpha_per_block), moving_price=price, price=SimpleNamespace(tao=99.0)
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _no_price_feed(monkeypatch):
+    """No test reaches CoinGecko: a round's SOL rate comes from ``hourly_rates`` (default: unavailable)."""
+    calls = []
+
+    def fetch(hour):
+        calls.append(hour)
+        return _no_price_feed.rates.get(hour)
+
+    _no_price_feed.rates = {}
+    _no_price_feed.calls = calls
+    monkeypatch.setattr(scoring_mod, 'fetch_sol_tao_rate', fetch)
+    return _no_price_feed
+
+
+def with_subtensor(v: SimpleNamespace, subnet=None) -> SimpleNamespace:
+    """Give a scoring stand-in a subtensor whose ``subnet`` read returns ``subnet_info()`` (or ``subnet``)."""
+    reads = []
+
+    def read(netuid):
+        reads.append(netuid)
+        if callable(subnet):
+            return subnet()
+        return subnet or subnet_info()
+
+    v.subtensor = SimpleNamespace(subnet=read)
+    v.config = SimpleNamespace(netuid=7)
+    v.subnet_reads = reads
+    return v
+
+
+def add_fee(store: ValidatorStateStore, key: str, fee: int, backing: str, at: int, legs=('btc', 'tao', 1, 1)):
+    """One completed, unqualified fill carrying ``fee`` — inert for pools and the β slice."""
+    from_chain, to_chain, from_amount, to_amount = legs
+    store.insert_clearing_rate(at, 'hk_x', from_chain, to_chain, from_amount, to_amount, key, backing, fee=fee)

+def seed_btc_sol_crown(v: SimpleNamespace, hotkey: str = 'hk_a') -> None:
+    conn = v.state_store.require_connection()
+    for from_chain, to_chain in (('btc', 'sol'), ('sol', 'btc')):
+        conn.execute(
+            'INSERT INTO rate_events (hotkey, from_chain, to_chain, rate, block) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)',
+            (hotkey, from_chain, to_chain, 0.00020, 0),
+        )
+    conn.commit()
+
+
+def fees_for_share(share: float) -> int:
+    """The rao fee that yields ``share`` against ``EMISSION_24H``."""
+    return round(share * EMISSION_24H / FEE_POOL_MULTIPLE * TAO)

+        assert 'fee' in cols

+
+    def test_only_the_swap_completed_fee_counts(self, store: ValidatorStateStore):
+        """Reservation, quote-churn and pool-entry fees ride other events and never reach the fee sum;
+        the swap fee is stored as the event's absolute ``fee``, not re-derived from collateral."""
+        index = SolanaEventIndex(store)
+        attribution = {'pk_a': 'hk_a'}
+
+        def rec(name, slot, **fields):
+            return EventRecord(
+                name=name, fields={'miner': 'pk_a', **fields}, slot=slot, block_time=1_000 + slot, signature=f's{slot}'
+            )
+
+        index.ingest(
+            [
+                rec(
+                    'PoolOpened', 1, opener='pk_u', from_chain='btc', to_chain='tao', collateral_chain='tao', fee_paid=7
+                ),
+                rec('ReservationRequested', 2, router='pk_r', requests=1, fee_paid=11, collateral_chain='tao'),
+                rec('QuoteRemoved', 3, from_chain='btc', to_chain='tao', collateral_chain='tao', remove_fee=13),
+                rec(
+                    'SwapCompleted',
+                    4,
+                    swap_key=b'\x01' * 32,
+                    from_chain='btc',
+                    to_chain='tao',
+                    collateral_chain='tao',
+                    collateral_amount=500 * TAO,
+                    from_amount=1_000,
+                    to_amount=500 * TAO,
+                    fee=5 * TAO,

+        assert store.get_swap_fees(0, 2_000) == {'tao': 5 * TAO}
+        assert window_fees_tao(store, 0, 2_000, NO_RATE) == pytest.approx(5.0)

+    def test_mixed_sol_and_tao_fees_convert_at_the_given_rate(self, store: ValidatorStateStore):
+        add_fee(store, 'f-sol', SOL // 100, 'sol', at=20, legs=('sol', 'btc', 1, 1))  # 0.01 SOL
+        add_fee(store, 'f-tao', TAO // 200, 'tao', at=21)  # 0.005 TAO
+        assert window_fees_tao(store, 0, 100, lambda: 2.0) == pytest.approx(0.01 * 2.0 + 0.005)

+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        'backing, rate', [('sol', NO_RATE), ('eth', lambda: 2.0)], ids=['sol-no-rate-yet', 'unknown-backing']

+    def test_a_fee_with_no_conversion_is_skipped_and_tao_fees_still_count(self, store, backing, rate):

+class TestSolTaoRate:
+    def test_rate_hour_is_the_last_full_hour_at_least_ten_minutes_old(self):

+    H = 10 * HOUR

+    def test_rate_is_sol_usd_over_tao_usd_for_the_same_hour(self):

+        def fetch(coin_id, hour, timeout):

+        assert fetch_sol_tao_rate(5 * HOUR, fetch=fetch, sleep=lambda s: None) == pytest.approx(0.5)

+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _clock():
+        t = [0.0]
+        sleeps = []
+
+        def sleep(secs):

+        return t, sleeps, sleep, lambda: t[0]

+    def test_retries_back_off_and_stop_after_three_attempts(self):

+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(

+        """Slow reads stop at the budget; a Retry-After is honoured only when it fits it."""

@@ -0,0 +1,99 @@
+import asyncio
+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+import websockets
+
+
+async def wait_until(condition: Callable[[], bool], timeout: float = 2) -> None:
+    async with asyncio.timeout(timeout):
+        while not condition():
+            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
+
+
+class AbstractWSTestServer(ABC):
+    """A WebSocket server on localhost that `async with` starts and stops."""
+
+    host = "localhost"
+
+    def __init__(self, port: int) -> None:
+        self.port = port
+        self.ws_server: websockets.Server | None = None
+
+    async def start(self) -> None:
+        self.ws_server = await websockets.serve(
+            self._serve, self.host, self.port, process_request=self._process_request
+        )
+
+    async def stop(self) -> None:
+        self.ws_server.close()
+        await self.ws_server.wait_closed()
+
+    async def __aenter__(self):
+        await self.start()
+        return self
+
+    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
+        await self.stop()
+
+    @property
+    def url(self) -> str:
+        return f"ws://{self.host}:{self.port}"
+
+    @property
+    def connections(self) -> set[websockets.ServerConnection]:
+        return self.ws_server.connections
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    async def _serve(self, ws: websockets.ServerConnection) -> None: ...
+
+    async def _process_request(
+        self, connection: websockets.ServerConnection, request: websockets.Request
+    ) -> None:
+        """Called during every opening handshake, before the connection is accepted."""
+
+
+class ReconnectingWSTestServer(AbstractWSTestServer):
+    """
+    A WebSocket peer that closes the first connection after `drop_first_connection_after`
+    messages, so the client's next send() or receive() has to reconnect. Every later handshake
+    takes `handshake_delay` seconds, which keeps a reconnect in flight long enough for a
+    concurrent one to start. Received messages are queued as (connection number, message).
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, port: int, *, drop_first_connection_after: int = 0, handshake_delay: float = 0
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(port)
+        self.drop_first_connection_after = drop_first_connection_after
+        self.handshake_delay = handshake_delay
+        self.connection_count = 0
+        self.delayed_handshakes = 0
+        self.received: asyncio.Queue[tuple[int, str | bytes]] = asyncio.Queue()
+
+    @property
+    def connection(self) -> websockets.ServerConnection:
+        (connection,) = self.connections
+        return connection
+
+    async def _process_request(
+        self, connection: websockets.ServerConnection, request: websockets.Request
+    ) -> None:
+        if self.connection_count:
+            self.delayed_handshakes += 1
+            await asyncio.sleep(self.handshake_delay)
+            self.delayed_handshakes -= 1
+
+    async def _serve(self, ws: websockets.ServerConnection) -> None:
+        self.connection_count += 1
+        number = self.connection_count
+        limit = self.drop_first_connection_after if number == 1 else None
+        received = 0
+        while limit is None or received < limit:
+            try:
+                message = await ws.recv()
+            except websockets.ConnectionClosed:
+                return
+            await self.received.put((number, message))
+            received += 1
+        # Returning closes the connection.

files.name: compute_horde_sdk/changelog.d/+multi-upload-cancellation.fixed.md
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+When one file of a `MultiUpload` fails to upload, the uploads still in progress are cancelled before `OutputUploadFailed` is raised; uploads that already finished stay delivered.

files.name: compute_horde_sdk/changelog.d/+output-upload-confinement.fixed.md
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+Output uploads are confined to the output directory: `relative_path` of single-file uploads must be a canonical relative path with no component longer than 255 bytes, the uploader opens output files without following symlinks and rejects anything that is not a regular file or exceeds the size limit, zipped uploads leave out symlinks, other non-regular entries and empty directories, and the HTTP response of an upload receiver is cut off at the 10 MiB cap.

files.name: compute_horde_sdk/changelog.d/+output-volume-path-validation.changed.md
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+`HTTPOutputVolume` mount paths must be `/output/` followed by a canonical relative path; paths such as `/output//x`, `/output/../x` or `/output/x/` now raise `ValueError` when the job is created.

files.name: compute_horde_sdk/changelog.d/+put-upload-chunks.fixed.md
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+HTTP PUT output uploads send the file in chunks of at most 64 KiB instead of one chunk per line, so a file without newlines is no longer read into memory whole.

files.name: compute_horde_sdk/changelog.d/+untrusted-files.added.md
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+Added `compute_horde_core.untrusted_files` for reading files from, and writing files into, a directory populated by an untrusted process without following symlinks and with a size bound checked before reading.

files.name: compute_horde_sdk/changelog.d/+zipped-output-upload-errors.fixed.md
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+Zipped output uploads accept files modified after 2107 and fail with `OutputUploadFailed` instead of an unhandled exception when a file name is not valid UTF-8. An output directory with directories nested more than 100 levels deep also fails with `OutputUploadFailed`. `MultiUpload` builds its system output zip before it sends any file.

@@ -0,0 +1,279 @@
+"""
+Reading and writing files in a directory that an untrusted process has populated.
+
+A job container writes into host directories that are later read with the
+privileges of the process collecting the results. Every entry is treated as
+hostile: no path component is ever followed as a symlink, only regular files
+are opened, and the size reported by the kernel is checked before any content
+is read. A file is written there only as a new regular file that replaces
+whatever entry had its name. Relative paths chosen by an untrusted party are
+accepted only in a single canonical spelling, so a path can never name
+anything above the directory it is resolved against.
+"""
+
+import contextlib
+import dataclasses
+import errno
+import os
+import pathlib
+import stat
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+
+# O_NONBLOCK and O_NOCTTY: an entry swapped for a FIFO or a terminal between the
+# type check and the open neither blocks the open nor becomes the controlling terminal.
+_OPEN_FLAGS = {
+    stat.S_IFDIR: os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC,
+    stat.S_IFREG: os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC | os.O_NONBLOCK | os.O_NOCTTY,
+}
+# O_EXCL: an entry planted under the name after it was unlinked fails the open instead of being opened.
+_WRITE_FLAGS = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC | os.O_NONBLOCK
+_FILE_TYPE_NAMES = {
+    stat.S_IFREG: "regular file",
+    stat.S_IFDIR: "directory",
+    stat.S_IFLNK: "symlink",
+    stat.S_IFIFO: "FIFO",
+    stat.S_IFCHR: "character device",
+    stat.S_IFBLK: "block device",
+    stat.S_IFSOCK: "socket",
+}
+_READ_CHUNK_SIZE = 1 << 20
+_FORBIDDEN_COMPONENTS = frozenset({"", ".", ".."})
+_MAX_NAME_BYTES = 255
+# Every directory level being walked keeps a descriptor open and a generator frame alive.
+_MAX_WALK_DEPTH = 100
+
+
+class UntrustedFileRejected(Exception):
+    """A path under an untrusted directory was not opened or read; `reason` says why."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path: str, reason: str) -> None:
+        super().__init__(f"{path}: {reason}")
+        self.path = path
+        self.reason = reason
+
+
+class InvalidRelativePath(UntrustedFileRejected, ValueError):
+    """Also a ValueError, so pydantic validators can raise it as is."""
+
+
+class SymlinkRejected(UntrustedFileRejected):
+    pass
+
+
+class UnexpectedFileType(UntrustedFileRejected):
+    pass
+
+
+class FileTooLarge(UntrustedFileRejected):
+    pass
+
+
+class FileSizeChanged(UntrustedFileRejected):
+    pass
+
+
+class EntryNotReplaceable(UntrustedFileRejected):
+    pass
+
+
+class DirectoryTooDeep(UntrustedFileRejected):
+    pass
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
+class OpenedFile:
+    path: str
+    fd: int
+    stat: os.stat_result
+
+
+def split_relative_path(relative_path: str) -> list[str]:
+    """
+    Components of a relative path in its single accepted spelling, or `InvalidRelativePath`.
+
+    Meant for paths chosen by an untrusted party. Accepted: a path `open_regular_file`
+    accepts that contains no backslash and no component longer than 255 bytes in UTF-8.
+    Joining the components with '/' gives the input back, so a validated path needs no
+    normalization anywhere.
+    """
+    if "\\" in relative_path:
+        raise InvalidRelativePath(relative_path, "must not contain backslashes")
+    components = _split_confined(relative_path)
+    if any(len(component.encode()) > _MAX_NAME_BYTES for component in components):
+        raise InvalidRelativePath(relative_path, f"must not have components longer than {_MAX_NAME_BYTES} bytes")
+    return components
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def open_directory(path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> Iterator[int]:
+    """Open `path` as a directory descriptor; `path` itself must not be a symlink."""
+    with _open_component(None, path, os.fspath(path), stat.S_IFDIR) as (fd, _):
+        yield fd
+
+
+def list_entries(dir_fd: int) -> list[str]:
+    """Names of the current entries in the directory, whatever their type."""
+    # Rewind first: btrfs otherwise hides entries created after the descriptor was opened.
+    os.lseek(dir_fd, 0, os.SEEK_SET)
+    return os.listdir(dir_fd)
+
+
+def walk_regular_files(dir_fd: int) -> Iterator[str]:
+    """
+    Relative paths of the regular files below the directory `dir_fd`, in no particular order.
+
+    Subdirectories are entered through descriptors opened without following
+    symlinks. Symlinks and every other non-regular entry are skipped. Names are
+    kept as `os.listdir` returns them, so they may contain backslashes or
+    surrogate escapes; `open_regular_file` accepts every path yielded here.
+    A directory nested more than 100 levels deep raises `DirectoryTooDeep`.
+    """
+    yield from _walk(dir_fd, pathlib.PurePosixPath())

+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def open_regular_file(dir_fd: int, relative_path: str) -> Iterator[OpenedFile]:
+    """
+    Open `relative_path` beneath the directory `dir_fd` without following any symlink.
+
+    `relative_path` must be non-empty and '/'-separated, without a leading '/', NUL
+    bytes or empty, '.' or '..' components, or `InvalidRelativePath` is raised; any
+    other character, a backslash included, is part of a name. Each component is
+    opened relative to the previous one, so a symlink or an unexpected file type
+    anywhere in the path is rejected instead of followed.
+    """
+    *directories, name = _split_confined(relative_path)
+    with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
+        walked = pathlib.PurePosixPath()
+        for directory in directories:
+            walked /= directory
+            dir_fd, _ = stack.enter_context(_open_component(dir_fd, directory, str(walked), stat.S_IFDIR))
+        fd, st = stack.enter_context(_open_component(dir_fd, name, relative_path, stat.S_IFREG))
+        yield OpenedFile(path=relative_path, fd=fd, stat=st)
+
+
+def read_bounded(file: OpenedFile, max_size: int) -> bytes:
+    """
+    Read the whole content of an opened regular file of at most `max_size` bytes.
+
+    The size reported by fstat is checked before reading and never more than
+    `max_size + 1` bytes are read, so an oversized file costs no memory. Content
+    that does not match the reported size, because the file is still being
+    written to, is rejected.
+    """
+    expected_size = file.stat.st_size
+    if expected_size > max_size:
+        raise FileTooLarge(file.path, f"is {expected_size:,} bytes, more than the allowed {max_size:,} bytes")
+    content = _read_up_to(file.fd, expected_size + 1)
+    if len(content) != expected_size:
+        raise FileSizeChanged(file.path, f"read {len(content):,} bytes, expected {expected_size:,} bytes")
+    return content

+
+def read_regular_file(dir_fd: int, relative_path: str, max_size: int) -> bytes:
+    with open_regular_file(dir_fd, relative_path) as file:
+        return read_bounded(file, max_size)
+
+
+def _read_up_to(fd: int, limit: int) -> bytes:
+    chunks: list[bytes] = []
+    remaining = limit
+    while remaining > 0:
+        chunk = os.read(fd, min(remaining, _READ_CHUNK_SIZE))
+        if not chunk:
+            break
+        chunks.append(chunk)
+        remaining -= len(chunk)
+    return b"".join(chunks)
+
+
+def _split_confined(relative_path: str) -> list[str]:
+    if not relative_path:
+        raise InvalidRelativePath(relative_path, "must not be empty")
+    if "\0" in relative_path:
+        raise InvalidRelativePath(relative_path, "must not contain NUL bytes")
+    if relative_path.startswith("/"):
+        raise InvalidRelativePath(relative_path, "must be relative, not absolute")
+    components = relative_path.split("/")
+    if _FORBIDDEN_COMPONENTS.intersection(components):
+        raise InvalidRelativePath(relative_path, "must not contain empty, '.' or '..' components or end with '/'")
+    return components

+def _walk(dir_fd: int, prefix: pathlib.PurePosixPath) -> Iterator[str]:
+    for name in list_entries(dir_fd):
+        path = prefix / name

+        elif file_type == stat.S_IFDIR:

+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _open_component(
+    dir_fd: int | None, name: str | os.PathLike[str], path: str, expected_type: int
+) -> Iterator[tuple[int, os.stat_result]]:
+    # Check the type before opening: opening a device node can have side effects.
+    _check_type(os.stat(name, dir_fd=dir_fd, follow_symlinks=False), path, expected_type)
+    try:
+        fd = os.open(name, _OPEN_FLAGS[expected_type], dir_fd=dir_fd)
+    except OSError as e:
+        if e.errno == errno.ELOOP:
+            raise SymlinkRejected(path, "is a symlink") from e
+        raise
+    try:
+        # The open descriptor is what gets read, so its type is the one that counts.
+        st = os.fstat(fd)
+        _check_type(st, path, expected_type)
+        yield fd, st
+    finally:
+        os.close(fd)
+
+
+def _check_type(st: os.stat_result, path: str, expected_type: int) -> None:
+    actual_type = stat.S_IFMT(st.st_mode)
+    if actual_type == expected_type:
+        return
+    if actual_type == stat.S_IFLNK:
+        raise SymlinkRejected(path, "is a symlink")
+    actual_name = _FILE_TYPE_NAMES.get(actual_type, "file of unknown type")
+    raise UnexpectedFileType(path, f"is a {actual_name}, expected a {_FILE_TYPE_NAMES[expected_type]}")
+
+
+def write_regular_file(dir_fd: int, name: str, data: str | bytes) -> None:
+    """
+    Create `name` directly beneath the directory `dir_fd` as a new regular file holding `data`.
+
+    `name` must be a single file name; '', '.', '..' and names containing '/' or
+    a NUL byte raise `InvalidRelativePath`. Whatever the untrusted process left
+    under that name is unlinked first, so a symlink is never followed and a FIFO
+    is never opened. A directory cannot be unlinked and is rejected with
+    `EntryNotReplaceable`. `str` data is written as UTF-8.
+    """
+    _check_file_name(name)
+    try:
+        os.unlink(name, dir_fd=dir_fd)
+    except FileNotFoundError:
+        pass
+    except OSError as e:
+        raise EntryNotReplaceable(name, f"cannot be replaced: {e.strerror}") from e
+    fd = os.open(name, _WRITE_FLAGS, 0o644, dir_fd=dir_fd)
+    try:
+        _write_all(fd, data.encode() if isinstance(data, str) else data)
+    finally:
+        os.close(fd)
+
+
+def _check_file_name(name: str) -> None:
+    if name in ("", ".", "..") or "/" in name or "\0" in name:
+        raise InvalidRelativePath(name, "must be a single file name")
+
+
+def _write_all(fd: int, data: bytes) -> None:
+    view = memoryview(data)
+    while view:
+        view = view[os.write(fd, view) :]
