files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,187 @@ +# Submission terms + +**Terms version:** `v12`
+**Effective date:** 2026-10-21
+**Manual review policy:** `v4` + +These terms apply only to submissions accepted on or after the effective date. A submission +accepted earlier remains governed by the terms and review-policy version recorded at acceptance. + +Served as `body_md` by `GET /v1/catalog/submission-terms`, alongside the machine-readable +disqualification list from `submission_api/credits.py`. The prose here explains those +codes; the list is the authority on what they are. Shown to a miner before they spend a +credit, and to a reviewer when they decide, so that no rejection can cite a reason the +miner was never told. + +## What a credit buys + +One credit buys **one verification attempt**. That is the whole of it. + +Payment does not change Lean's verdict, does not reserve a conjecture, does not entitle +you to a review outcome, and does not guarantee a reward. An attempt that the kernel +rejects is an attempt that was made; the credit is spent. + +A credit is refunded only when the attempt was never made or could not be made for a +reason on our side — the verifier was misconfigured, the sandbox was unavailable, a pin +rotation invalidated the task mid-flight. A proof that fails is not one of those cases. + +## What verification checks + +Your proof is compiled in an isolated container against the pinned environment named in +`GET /v1/catalog/meta`, and checked by the Lean kernel and Comparator. It must: + +- prove the exact statement in the task's `Challenge.lean`, as published, with its + published digest; +- depend on no admitted result — no `sorry`, no `sorryAx`, and no lemma that + transitively relies on one; +- import nothing the task's `forbidden_dependencies` excludes, including the source + declaration itself; +- close over no axiom outside the task's `permitted_axioms`; +- fit inside the task's declared byte and time limits. + +Every one of these is in the machine contract on the conjecture's detail page. Nothing is +checked that is not published there. + +## Reward review + +A Lean-valid proof is **held for review** before any reward is paid, and review can +refuse it. The reasons it can refuse are exactly the `disqualification_reasons` list on +this endpoint — a reviewer cannot invent one — and a refusal returns the code and any +miner-visible notes. + +Verification, review, and reward are three independent states. A proof can be verified and +not approved; approved and not yet paid. Reading one says nothing about the others. + +One reward is paid per exact theorem target. Its proof and refutation tasks compete for that one +reward, including across source repins. Independently formalized parents, parts, and variants are +separate targets and can each earn a reward. + +A reward is disqualified as `NOT_NOVEL` if the result was already available in the exact +pinned environment, or a complete, established public proof of the same direct mathematical +problem predates our acceptance of the submission. This includes conventional mathematical +proofs and computer-assisted proofs, even if they were never formalized in Lean. An independent +rediscovery, a different argument, or a first Lean formalization does not restore eligibility. + +We must identify the actual prior proof, establish reliable public chronology, match the exact +scope and hypotheses, and explain why the proof is complete and established. An unsupported +claim, inaccessible announcement, intention to prove, or proof of only a different/special case +is insufficient. Material uncertainty about validity, chronology, or target match must be +resolved before rejecting on that basis. `NOT_NOVEL` concerns bounty eligibility and does not +accuse the submitter of plagiarism or declare their Lean proof invalid. + +A reward may also be refused when public, dated evidence shows that the same target had already +been completed in an external formal proof system before we accepted the submission. This is +recorded as `PRIOR_EXTERNAL_FORMALIZATION`; it is not an accusation that the miner copied anyone's +work. A claim or announcement that a paper was formalized does not by itself meet this standard +when no inspectable artifact, theorem statement, certificate, or other target-specific record is +available. A mathematical paper may instead be evaluated under `NOT_NOVEL` using the requirements +above. + +Bounty amounts shown in the catalog are dynamic estimates. For submissions accepted after the V012 +policy activation, a fresh quote is locked and will not be repriced during verification or review. +The lock is conditional: it does not reserve the reward target, and another proof may become the +successful claim first. Rejected attempts release their treasury exposure. If your submission +is approved for the full conjecture bounty, its payout event copies the locked amount and pricing +inputs exactly. + +For a `FORMALIZATION_DEFECT_AWARD` under review policy `v3` or `v4`, the reward is **$750 USD equivalent +or the task bounty locked for your submission, whichever is less**, paid in Subnet 66 Alpha. +Convert $750 to integer Alpha rao at the authoritative Alpha/USD rate when the payout record is +created, using the existing nearest-rao rounding convention, then take the smaller of that amount +and your locked bounty. This replaces the full conjecture bounty; it is not an additional reward. +Submissions accepted under earlier review policies retain their recorded award terms, including +the fixed $750 defect award under policies `v1` and `v2`. + +Submissions accepted before that activation retain the payout-time pricing policy in force when +they were submitted; the new lock is not applied retroactively. + +## Chat logs + +**Every open problem requires the AI chat logs that produced the proof.** Upload them **before +submitting the proof**: from a signed-in account on the website, or with `conjectures logs +upload` from a CLI session whose coldkey is linked to your account. A coldkey-signed +submission uses the logs deposited by the account that coldkey is linked to; a coldkey linked +to no account cannot submit. A proof is not accepted without its logs, and no credit or +payment is spent. A reviewer accepts them only if they are the original chat logs that +produced the proof, not a recreation of them. If the logs are incomplete, the reviewer may ask +for more instead of rejecting them: you can then upload a new version, up to three versions in +all, each still the original chats and showing the proof before it was submitted. If none +arrives within 14 days of the request, or the logs are still not enough, they may be rejected. +Rejected or withdrawn logs mean the proof is rejected as `CHAT_LOGS_NOT_ACCEPTED`: no bounty +is paid and the target reopens to other solvers. The separately capped formalization-defect +award retains its existing rules. The [chat-log terms](../trajectories/chat-log-terms-v5.md) +apply. + +Requiring logs does not change what a problem pays. Targets first admitted under +`linear-age-v3-chat-logs`, including the P34 and P35 unit-square circle-packing targets, start +at **2.5% of the available Alpha treasury** and grow to 12.5% over 15 days, rounded down to +integer rao and locked at submission. Older targets retain the starting share they opened +with. A submission accepted before these terms took effect keeps the rules recorded at +acceptance and needs no logs. + +For full-bounty proofs submitted before chat-log intake opened, accepted logs earn an +additional **$500 USD for Erdős problems**, or **$250 USD for all other problems**, based +on the original task bundle and paid in Subnet 66 Alpha worth that amount when paid. The chat +must show the proof before it was submitted. Claims close one year after intake opened. +Existing proof payouts are not reduced or made conditional on logs. There is no extra log +bonus for a proof that required logs. + +Uploading logs grants Conjectures a permanent, worldwide, non-exclusive right to use, copy, +sell and license them to buyers, including for training and evaluating AI systems, once they +are accepted. Logs are not published openly, by us or by buyers. Logs that are not accepted +are deleted within 90 days; accepted logs are kept so they can be sold. + +## Attribution and publication + +**Your identity is published with your result.** Every result on the public feeds — certified or +awaiting review — names its solver: your account display name if you have set one, and otherwise +the coldkey that signed the submission. Submitting is a public act: assume that anyone can see +which identity attempted which conjecture, and when. + +Note that setting a display name publishes it. If you would rather be identified only by an +address, leave it unset. + +**Public name credit is optional and permanent for that submission.** You may attach a public +credit name and, optionally, an HTTPS profile URL and ORCID. These values are included in the +request digest your coldkey signs, stored as a snapshot on the submission, and published beside +your solver identity once the result reaches a public feed. They are not taken from your mutable +account display name. Omit public credit and you are credited by display name or coldkey as +above. Do not name another person or +team without their permission. + +**An approved proof is published in full.** Once review approves your submission, the exact +`Main.lean` you sent is served at `GET /v1/results/{id}/solution`, together with its digest. A +proof that is still in review, was refused, or failed the kernel is not published. + +Per-conjecture activity is still served as salted pseudonyms, but they are weak now and you should +not rely on them: because a verified result names your solver identity and carries its verification time, +the pseudonyms on a conjecture you have a verified result for can be matched back to you by +timing — and with that, your unsuccessful attempts on that conjecture too. + +What is still never published: your paying coldkey, your payment reference, the funding extrinsic, +and the verifier's stdout or stderr. + +## Your keys and your money + +- Amounts are integer rao throughout. 1 TAO is 1,000,000,000 rao. +- Deposits are credited at the amount **observed on chain**, not the amount you declared. + A short transfer is credited short. +- Credits are non-transferable and are not refundable to TAO. +- The validator never asks for and never holds a secret key. Every signature you provide + is over a message this service minted, and you can read it before signing. +- A payout needs one coldkey. It does not have to be a key you have proved to us, or even one + you control — it is only a destination — so check it carefully. Set it + together on your account before a reward can be paid. + +## Conduct + +Do not attempt to overload, probe, or game the validator. Concretely: do not submit proofs +you have no reason to believe are valid in order to map the checker's behaviour, do not +attempt to escape the verification sandbox, and do not submit work that is not yours to +claim. Any of these is grounds for refusing a reward and for closing an account. + +## Changes + +These terms are versioned. The version and effective date are on this endpoint, and the +version in force when a submission was accepted is the version that governs it — a later +change does not apply retroactively to a submission already made.

This replaces the full conjecture bounty; it is not an additional reward. +Submissions accepted under earlier review policies retain their recorded award terms, including +the fixed $750 defect award under policies `v1` and `v2`. + +Submissions accepted before that activation retain the payout-time pricing policy in force when +they were submitted; the new lock is not applied retroactively. + +## Chat logs + +**Every open problem requires the AI chat logs that produced the proof.** Upload them **before +submitting the proof**: from a signed-in account on the website, or with `conjectures logs +upload` from a CLI session whose coldkey is linked to your account. A coldkey-signed +submission uses the logs deposited by the account that coldkey is linked to; a coldkey linked +to no account cannot submit. A proof is not accepted without its logs, and no credit or +payment is spent. A reviewer accepts them only if they are the original chat logs that +produced the proof, not a recreation of them. If the logs are incomplete, the reviewer may ask +for more instead of rejecting them: you can then upload a new version, up to three versions in +all, each still the original chats and showing the proof before it was submitted. If none +arrives within 14 days of the request, or the logs are still not enough, they may be rejected. +Rejected or withdrawn logs mean the proof is rejected as `CHAT_LOGS_NOT_ACCEPTED`: no bounty +is paid and the target reopens to other solvers. The separately capped formalization-defect +award retains its existing rules. The [chat-log terms](../trajectories/chat-log-terms-v5.md) +apply. + +Requiring logs does not change what a problem pays. Targets first admitted under +`linear-age-v3-chat-logs`, including the P34 and P35 unit-square circle-packing targets, start +at **2.5% of the available Alpha treasury** and grow to 12.5% over 15 days, rounded down to +integer rao and locked at submission. Older targets retain the starting share they opened +with. A submission accepted before these terms took effect keeps the rules recorded at +acceptance and needs no logs. + +For full-bounty proofs submitted before chat-log intake opened, accepted logs earn an +additional **$500 USD for Erdős problems**, or **$250 USD for all other problems**, based +on the original task bundle and paid in Subnet 66 Alpha worth that amount when paid. The chat +must show the proof before it was submitted. Claims close one year after intake opened. +Existing proof payouts are not reduced or made conditional on logs. There is no extra log +bonus for a proof that required logs. + +Uploading logs grants Conjectures a permanent, worldwide, non-exclusive right to use, copy, +sell and license them to buyers, including for training and evaluating AI systems, once they +are accepted. Logs are not published openly, by us or by buyers. Logs that are not accepted +are deleted within 90 days; accepted logs are kept so they can be sold. + +## Attribution and publication + +**Your identity is published with your result.** Every result on the public feeds — certified or +awaiting review — names its solver: your account display name if you have set one, and otherwise +the coldkey that signed the submission. Submitting is a public act: assume that anyone can see +which identity attempted which conjecture, and when. + +Note that setting a display name publishes it. If you would rather be identified only by an +address, leave it unset. + +**Public name credit is optional and permanent for that submission.** You may attach a public +credit name and, optionally, an HTTPS profile URL and ORCID. These values are included in the +request digest your coldkey signs, stored as a snapshot on the submission, and published beside +your solver identity once the result reaches a public feed. They are not taken from your mutable +account display name. Omit public credit and you are credited by display name or coldkey as +above. Do not name another person or +team without their permission. + +**An approved proof is published in full.** Once review approves your submission, the exact +`Main.lean` you sent is served at `GET /v1/results/{id}/solution`, together with its digest. A +proof that is still in review, was refused, or failed the kernel is not published. + +Per-conjecture activity is still served as salted pseudonyms, but they are weak now and you should +not rely on them: because a verified result names your solver identity and carries its verification time, +the pseudonyms on a conjecture you have a verified result for can be matched back to you by +timing — and with that, your unsuccessful attempts on that conjecture too. + +What is still never published: your paying coldkey, your payment reference, the funding extrinsic, +and the verifier's stdout or stderr. + +## Your keys and your money + +- Amounts are integer rao throughout. 1 TAO is 1,000,000,000 rao. +- Deposits are credited at the amount **observed on chain**, not the amount you declared. + A short transfer is credited short. +- Credits are non-transferable and are not refundable to TAO. +- The validator never asks for and never holds a secret key. Every signature you provide + is over a message this service minted, and you can read it before signing. +- A payout needs one coldkey. It does not have to be a key you have proved to us, or even one + you control — it is only a destination — so check it carefully. Set it + together on your account before a reward can be paid. + +## Conduct + +Do not attempt to overload, probe, or game the validator. Concretely: do not submit proofs +you have no reason to believe are valid in order to map the checker's behaviour, do not +attempt to escape the verification sandbox, and do not submit work that is not yours to +claim. Any of these is grounds for refusing a reward and for closing an account. + +## Changes + +These terms are versioned. The version and effective date are on this endpoint, and the +version in force when a submission was accepted is the version that governs it — a later +change does not apply retroactively to a submission already made.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
+# Chat-log terms — v5
+
+Plain-language terms for sending the AI chat logs behind a proof. They apply from the moment
+chat-log intake opens; that moment is shown on the chat-log page. If we ever have to correct
+that moment, the page shows the corrected one, and logs already uploaded keep the moment that
+applied when they were uploaded. Logs uploaded under an earlier version of these terms keep
+that version.
+
+**What you send.** The real chat or chats, exported from the AI tool you used, in which you
+found the proof: messages, tool calls and results, files, and the model's reasoning wherever
+your tool saved it as readable text. Leave out reasoning your tool kept encrypted or withheld,
+and do not try to decrypt or recreate it.
+
+**When you send it.** Every open problem requires logs. Upload them before you submit the
+proof, from your account on the website or with `conjectures logs upload`. A proof is not
+accepted without them. If a reviewer finds the logs incomplete, they may ask for more instead
+of rejecting them: you can then upload a new version, up to three versions in all. Each
+version must still be the original chats and show the proof before it was submitted. If no
+new version arrives within 14 days of the request, or the logs are still not enough, they
+may be rejected. For a proof submitted before intake opened, you can upload its logs
+within one year of that moment.
+
+**What we check.** That these are the original chat logs that produced the proof, not a
+recreation of them.
+
+**What it pays.** The problem's bounty, locked when you submit and paid only if the logs are
+accepted. Problems added from October 13, 2026 start at 2.5% of the available Alpha treasury
+and grow to 12.5% over 15 days; earlier problems keep the schedule they opened with. If the
+logs are rejected or you withdraw them, the bounty is not paid and the problem reopens to
+other solvers. For a proof submitted before intake opened and approved for its full bounty,
+accepted logs earn an extra $500 for an Erdős problem or $250 for any other problem,
+paid in Subnet 66 Alpha worth that amount when it is paid. Your original reward does not
+change.
+
+**What you give us.** By uploading, you give Conjectures a permanent, worldwide,
+non-exclusive right to use, copy, sell and license the logs to buyers, including for
+training and evaluating AI systems. This takes effect once the logs are accepted. We do not
+publish the logs openly, and buyers may not either. You keep your own rights to them. If we
+later withdraw acceptance because the proof is disqualified, this right ends and the logs
+are deleted within 90 days.
+
+**Your promises.** The logs are real, the proof is yours, and you are allowed to share the
+logs, including under your AI provider's terms. Anything from other people is included with
+their permission.
+
+**Withdrawing and deletion.** You can withdraw logs before they are accepted; for a proof that
+required them, that gives up the bounty. Logs that are rejected, withdrawn or never accepted
+are deleted within 90 days, and logs uploaded for a proof that is never submitted within 24
+hours. Accepted logs are kept so they can be sold. A short record of each upload (who, when,
+which proof, file fingerprints and the decision) is kept for seven years, or longer while it
+backs a payout or accepted logs, for our accounting and to stop the same logs being claimed
+twice.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,127 @@
+# AL2023 host certificate distrust
+
+This is one reviewed, public OpenSSL `TRUSTED CERTIFICATE` source for
+`/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem`. It is explicit
+host provisioning, separate from service deployment. Do not put it in
+`anchors/` or `blocklist/`, install AAA, or edit generated bundles.
+
+- G3 certificate DER SHA256: `86a1ecba089c4a8d3bbe2734c612ba341d813e043cf9e8a862cd5c57a36bbe6b`.
+- Source file SHA256: `661798181d9251cd062f8ece4712bfce980138ac3ac085b4a3c77b12065b892b`.
+- AUX has no trusted uses. It rejects `anyExtendedKeyUsage`, `serverAuth`,
+  `clientAuth`, `emailProtection`, `codeSigning`, `timeStamping`, `OCSPSigning`.
+
+The unchanged X.509 certificate comes from the [official certifi 2024.08.30 bundle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/certifi/python-certifi/2024.08.30/certifi/cacert.pem)
+(bundle SHA256 `94edeb66e91774fcae93a05650914e29096259a5c7e871a1f65d461ab5201b47`).
+That old bundle is an identity source only. The [p11-kit 0.24.1 manual](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p11-glue/p11-kit/0.24.1/doc/manual/p11-kit-trust.xml)
+documents TRUSTED CERTIFICATE policy input; installed `update-ca-trust(8)`
+documents the neutral source directory. The source can be reproduced from the
+public G3 PEM with OpenSSL `x509 -clrtrust -clrreject`, seven `-addreject` options
+using the OIDs above in that order, and `-trustout`. No private key is involved.
+
+## Measured policy and limits
+
+The October 22 private-namespace test passed with installed p11-kit 0.24.1 and
+OpenSSL 3.2.2, including its `codesign` purpose. The exact test script SHA256 was
+`da8454f896392530438193d8b81b3802400e4f8bc938ea1a85a53d45295950f1`.
+It measured all ten purposes plus default before/after, with no new acceptance.
+G3 was explicitly rejected (error 28) for `sslserver`, `sslclient`,
+`nssslserver`, `smimesign`, `smimeencrypt`, `timestampsign`, `codesign`, `any`,
+and default. Its `crlsign` and `ocsphelper` compatibility acceptance stayed
+unchanged. This is not an all-purpose or all-consumer fix.
+
+AAA DER SHA256 is `d7a7a0fb5d7e2731d771e9484ebcdef71d5f0c3e0a2948782bc83ee0ea699ef4`.
+It was already excluded from TLS and rejected for client/server TLS and
+`any`/default. Its full purpose vector and AUX bytes remain unchanged; its
+existing email/code-signing and compatibility acceptance is not remediated here.
+Plain-PEM blocklisting widened generic trust for both roots, so that proposal
+was rejected. No AAA file is installed by this procedure.
+
+The passing test changed TLS anchors 143 to 142, removed only G3 from TLS,
+email and code-signing bundles, and preserved every other anchor/AUX value.
+Fresh OS-default TLS and same-endpoint wrong-hostname controls passed for
+`openrouter.ai`, `api.scrapingdog.com`, `pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`.
+Logical rollback passed; the outside whole-store manifest stayed
+`4d1b064e8292a4d83d3cef4a3dec7bd521f9d3116363c8900e9475840642c29b`.
+The manifest covers all three trust input/output trees, aliases, default CA
+paths and extraction-script hash, including file contents, links, mode/owner.
+
+## Apply on each host after review
+
+Do not overlap an active release or another trust writer. Use the exact
+reviewed commit. First record OS/tool versions and the complete trust manifest,
+all TLS/email/code-signing DER sets and OpenSSL certificate/AUX values, and both
+root verification vectors. Keep that evidence outside the trust trees. Run the
+reviewed private-namespace test against this host's current inputs first; stop
+if it differs from the reviewed policy or cannot prove isolation, retained
+anchors, TLS controls and rollback. The count/hash above is gateway evidence,
+not an assumed baseline for the validator or a later vendor update.
+
+Confirm `/etc/pki/ca-trust/source` is the real root-owned directory. The one
+destination must be absent, including dangling symlinks. Verify the installed
+`/usr/bin/update-ca-trust` SHA256 is
+`d321db9aa915ea4fc54d796badc869c3654ef0ce35dc8e35a4e8f59f0f62fa25`.
+Stop for review if it differs. This pinned vendor script ignores arguments and
+writes only its fixed extracted outputs. Verify the source checksum:
+
+```bash
+sha256sum --check deploy/ca-trust/SHA256SUMS
+sha256sum /usr/bin/update-ca-trust
+```
+
+Before installation, create a new root-owned mode-0700 backup directory and
+record its exact path. Copy the complete three trees, then verify the backup
+against the before manifest:
+
+```bash
+CA_BACKUP=$(sudo -n mktemp -d /var/tmp/leadpoet-ca-backup.XXXXXXXX)
+sudo -n cp -a --parents /etc/pki/ca-trust /usr/share/pki/ca-trust-source /usr/share/pki/ca-trust-legacy "$CA_BACKUP"
+```
+
+The backup is evidence and recovery input; do not overwrite live vendor trees
+from it during ordinary rollback.
+
+Run the following as sequential checked operations. Stop on any failure.
+The shell's noclobber mode refuses an existing destination; do not replace it.
+
+```bash
+sudo -n /bin/sh -eu -c 'set -C; umask 022; cat "$1" > "$2"; chown 0:0 "$2"; chmod 0644 "$2"' -- deploy/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem
+sudo -n cmp deploy/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem
+sudo -n /usr/bin/update-ca-trust
+```
+
+No package or service action is part of this procedure. After extraction,
+require the measured source SHA256, root ownership and mode 0644. Require
+TLS/email/code-signing DER sets equal baseline minus G3 and all unrelated AUX
+bytes unchanged, including AAA. Fresh Python OS-default roots must equal the
+candidate TLS set. Repeat both full verification vectors and reject any new
+acceptance; require G3 error 28 for the nine modes listed above. Use explicit
+`-CAfile /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/openssl/ca-bundle.trust.crt`,
+`-no-CApath -no-CAstore`, and each `-purpose` (omit it for default). These are
+root self-verification controls, not forged-chain tests. Repeat the four fresh
+OS-default TLS/hostname controls before declaring the host ready.
+
+## Activation, rollback and retirement
+
+Fresh OS-default contexts read the regenerated store. Existing contexts/pools
+can retain old roots until recreated. Apply before the next planned validator
+startup when possible. Any required process refresh uses its existing
+canonical activation path; this procedure does not restart services. The
+cached gateway Arena proxy and provider HTTPX transport use patched certifi
+(`trust_env=False`), separate from OS trust. aiohttp can cache an OS context at
+import. Container/enclave stores and custom CA overrides are separate.
+
+For rollback, confirm the one destination is still a regular, root-owned file
+with the exact reviewed source SHA256 and mode. Stop on any mismatch. Remove
+only `/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem`, then run the
+pinned `/usr/bin/update-ca-trust`. Require the original DER sets, all AUX values,
+both full verification vectors and fresh OS contexts to match baseline.
+Do not restore old generated bundles or remove unrelated source entries.
+Rollback restores baseline G3 trust, so keep the security consequence explicit.
+Existing contexts may still need separate activation after rollback.
+
+Retire this local override only after an approved vendor bundle, tested without
+this exact local source in an isolated copy, rejects G3 for the same nine modes,
+preserves AAA/unrelated policy, introduces no acceptance in any measured mode,
+and passes fresh-context and four-host TLS controls. Then remove only the
+matching local file, regenerate and verify. Keep it across vendor updates until
+those exit criteria pass. Do not delete the recorded backup as part of apply.

files.name: tests/test_host_ca_distrust.py
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+"""Pin the public G3 identity and its explicit OpenSSL AUX rejection policy."""
+
+import base64
+import hashlib
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+SOURCE = ROOT / "deploy/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem"
+SOURCE_SHA256 = "661798181d9251cd062f8ece4712bfce980138ac3ac085b4a3c77b12065b892b"
+DER_SHA256 = "86a1ecba089c4a8d3bbe2734c612ba341d813e043cf9e8a862cd5c57a36bbe6b"
+# DER-encoded OID values. AUX rejects are independent of X.509 extensions.
+REJECTED_OIDS = {
+    "anyExtendedKeyUsage": "551d2500",       # 2.5.29.37.0
+    "serverAuth": "2b06010505070301",       # 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1
+    "clientAuth": "2b06010505070302",
+    "emailProtection": "2b06010505070304",
+    "codeSigning": "2b06010505070303",
+    "timeStamping": "2b06010505070308",
+    "OCSPSigning": "2b06010505070309",
+}
+
+
+def der_item(value):
+    """Read one definite-length DER item; return its content and remainder."""
+    assert len(value) >= 2
+    tag, size = value[:2]
+    offset = 2
+    if size & 0x80:
+        count = size & 0x7f
+        assert 0 < count <= 4 and len(value) >= offset + count
+        size = int.from_bytes(value[offset:offset + count], "big")
+        offset += count
+    end = offset + size
+    assert end <= len(value)
+    return tag, value[offset:end], value[end:]
+
+
+def trusted_payload():
+    match = re.fullmatch(
+        rb"-----BEGIN TRUSTED CERTIFICATE-----\n([A-Za-z0-9+/=\n]+)\n-----END TRUSTED CERTIFICATE-----\n",
+        SOURCE.read_bytes(),
+    )
+    assert match
+    return base64.b64decode(match[1].replace(b"\n", b""), validate=True)
+
+
+def test_exact_public_source_and_unchanged_x509_identity():
+    assert {p.name for p in SOURCE.parent.iterdir()} == {SOURCE.name}
+    assert not (ROOT / "deploy/ca-trust/blocklist").exists()
+    assert SOURCE.is_file() and not SOURCE.is_symlink()
+    assert hashlib.sha256(SOURCE.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == SOURCE_SHA256
+    payload = trusted_payload()
+    tag, _, aux = der_item(payload)
+    assert tag == 0x30 and aux
+    certificate = payload[:len(payload) - len(aux)]
+    assert hashlib.sha256(certificate).hexdigest() == DER_SHA256
+
+
+def test_aux_has_only_explicit_rejections_and_no_trusted_uses():
+    _, _, aux = der_item(trusted_payload())
+    tag, content, remainder = der_item(aux)
+    assert tag == 0x30 and not remainder
+    # X509_CERT_AUX has an optional trust SEQUENCE followed by reject [0].
+    # Requiring only [0] excludes every trusted use and any unreviewed AUX field.
+    tag, rejects, remainder = der_item(content)
+    assert tag == 0xA0 and not remainder
+    actual = []
+    while rejects:
+        tag, oid, rejects = der_item(rejects)
+        assert tag == 0x06
+        actual.append(oid.hex())
+    assert actual == list(REJECTED_OIDS.values())
+
+
+def test_operator_checksum_manifest_covers_the_only_installed_source():
+    relative = SOURCE.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
+    assert (ROOT / "deploy/ca-trust/SHA256SUMS").read_text() == f"{SOURCE_SHA256}  {relative}\n"

+sudo -n cp -a --parents /etc/pki/ca-trust /usr/share/pki/ca-trust-source /usr/share/pki/ca-trust-legacy "$CA_BACKUP"
+```
+
+The backup is evidence and recovery input; do not overwrite live vendor trees
+from it during ordinary rollback.
+
+Run the following as sequential checked operations. Stop on any failure.
+The shell's noclobber mode refuses an existing destination; do not replace it.
+
+```bash
+sudo -n /bin/sh -eu -c 'set -C; umask 022; cat "$1" > "$2"; chown 0:0 "$2"; chmod 0644 "$2"' -- deploy/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem
+sudo -n cmp deploy/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem
 sudo -n /usr/bin/update-ca-trust
 ```
 
-Run these as sequential checked operations. Stop immediately if any operation
-fails; do not continue to regeneration after a failed copy or comparison.
-The copies made by `sudo` are root-owned. No package, service, or generated
-trust-output file is edited directly. The vendor command ignores destination
-arguments and regenerates its fixed extracted outputs.
-
-## Verify and activate
-
-Verify that TLS, email and code-signing anchor sets equal their before-state
-minus these two DER fingerprints, and that every unrelated OpenSSL trust
-attribute is unchanged. Do not assume both hosts have the same initial count.
-The October 22 gateway private-namespace test measured TLS 143 -> 142; AAA was
-already absent from TLS. It preserved all other anchors and trust attributes,
-passed real OS-default TLS and wrong-hostname controls for `openrouter.ai`,
-`api.scrapingdog.com`, `pypi.org` and `files.pythonhosted.org`, and restored the
-initial logical trust on rollback without changing the live store.
-
-Use the generated `extracted/openssl/ca-bundle.trust.crt` with explicit CAfile,
-`-no-CApath -no-CAstore`, and `openssl verify -purpose` for `sslserver`,
-`sslclient`, `smimesign` and `smimeencrypt`. Each root must fail with error 28,
-`certificate rejected`. These are root self-verification controls, not forged
-certificate chains. Also inspect freshly created Python OS-default contexts
-and repeat the four-host TLS/hostname controls before declaring host readiness.
-
-Generic OpenSSL `-purpose any` is supported but is not covered by this vendor
-named-purpose distrust export. Both roots remained accepted in that mode in
-the isolated test. This procedure does not claim to fix every purpose or
-consumer and does not rewrite vendor output to change generic verification.
-
-Fresh OS-default contexts read the regenerated store. Existing SSL contexts
-and connection pools can keep their old roots until recreated. Apply before
-the next normal validator startup when possible. Any needed process refresh
-must use its existing canonical activation path; this procedure does not
-restart services. Certifi-backed clients and pip's vendored certifi use their
-own bundles and require their separate patched versions. The gateway's cached
-Arena proxy context is certifi-backed (`trust_env=False`); OS regeneration does
-not change that context. Host processes that use aiohttp's cached OS context
-need recreation to observe this change. Container/enclave stores are separate.
-
-## Rollback and retirement
-
-Rollback only files newly created by this application. First compare both
-installed files to the exact reviewed source and confirm they remain regular,
-root-owned files. Stop if their identity or contents changed. Remove only these
-two named blocklist files and run `/usr/bin/update-ca-trust` again. Verify the
-initial logical anchor sets and unrelated trust attributes are restored.
-Do not restore old generated bundles or remove unrelated blocklist entries.
-Existing contexts still require separate activation after a rollback.
-
-Retire this local override only after an approved vendor trust-bundle update
-itself rejects both exact certificates for the required named purposes.
-First prove this with only these two local entries removed in an isolated
-copy, preserve all other anchors, and repeat fresh-context and TLS controls.
-Then remove only the matching owned files, regenerate, and verify again.
-Until that evidence exists, retain the blocklist across vendor updates.
+No package or service action is part of this procedure. After extraction,
+require the measured source SHA256, root ownership and mode 0644. Require
+TLS/email/code-signing DER sets equal baseline minus G3 and all unrelated AUX
+bytes unchanged, including AAA. Fresh Python OS-default roots must equal the
+candidate TLS set. Repeat both full verification vectors and reject any new
+acceptance; require G3 error 28 for the nine modes listed above. Use explicit
+`-CAfile /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/openssl/ca-bundle.trust.crt`,
+`-no-CApath -no-CAstore`, and each `-purpose` (omit it for default). These are
+root self-verification controls, not forged-chain tests. Repeat the four fresh
+OS-default TLS/hostname controls before declaring the host ready.
+
+## Activation, rollback and retirement
+
+Fresh OS-default contexts read the regenerated store. Existing contexts/pools
+can retain old roots until recreated. Apply before the next planned validator
+startup when possible. Any required process refresh uses its existing
+canonical activation path; this procedure does not restart services. The
+cached gateway Arena proxy and provider HTTPX transport use patched certifi
+(`trust_env=False`), separate from OS trust. aiohttp can cache an OS context at
+import. Container/enclave stores and custom CA overrides are separate.
+
+For rollback, confirm the one destination is still a regular, root-owned file
+with the exact reviewed source SHA256 and mode. Stop on any mismatch. Remove
+only `/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem`, then run the
+pinned `/usr/bin/update-ca-trust`. Require the original DER sets, all AUX values,
+both full verification vectors and fresh OS contexts to match baseline.
+Do not restore old generated bundles or remove unrelated source entries.
+Rollback restores baseline G3 trust, so keep the security consequence explicit.
+Existing contexts may still need separate activation after rollback.
+
+Retire this local override only after an approved vendor bundle, tested without
+this exact local source in an isolated copy, rejects G3 for the same nine modes,
+preserves AAA/unrelated policy, introduces no acceptance in any measured mode,
+and passes fresh-context and four-host TLS controls. Then remove only the
+matching local file, regenerate and verify. Keep it across vendor updates until
+those exit criteria pass. Do not delete the recorded backup as part of apply.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+"""Pin the public G3 identity and its explicit OpenSSL AUX rejection policy."""
+
+import base64
+import hashlib
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+SOURCE = ROOT / "deploy/ca-trust/source/leadpoet-emsign-ecc-g3.trusted.pem"
+SOURCE_SHA256 = "661798181d9251cd062f8ece4712bfce980138ac3ac085b4a3c77b12065b892b"
+DER_SHA256 = "86a1ecba089c4a8d3bbe2734c612ba341d813e043cf9e8a862cd5c57a36bbe6b"
+# DER-encoded OID values. AUX rejects are independent of X.509 extensions.
+REJECTED_OIDS = {
+    "anyExtendedKeyUsage": "551d2500",       # 2.5.29.37.0
+    "serverAuth": "2b06010505070301",       # 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1
+    "clientAuth": "2b06010505070302",
+    "emailProtection": "2b06010505070304",
+    "codeSigning": "2b06010505070303",
+    "timeStamping": "2b06010505070308",
+    "OCSPSigning": "2b06010505070309",
+}
+
+
+def der_item(value):
+    """Read one definite-length DER item; return its content and remainder."""
+    assert len(value) >= 2
+    tag, size = value[:2]
+    offset = 2
+    if size & 0x80:
+        count = size & 0x7f
+        assert 0 < count <= 4 and len(value) >= offset + count
+        size = int.from_bytes(value[offset:offset + count], "big")
+        offset += count
+    end = offset + size
+    assert end <= len(value)
+    return tag, value[offset:end], value[end:]
+
+
+def trusted_payload():
+    match = re.fullmatch(
+        rb"-----BEGIN TRUSTED CERTIFICATE-----\n([A-Za-z0-9+/=\n]+)\n-----END TRUSTED CERTIFICATE-----\n",
+        SOURCE.read_bytes(),
+    )
+    assert match
+    return base64.b64decode(match[1].replace(b"\n", b""), validate=True)
+
+
+def test_exact_public_source_and_unchanged_x509_identity():
+    assert {p.name for p in SOURCE.parent.iterdir()} == {SOURCE.name}
+    assert not (ROOT / "deploy/ca-trust/blocklist").exists()
+    assert SOURCE.is_file() and not SOURCE.is_symlink()
+    assert hashlib.sha256(SOURCE.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == SOURCE_SHA256
+    payload = trusted_payload()
+    tag, _, aux = der_item(payload)
+    assert tag == 0x30 and aux
+    certificate = payload[:len(payload) - len(aux)]
+    assert hashlib.sha256(certificate).hexdigest() == DER_SHA256
+
+
+def test_aux_has_only_explicit_rejections_and_no_trusted_uses():
+    _, _, aux = der_item(trusted_payload())
+    tag, content, remainder = der_item(aux)
+    assert tag == 0x30 and not remainder
+    # X509_CERT_AUX has an optional trust SEQUENCE followed by reject [0].
+    # Requiring only [0] excludes every trusted use and any unreviewed AUX field.
+    tag, rejects, remainder = der_item(content)
+    assert tag == 0xA0 and not remainder
+    actual = []
+    while rejects:
+        tag, oid, rejects = der_item(rejects)
+        assert tag == 0x06
+        actual.append(oid.hex())
+    assert actual == list(REJECTED_OIDS.values())
+
+
+def test_operator_checksum_manifest_covers_the_only_installed_source():
+    relative = SOURCE.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
+    assert (ROOT / "deploy/ca-trust/SHA256SUMS").read_text() == f"{SOURCE_SHA256}  {relative}\n"

+the returned certificate against your request and policy, so it is the preferred
+check. If the live query remains pending, report those digests, your hotkey/UID,
+client revision and retry reason; preserve the original signed request and source.

+
 The command checks local hashes, verifies the cohort history, selects the model
 delivery mechanism from the signed plan or its authenticated transport adoption, waits for complete byte

+C5 certification is complete and C5 competition rewards are live. C6 is still in

+The C6 intake cutoff will be announced separately.
+
+## Submit a model for C6
+
+1. Keep the submitting hotkey registered on subnet **78**. Registration alone is
+   not cohort participation and does not guarantee a score or reward.
+2. [Install or update the published model client](miners/connection.md#install-or-update-the-model-submission-client) as the account that owns your wallet.
+3. Prepare the runnable bundle, signed submission and cohort consent using the
+   [model contribution requirements](contributors/models.md). Keep the exact
+   signed participation request and original source directory.
+4. Follow the [public-model upload steps](miners/model.md#model-files-for-recoverable-cohorts).

+   admission and review. A running endpoint is not required to submit this track.
+5. After upload, [query current admission](miners/model.md#check-admission-after-upload)
+   with the original request. The initial receipt stays `pending_attestation`;
+   it is not a live status display.

+the exact cohort and its history, accepted tracks, readiness and admission URL.
+For C6 and later, prepare public models; later openings require their authenticated
+successor plans. An older endpoint plan is not an instruction to enroll an endpoint
+for a successor that has not opened.
+
+## Understand the result
+
+| What you see | What it establishes |
+| --- | --- |
+| Upload/participation receipt with `pending_attestation` | The owner retained that request. This original acknowledgement does not update. |
+| `query-cohort-admission` returns `pending_attestation` | The current admission certificate is still pending for that exact request. |
+| `query-cohort-admission` returns `admission_certified` | Participation has a verified admission certificate. It is separate from scoring and final cohort certification. |
+| Published quality results | Evaluation results are available, with the published provisional/final scope. |
+| Finalized reward allocation and chain incentives | Reward activation has reached the chain. A dashboard balance or admission receipt alone does not prove a payment. |
+
+If the live admission query remains pending, preserve the request and report the
+cohort ID, consent digest, hotkey/UID, client revision and relevant retry reason.
+Do not create new nonces or replace the signed request merely to clear a temporary
+server hold. Do not share wallet secrets or presigned R2 capabilities.
+
+## Existing endpoint installations
+
+The [connection guide](miners/connection.md) remains authoritative for supported
+runtime upgrades, policy files and retained endpoint-state compatibility. Preserve
+existing assignment, grant, nonce and retirement journals. Endpoint participation
+and public-model participation are distinct; running an endpoint does not submit
+a model for C6.
+
+The [bridge specification](operators/bridge.md) remains relevant to historical
+policies and retained verification/recovery consumers. Its HTTPS keepalive rules
+are not the current C5 competition reward mechanism and do not replace C6 model
+submission. Check the [public results API](reference/competition-results-api.md)
+for the selected cohort and published result scope.

+"""``--share-setup``: send this process's hardware to the validator at start, then every few hours.
+
+Best effort: a refusal or an unreachable validator is logged and never stops mining.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import logging
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from reliquary.protocol.miner_setup import (
+    MINER_SETUP_PATH, MinerSetupRequest, build_miner_setup_binding, collect_miner_setup, load_instance_id,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+RESEND_EVERY_S = 6 * 3600
+
+
+async def send_miner_setup(client, *, validator_url: str, validator_hotkey: str, wallet, report) -> bool:
+    hotkey = wallet.hotkey.ss58_address
+    at = int(time.time())
+    binding = build_miner_setup_binding(hotkey=hotkey, at=at, report=report, validator_hotkey=validator_hotkey)
+    request = MinerSetupRequest(miner_hotkey=hotkey, at=at, report=report,
+                                signature=wallet.hotkey.sign(binding).hex())
+    try:
+        response = await client.post(validator_url.rstrip("/") + MINER_SETUP_PATH,
+                                     json=request.model_dump(mode="json"), timeout=15.0)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        logger.warning("miner setup not sent (%s)", type(exc).__name__)
+        return False
+    if response.status_code != 200:
+        logger.warning("miner setup refused: %s %s", response.status_code, response.text[:200])
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+async def share_setup_forever(client, *, validator_url: str, validator_hotkey: str, wallet, work_dir: str,
+                              note: str = "", every_s: float = RESEND_EVERY_S) -> None:
+    hotkey = wallet.hotkey.ss58_address
+    instance_id = load_instance_id(Path(work_dir) / "state" / "miner-setup-instance-id")
+    while True:
+        report = await asyncio.to_thread(collect_miner_setup, hotkey=hotkey, instance_id=instance_id, note=note)
+        if await send_miner_setup(client, validator_url=validator_url, validator_hotkey=validator_hotkey,
+                                  wallet=wallet, report=report):
+            logger.info("miner setup shared: %d GPU(s) %s", len(report.gpus),
+                        sorted({gpu.name for gpu in report.gpus}))
+        await asyncio.sleep(every_s)
+
+
+__all__ = ["send_miner_setup", "share_setup_forever"]

@@ -0,0 +1,156 @@
+"""Opt-in, self-declared miner hardware (``POST /miner/setup``).
+
+Nothing here is attested and nothing reads it for scoring or pay: it is a census the subnet owner asked miners to
+share. The request is still signed by the hotkey for one validator and route, so nobody declares for someone else.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
+
+MINER_SETUP_PATH = "/miner/setup"
+MINER_SETUP_DOMAIN = b"reliquary/miner-setup/v1"
+MAX_GPUS = 64
+
+
+class GpuInfo(BaseModel):
+    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
+
+    name: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=160)
+    memory_mib: int = Field(default=0, ge=0, le=10_000_000)
+    # sha256(hotkey, GPU UUID), truncated: counts each card once across a hotkey's processes without revealing it.
+    id_hash: str = Field(default="", pattern=r"^([0-9a-f]{16})?$")
+
+
+class MinerSetupReport(BaseModel):
+    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
+
+    instance_id: str = Field(..., pattern=r"^[0-9a-f]{16,64}$")
+    gpus: list[GpuInfo] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=MAX_GPUS)
+    cpu_count: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0, le=100_000)
+    ram_gib: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0, le=1_000_000)
+    note: str = Field(default="", max_length=500)
+
+
+class MinerSetupRequest(BaseModel):
+    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
+
+    miner_hotkey: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=64)
+    at: int = Field(..., ge=0)
+    report: MinerSetupReport
+    signature: str = Field(default="", max_length=256)
+
+
+def _report_digest(report: MinerSetupReport) -> bytes:
+    body = json.dumps(report.model_dump(mode="json"), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
+    return hashlib.sha256(body.encode("utf-8")).digest()
+
+
+def build_miner_setup_binding(*, hotkey: str, at: int, report: MinerSetupReport, validator_hotkey: str,
+                              path: str = MINER_SETUP_PATH) -> bytes:
+    parts = [str(hotkey).encode("utf-8"), int(at).to_bytes(8, "big", signed=False), _report_digest(report),
+             str(validator_hotkey).encode("utf-8"), str(path).encode("utf-8")]
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    h.update(MINER_SETUP_DOMAIN)
+    for part in parts:
+        h.update(len(part).to_bytes(4, "big"))
+        h.update(part)
+    return h.digest()
+
+
+def verify_miner_setup_signature(request: MinerSetupRequest, *, validator_hotkey: str,
+                                 path: str = MINER_SETUP_PATH) -> bool:
+    from reliquary.protocol.signatures import verify_hotkey_signature
+
+    try:
+        binding = build_miner_setup_binding(hotkey=request.miner_hotkey, at=request.at, report=request.report,
+                                            validator_hotkey=validator_hotkey, path=path)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError):
+        return False
+    return verify_hotkey_signature(request.miner_hotkey, binding, request.signature)
+
+
+# --- collection on the miner -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def _visible(devices: list[dict], visible: str | None) -> list[dict]:
+    """The GPUs this process may use: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES by index or UUID (unset: all of them)."""
+    if visible is None:
+        return devices
+    wanted = [item.strip() for item in visible.split(",") if item.strip()]
+    picked = []
+    for item in wanted:
+        if item.isdigit():
+            picked += [d for d in devices if d["index"] == int(item)]
+        else:
+            picked += [d for d in devices if d["uuid"].startswith(item)]
+    return picked
+
+
+def query_gpus(run=subprocess.run) -> list[dict]:
+    """``nvidia-smi``'s GPUs (index, name, memory_mib, uuid); empty without it. Never initialises CUDA here, so
+    vLLM still owns the device."""
+    if shutil.which("nvidia-smi") is None and run is subprocess.run:
+        return []
+    try:
+        out = run(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,uuid", "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"],
+                  capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10, check=True).stdout
+    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
+        return []
+    devices = []
+    for line in out.splitlines():
+        fields = [f.strip() for f in line.split(",")]
+        if len(fields) != 4 or not fields[0].isdigit():
+            continue
+        try:
+            memory = int(float(fields[2]))
+        except ValueError:
+            memory = 0
+        devices.append({"index": int(fields[0]), "name": fields[1], "memory_mib": memory, "uuid": fields[3]})
+    return devices
+
+
+def _ram_gib() -> float | None:
+    try:
+        return round(os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE") * os.sysconf("SC_PHYS_PAGES") / 2**30, 1)
+    except (ValueError, OSError, AttributeError):
+        return None
+
+
+def collect_miner_setup(*, hotkey: str, instance_id: str, note: str = "", devices: list[dict] | None = None,
+                        visible: str | None = None) -> MinerSetupReport:
+    if devices is None:
+        devices = query_gpus()
+        visible = os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES")
+    gpus = [GpuInfo(name=d["name"][:160] or "unknown", memory_mib=d["memory_mib"],
+                    id_hash=hashlib.sha256(f"{hotkey}:{d['uuid']}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16] if d["uuid"] else "")
+            for d in _visible(devices, visible)][:MAX_GPUS]
+    return MinerSetupReport(instance_id=instance_id, gpus=gpus, cpu_count=os.cpu_count(), ram_gib=_ram_gib(),
+                            note=note[:500])
+
+
+def load_instance_id(path) -> str:
+    """This miner process's id, kept under its work dir so a restart reports as the same instance."""
+    from pathlib import Path
+
+    path = Path(path)
+    try:
+        value = path.read_text().strip()
+        if len(value) == 32 and all(c in "0123456789abcdef" for c in value):
+            return value
+    except OSError:
+        pass
+    value = os.urandom(16).hex()
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(value + "\n")
+    return value
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "GpuInfo", "MINER_SETUP_PATH", "MinerSetupReport", "MinerSetupRequest", "build_miner_setup_binding",
+    "collect_miner_setup", "load_instance_id", "query_gpus", "verify_miner_setup_signature",
+]

+"""``POST /miner/setup``: keep the latest hardware each opted-in miner process declares (``protocol/miner_setup.py``).
+
+Stored in the validator's state dir, read with ``reliquary miner-setups``; never served publicly, never scored.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import json
+import logging
+import sqlite3
+import threading
+import time
+from collections import Counter
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Awaitable, Callable
+
+from fastapi import APIRouter
+from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
+
+from reliquary.protocol.miner_setup import MINER_SETUP_PATH, MinerSetupRequest, verify_miner_setup_signature
+from reliquary.validator.corpus_registration import NOT_REGISTERED, UNAVAILABLE
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+DB_NAME = "miner-setups.sqlite3"
+REQUEST_SKEW_S = 120
+MIN_INTERVAL_S = 60          # per hotkey and instance
+MAX_INSTANCES_PER_HOTKEY = 32
+ACTIVE_WINDOW_S = 24 * 3600
+
+
+class MinerSetupStore:
+    def __init__(self, path: str | Path) -> None:
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._db = sqlite3.connect(str(path), check_same_thread=False)
+        self._db.execute(
+            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS setups (hotkey TEXT NOT NULL, instance_id TEXT NOT NULL, "
+            "at INTEGER NOT NULL, received_at REAL NOT NULL, report TEXT NOT NULL, "
+            "PRIMARY KEY (hotkey, instance_id))")
+        self._db.commit()
+
+    def put(self, hotkey: str, instance_id: str, at: int, received_at: float, report: dict,
+            *, min_interval_s: float | None = None) -> bool:
+        with self._lock, self._db:
+            self._db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
+            if min_interval_s is not None:
+                last = self._db.execute("SELECT at, received_at FROM setups WHERE hotkey=? AND instance_id=?",
+                                        (hotkey, instance_id)).fetchone()
+                if last is not None and (at <= last[0] or received_at - last[1] < min_interval_s):
+                    return False
+            self._db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO setups VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
+                             (hotkey, instance_id, at, received_at, json.dumps(report, sort_keys=True)))
+            # Bound one hotkey's rows: its oldest instances go first.
+            self._db.execute(
+                "DELETE FROM setups WHERE hotkey=? AND instance_id NOT IN (SELECT instance_id FROM setups "
+                "WHERE hotkey=? ORDER BY received_at DESC LIMIT ?)", (hotkey, hotkey, MAX_INSTANCES_PER_HOTKEY))
+            return True
+
+    def rows(self) -> list[dict]:
+        with self._lock:
+            rows = self._db.execute(
+                "SELECT hotkey, instance_id, at, received_at, report FROM setups ORDER BY hotkey, received_at"
+            ).fetchall()
+        return [{"hotkey": h, "instance_id": i, "at": a, "received_at": r, "report": json.loads(rep)}
+                for h, i, a, r, rep in rows]
+
+
+def summarize(rows: list[dict], *, now: float | None = None, active_window_s: float = ACTIVE_WINDOW_S) -> list[dict]:
+    """One line per hotkey over its instances seen within ``active_window_s``: each card counted once."""
+    now = time.time() if now is None else now
+    by_hotkey: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
+    for row in rows:
+        if now - row["received_at"] <= active_window_s:
+            by_hotkey.setdefault(row["hotkey"], []).append(row)
+    out = []
+    for hotkey, items in sorted(by_hotkey.items()):
+        cards: dict[str, str] = {}
+        anonymous: list[str] = []
+        notes = []
+        for row in items:
+            for gpu in row["report"].get("gpus", []):
+                if gpu.get("id_hash"):
+                    cards[gpu["id_hash"]] = gpu["name"]
+                else:
+                    anonymous.append(gpu["name"])
+            if row["report"].get("note"):
+                notes.append(row["report"]["note"])
+        gpus = Counter(list(cards.values()) + anonymous)
+        out.append({"hotkey": hotkey, "instances": len(items), "gpu_count": sum(gpus.values()),
+                    "gpus": dict(gpus), "notes": sorted(set(notes)),
+                    "last_seen": max(row["received_at"] for row in items)})
+    return out
+
+
+def build_miner_setup_router(store: MinerSetupStore, *, validator_hotkey: str,
+                             registration: Callable[[str], Awaitable[str | None]] | None = None,
+                             clock: Callable[[], float] = time.time, request_skew_s: int = REQUEST_SKEW_S,
+                             min_interval_s: float = MIN_INTERVAL_S,
+                             verify: Callable[..., bool] = verify_miner_setup_signature) -> APIRouter:
+    router = APIRouter()
+
+    def refuse(status: int, reason: str, **extra) -> JSONResponse:
+        return JSONResponse(status_code=status, content={"error": reason, **extra})
+
+    @router.post(MINER_SETUP_PATH)
+    async def miner_setup(request: MinerSetupRequest):
+        now = clock()
+        if not request.signature:
+            return refuse(401, "signature_required")
+        if abs(int(now) - request.at) > request_skew_s:
+            return refuse(409, "stale_request", max_skew_s=request_skew_s, now=int(now))
+        if not await asyncio.to_thread(verify, request, validator_hotkey=validator_hotkey, path=MINER_SETUP_PATH):
+            return refuse(403, "bad_signature")
+        if registration is not None:
+            try:
+                why = await registration(request.miner_hotkey)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                logger.warning("miner setup registration check failed (%s)", type(exc).__name__)
+                why = UNAVAILABLE
+            if why == NOT_REGISTERED:
+                return refuse(403, "hotkey_not_registered")
+            if why is not None:
+                return refuse(503, "registration_unavailable")
+        instance = request.report.instance_id
+        stored = await asyncio.to_thread(store.put, request.miner_hotkey, instance, request.at, now,
+                                         request.report.model_dump(mode="json"), min_interval_s=min_interval_s)
+        if not stored:
+            return refuse(429, "too_frequent", min_interval_s=min_interval_s)
+        return {"stored": True}
+
+    return router
+
+
+__all__ = ["DB_NAME", "MinerSetupStore", "build_miner_setup_router", "summarize"]

@@ -260,6 +260,45 @@ probe for UIDs flagged by these signals.
 - Every hotkey pays the subnet registration burn, which is the natural per-node cost.
 - With the rules above, a sybil hotkey earns nothing extra, so its registration is pure cost.
 
+### 4.6 Per-coldkey diminishing returns (replaces the lite brake)
+From `COLDKEY_DR_START_UTC` (date set in the release notes; until then nothing in this section applies and the order_ratio
+0.5 brake of section 5 stays) the small pools **s1-lite and s1-cpu** (`COLDKEY_DR_POOLS`) treat all hotkeys of one coldkey as one operator.
+s1-fast and s1-pro are not touched: there pay is linear in verified throughput (mechanism v2), one hotkey per machine is
+never worse than several, and the big coldkeys sit at the per-hotkey cap, i.e. they are real verified capacity. The
+brake this replaces only ever acted on the small tiers. Setting `COLDKEY_DR_POOLS` to all four pools makes the same rule
+apply to the GPU pools as well (simulated below as the alternative; not the default).
+
+- **Per pool, per coldkey.** The eligible slots of one coldkey in one pool are ranked by their in-pool score (`ema` x
+  capacity factor), best first, ties by slot id. The k-th slot keeps its whole score for k <= 2 (`COLDKEY_FREE_SLOTS`) and
+  is multiplied by 0.7 for every slot after that (`COLDKEY_DR_RATIO`): 3rd slot 70 %, 4th 49 %, 5th 34 %, 10th 5.8 %.
+  However many hotkeys a coldkey registers, they count for at most 2 + 0.7 / 0.3 = 4.33 full hotkeys in a pool.
+- **Nothing is burned.** The pool's share is split over the reduced scores as before, so the weight a farm loses goes
+  pro rata to every other miner of the pool. A coldkey with one or two hotkeys in a pool is not reduced; it gains only what
+  the pool redistributes.
+- **Tier-order cap on effective miners.** The cap of section 5 counts the sum of the factors per tier (effective miners)
+  instead of slots for tiers whose pools are in the set (slots as before for the others), so adding hotkeys no longer raises a tier's cap, and its ratio is 1.0 (the 0.5 brake is replaced, not
+  stacked). The 80 / 15 / 5 budgets stay the hard cap.
+- **Same hotkey, several pools.** Pools are separate: one hotkey in s1-fast and s1-pro is one slot in each.
+- **Unknown coldkey.** A slot whose UID has no coldkey in the metagraph snapshot counts as its own coldkey (fail open for
+  honest miners).
+- **What it does not do.** A farm that spreads its hotkeys over N coldkeys keeps 2 free slots per coldkey. The rule makes that
+  cost one more coldkey per two hotkeys; it cannot see links that are not on chain.
+
+Simulation on the live dashboard (21 Oct 10:12Z, 235 paid miners, `tools/sim_coldkey_dr.py`, numbers from `SIM.md` in the
+job folder), default scope (s1-lite, s1-cpu), raw change of pay (includes the weight the rule frees and the lifted brake):
+
+| pool | miner with one hotkey in the pool | 26-hotkey s1-lite coldkey |
+|---|---|---|
+| s1-fast | -4 % | n/a |
+| s1-pro | -4 % | n/a |
+| s1-lite | +98 % | -66 % |
+| s1-cpu | +243 % | n/a |
+
+The GPU pools lose 4 % because the lite brake used to send the small tier's excess up to the GPU tier; with the brake gone
+the tiers sit at their 80 / 15 / 5 budgets (GPU 83.4 % -> 80.0 %, small 16.2 % -> 18.9 %, cpu 0.3 % -> 1.2 %). The four
+big coldkeys: the s1-lite coldkey -66 %, the three GPU coldkeys -4 % each (they are not reduced). Alternative with all four
+pools: the s1-pro and s1-fast big coldkeys lose 45-71 %, every single-hotkey miner gains +32 % to +243 %.
+

files.patch:
@@ -112,6 +112,77 @@ them. Items never repeat inside the timed runs, so a legitimate exact-match cach
 - **Frozen thresholds:** margin, min gain, agreement gate, distance budget, items, runs and confirmations live in one block, `src/reax_subnet/engthresholds.py`. Its sha256 is logged when the validator starts and written into the state file (`thresholds_sha256`); changing a value is a new release.
 - Each validator keeps its own champion state; Yuma consensus combines them (stake-weighted), as for serving scores.
 
+## 5a. Reusing other entries (copy line)
+
+*From `ENGINE_COPYLINE_START_UTC` in `src/reax_subnet/engcomp.py` (date set in the release notes). Until then the previous
+rule applies unchanged: an entry that reuses another miner's files is judged by review alone.*
+
+Recombining what works is a legitimate way to make progress; repackaging is not. The line:
+
+1. **Ideas are free.** Re-implementing a technique you saw in a public entry is always allowed, with no declaration.
+2. **Reusing another entry's code, source or binaries, is allowed only if you declare it.** The image carries the label
+   `ai.reax.engine.parents`, a JSON list: `[{"uid": 4, "digest": "<64 hex of the parent image>", "files": ["/app/engine.py", "/app/kernels/"]}]`
+   (at most 8 parents, at most 2,000 files per parent, label at most 128 KiB; `files` are the paths in YOUR image whose content
+   comes from that parent, and an entry ending in `/` is a directory prefix covering everything below it). Such an entry
+   counts as **derived**: in every confirming session it must beat **every declared parent** by the full challenger margin (the
+   engine track's margin: 3 % or 3x the reference noise, whichever is larger), on top of the normal champion bar.
+   - **The parent is its hotkey.** The bar is the best valid score ever measured for ANY digest committed by the hotkey that
+     committed the declared parent digest. The declared `uid` must belong to that hotkey: if it does not, the label is a problem
+     and that entry is held out of the title until it is fixed. Only when the committer of the digest is not yet known is the
+     declared uid's hotkey used, read once and fixed. The set belongs to that one entry: another entry's label can never
+     change it, and a uid that is re-registered later changes nothing. Naming an old or weak digest of the parent, or a parent
+     whose latest run failed, does not lower it; the best score is kept even if the parent is measured again.
+   - **No score, no crowning.** A declared parent with no valid score yet holds the entry (never crowned, never on a missing
+     bar) until the parent has been measured.
+   - **Only declared parents set bars.** The validators build the bar from the label alone. Reuse that review finds but the
+     label does not declare is not a bar: it is a copy (point 4).
+   - **Read first.** From the start date an entry can be crowned only after its review record has been read: a missing or
+     unreadable record, or a label with any problem (bad JSON, nested deeper than 4 levels, more than 8 parents or 2,000 files
+     per parent), keeps that entry out of the title until it is fixed. A validator without a review directory crowns nobody.
+     A record written before the start date has no label fields: for an unmeasured digest the check runs again before its first
+     run; for an already-measured, eligible digest the validators re-read the image labels once (docker image inspect). Until
+     then it cannot be crowned, but it stays in the pool and nobody has to recommit. Only an image that is gone (not on
+     the host and not pullable by its digest) counts as "no parents declared" (it was measured before the rule; undeclared
+     reuse is still caught by a COPY marker). A docker error or timeout changes nothing: the re-read is retried next cycle
+     and the entry stays out of the title until it succeeds. A measured digest whose record is missing stays out of the
+     title (in release mode every measured digest has a record).
+3. **Binaries are treated like source, and closing code gives no protection and no payout.** A closed binary (`.so`, `.cubin`, ...
+   without published source; `.safetensors` and `.bin` files inside directories named exactly model, models, weights,
+   checkpoint(s) or tokenizer(s) are weights and not counted; any other `.bin` is listed as "weights? (check)") may be reused under the same declaration and the same
+   full-margin rule. But a component without published source keeps its entry **unpaid**: the owner's signed award approval is
+   withheld until the source is published. This is done by hand (no code gates it): **closed components present -> withhold the
+   approval**; it is on the review checklist and printed by the review tool.
+4. **Undeclared reuse found by our review is a copy.** The reviewer creates `COPY/<digest>`; **the marker alone is enough**
+   (`REVIEWED/<digest>` is not needed and is not created for a copy). In that cycle the commitment fails (it is never run) and
+   counts as a strike. The first strike has no further consequence; the **second and every later** one pauses that hotkey for
+   **7 days** (50 400 blocks; a later strike restarts the 7 days from its own block, never shortening a longer pause). A marker
+   put on an entry that was already measured, a former champion or the champion has the same effect: its result becomes a
+   failure, it is vacated if it holds the title, and it leaves the former-champion ranks and the keep-alive.
+5. **The same owner may reuse its own code freely**: parents on the same coldkey (chain snapshot), or a signed ownership proof
+   (below), are not constraints and are not copies.
+
+**While a hotkey is paused** it is out of the challenger pool, out of confirmation sessions and cannot be crowned; its new
+commitments are not evaluated. What it already earns from earlier, non-copy entries continues: the champion share of a
+sitting champion and the former-champion ranks (the former-champion slot keep-alive continues); waiting entries of a paused
+hotkey get no waiting keep-alive. A copy itself earns nothing.
+
+**Where the declaration lives.** In the image label, not in the chain commitment: the on-chain field is 128 bytes and an engine
+commitment already uses most of it. The label is part of the image configuration, which is part of the digest, so the declaration
+is bound to exactly the image that is run and cannot be changed afterwards; the pre-run check already reads the labels.
+
+**Ownership proof (different coldkeys, one owner).** The parent's hotkey signs (sr25519) the text
+`reax-eng/1 same-owner:<parent hotkey>><child hotkey>:<parent digest>` and the child image carries
+`ai.reax.engine.ownership=[{"parent_digest": "...", "parent_hotkey": "...", "signature": "<hex>"}]`. Validators accept it only
+when the signature verifies (`bittensor.sp_core.verify`) for exactly that parent digest and child hotkey; without the chain
+library the proof is not accepted.
+
+**Review tooling and checklist.** `tools/engine_parents_check.py CHILD_DIR --parent DIGEST=DIR ... --declared <label>` compares the
+extracted trees and prints the identical files and binaries, declared vs detected, and the verdict: "derived (declared)", "copy
+(undeclared)", "same owner", "independent" or "unverified declaration". It needs no docker. Pass every digest of the parent's
+hotkey; a declared digest without a tree is reported (exit 3). Checklist: (1) run the tool against the declared parents' hotkeys;
+(2) shared but undeclared files -> create `COPY/<child digest>` (exit 2); (3) closed components listed -> withhold the award
+approval until their source is published; (4) otherwise create `REVIEWED/<digest>` as usual.
+

 The split between serving and the competitions is defined once in [COMPETITIONS.md](COMPETITIONS.md)

+## Award-time Decision-Index check
+
+Before any generalist award request, the release owner's award pipeline scores the candidate and the official base
+(REAX 1, `decisionmodels/reax-1@ca2a0cc5...`) on the frozen house DI-proxy eval: the HF-DI-style composite (0.6 private
+same-skill + 0.4 private new-domain) plus the AA-style part, in the model's native protocol where it has one. This is a
+GPU run of about 10 minutes per candidate on the gen box and is not part of the validator. It exists so we do not pay for
+gains on our own pool that do not hold on the Decision Indices.
+
+`tools/award_di_proxy.py` takes the two per-item result files (`id`, `unit`/`area`, `weight_group`, `score` in [0,1],
+`protocol`), `--eval-file` with its expected `--eval-sha` (checked by the tool) and the ids, and prints the `di_proxy`
+block `{done, eval_id, eval_sha, protocol, base_id, items, score, base_score, diff, se}` in points (0-100, 4 decimals).
+It refuses mismatched item sets, duplicate or missing ids, NaN, out-of-range scores, differing unit/protocol per item and
+an eval sha mismatch. Composite weights come from a small JSON (unit -> weight, normalised; default equal over units).
+
+The comparison is paired per item: `diff` = weighted mean of (candidate - base) item scores, with the same weights.
+`se` is the larger of a stratified paired bootstrap (2,000 resamples per run, seeded) and the analytic paired SE.
+Threshold (non-inferiority): `lower90 = diff - 1.2816 x se >= -0.5` points. If the check fails, or the block is missing
+or not `done`, the signer does not release the award automatically and raises a manual card to Florian with the block
+and the item-level files. The tool only produces the numbers; the decision stays with the signer.
+

 - Set the opening and actual notice time together; notice defaults to disabled and must be no later than opening.
