files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,195 @@
+"""An RL run's held-out feed (``run_feed``) in W&B, in a dedicated evaluation run beside the trainer's.
+
+Two writes to that run (``<group>-evals`` by default, never the trainer's own: it has one writer):
+
+* ``publish_summary``: the whole ``reliquary.run-benchmarks.v1`` envelope as the summary key
+  ``reliquary_run_benchmarks``, which the platform's run monitor reads (``WANDB_RL_BENCHMARK_RUN_ID``,
+  reliquary-platform ``worker/run-benchmarks.ts`` ``readWandbRunBenchmarks``). Idempotent: an envelope equal to the
+  stored one but for ``observed_at`` is not written again. W&B stores a nested summary object flattened, as
+  ``reliquary_run_benchmarks.schema`` ... ``reliquary_run_benchmarks.benchmarks`` (lists stay whole): a reader rebuilds
+  the envelope from those keys (``stored_envelope``).
+* ``log_feed``: each new point as a history row, ``eval/<short>/pass@1`` and its ``delta`` to the baseline, plotted
+  against ``rl_step``. Logged points are remembered in a small JSON file, so each one is logged once.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import time
+from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+TRAINER_SUFFIX = "-trainer"
+SUMMARY_KEY = "reliquary_run_benchmarks"
+DEFAULT_PROJECT = "reliquary-validator"
+JOB_TYPE = "evaluation"
+
+
+def eval_run_ids(trainer_run_id: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    """``(group, run id)`` of the eval run beside ``trainer_run_id`` (``{group}-trainer``, ``telemetry.init``)."""
+    group = trainer_run_id[:-len(TRAINER_SUFFIX)] if trainer_run_id.endswith(TRAINER_SUFFIX) else trainer_run_id
+    return group, f"{group}-evals"
+
+
+def target(trainer_run_id: str, *, run_id: str | None = None, project: str | None = None,
+           entity: str | None = None) -> dict:
+    """Where the evaluation run is: flags, then ``WANDB_PROJECT`` / ``WANDB_ENTITY``, then defaults."""
+    from reliquary.eval.run_feed import RUN_ID
+
+    group, default_id = eval_run_ids(trainer_run_id)
+    run_id = run_id or default_id
+    if not RUN_ID.fullmatch(run_id):
+        raise ValueError(f"wandb run id {run_id!r}: letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-'")
+    if run_id == trainer_run_id:
+        raise ValueError("the evaluation run must not be the trainer's run: the trainer is its only writer")
+    return {"run_id": run_id, "group": group,
+            "project": project or os.getenv("WANDB_PROJECT") or DEFAULT_PROJECT,
+            "entity": entity or os.getenv("WANDB_ENTITY") or None}
+
+
+def _wandb_init(*, run_id: str, group: str, project: str | None = None, entity: str | None = None,
+                config: dict | None = None):
+    import wandb
+
+    run = wandb.init(project=project or os.getenv("WANDB_PROJECT") or DEFAULT_PROJECT,
+                     entity=entity or os.getenv("WANDB_ENTITY") or None, id=run_id, group=group,
+                     job_type=JOB_TYPE, resume="allow", config=config or {})
+    run.define_metric("rl_step")
+    run.define_metric("eval/*", step_metric="rl_step")
+    return run
+
+
+def stored_envelope(summary: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
+    """The envelope in a run's raw summary (``summaryMetrics``): the object itself, or rebuilt from its flattened
+    ``reliquary_run_benchmarks.<path>`` keys as the W&B server stores it. None when absent."""
+    if isinstance(summary.get(SUMMARY_KEY), Mapping):
+        return summary[SUMMARY_KEY]
+    prefix, found = SUMMARY_KEY + ".", {}
+    for key, value in summary.items():
+        if not key.startswith(prefix):
+            continue
+        *parents, leaf = key[len(prefix):].split(".")
+        node = found
+        for part in parents:
+            node = node.setdefault(part, {})
+        node[leaf] = value
+    return found or None
+
+
+def _stored_summary(*, run_id: str, project: str, entity: str | None) -> Any:
+    """The envelope stored in the run's summary, None when the run or the key does not exist."""
+    import wandb
+
+    api = wandb.Api()
+    try:
+        run = api.run(f"{entity or api.default_entity}/{project}/{run_id}")
+    except Exception:           # wandb.errors.CommError: no such run yet
+        return None
+    return stored_envelope(json.loads(json.dumps(dict(run.summary_metrics or {}))))
+
+
+def _same(a: Any, b: Any) -> bool:
+    if not isinstance(a, Mapping) or not isinstance(b, Mapping):
+        return False
+    return {**a, "observed_at": None} == {**b, "observed_at": None}
+
+
+def publish_summary(feed: Mapping[str, Any], *, run_id: str | None = None, project: str | None = None,
+                    entity: str | None = None, init: Callable[..., Any] = _wandb_init,
+                    stored: Callable[..., Any] = _stored_summary, now_ms: float | None = None) -> dict:
+    """Write ``feed`` into the evaluation run's summary under ``reliquary_run_benchmarks``. The envelope keeps the
+    TRAINER's run id (the dashboard matches it against its trainer source); the platform's checks run first."""
+    from reliquary.eval.run_feed import encode_feed, parse_feed
+
+    where = target(feed["run_id"], run_id=run_id, project=project, entity=entity)
+    body = encode_feed(feed)                                    # the platform's 512 KiB bound
+    parse_feed(json.loads(body), feed["run_id"], time.time() * 1000 if now_ms is None else now_ms)
+    out = {"run": where["run_id"], "project": where["project"], "entity": where["entity"],
+           "key": SUMMARY_KEY, "bytes": len(body)}
+    if _same(stored(run_id=where["run_id"], project=where["project"], entity=where["entity"]), feed):
+        return {**out, "written": False}
+    run = init(run_id=where["run_id"], group=where["group"], project=where["project"], entity=where["entity"],
+               config={"trainer_run_id": feed["run_id"]})
+    run.summary[SUMMARY_KEY] = json.loads(body)
+    run.finish()
+    return {**out, "written": True}
+
+
+def new_rows(feed: Mapping[str, Any], short_of: Mapping[str, str], logged: set[str]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[str]]:
+    """One wandb row per step not yet logged: ``eval/<short>/pass@1`` and its ``delta`` to the baseline. Returns
+    the rows (by step) and the ``<short>@<step>`` marks they cover. The baseline (step null: the start checkpoint)
+    is plotted at ``rl_step`` 0. Ungraded points wait for a later feed."""
+    rows: dict[int, dict] = {}
+    marks = []
+    for bench in feed["benchmarks"]:
+        key = short_of.get(bench["id"]) or bench["id"]
+        base = bench.get("baseline")
+        base_score = None if base is None else base.get("score")
+        for point in ([base] if base is not None else []) + list(bench["checkpoints"]):
+            step = 0 if point.get("step") is None else int(point["step"])
+            mark = f"{key}@{step}"
+            if point.get("score") is None or mark in logged:
+                continue
+            row = rows.setdefault(step, {"rl_step": step})
+            row[f"eval/{key}/pass@1"] = float(point["score"])
+            if base_score is not None:
+                row[f"eval/{key}/delta"] = float(point["score"]) - float(base_score)
+            marks.append(mark)
+    return [rows[s] for s in sorted(rows)], marks
+
+
+def log_feed(feed: Mapping[str, Any], *, short_of: Mapping[str, str], state_path: Path,
+             init: Callable[..., Any] = _wandb_init, run_id: str | None = None, project: str | None = None,
+             entity: str | None = None) -> dict:
+    """Log the feed's new points; fail-soft (the feed itself is unaffected), unlogged points retried next time."""
+    state_path = Path(state_path)
+    where = target(feed["run_id"], run_id=run_id, project=project, entity=entity)
+    try:
+        if where["entity"] is None:
+            import wandb
+
+            where["entity"] = wandb.Api().default_entity
+            if not isinstance(where["entity"], str) or not where["entity"]:
+                raise ValueError("W&B default entity is unavailable")
+        identity = {"trainer_run_id": feed["run_id"], "entity": where["entity"],
+                    "project": where["project"], "run_id": where["run_id"]}
+        destination = json.dumps(identity, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
+        state = json.loads(state_path.read_text()) if state_path.exists() else {}
+        # Unbound marks cannot establish delivery; retain each destination on a switch back.
+        targets = state.get("targets", {}) if isinstance(state, dict) else {}
+        logged = set(targets.get(destination, []))
+        rows, marks = new_rows(feed, short_of, logged)
+        if not rows:
+            return {"run": where["run_id"], "logged": 0}
+        run = init(run_id=where["run_id"], group=where["group"], project=where["project"], entity=where["entity"],
+                   config={"trainer_run_id": feed["run_id"]})
+        for row in rows:
+            run.log(row)
+        run.finish()
+        tmp = state_path.with_suffix(".tmp")
+        tmp.write_text(json.dumps({"targets": {**targets, destination: sorted(logged | set(marks))}}))
+        tmp.replace(state_path)
+    except Exception as exc:        # wandb down or misconfigured: the scores stay in the feed
+        logger.warning("wandb eval log failed (%s); points kept for the next feed", exc)
+        return {"run": where["run_id"], "logged": 0, "error": type(exc).__name__}
+    return {"run": where["run_id"], "logged": len(marks)}
+
+
+def mirror(feed: Mapping[str, Any], *, short_of: Mapping[str, str], state_path: Path, **where: Any) -> dict:
+    """Both writes, fail-soft (``eval schedule``): a W&B outage never stops the schedule; the next feed retries."""
+    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
+    try:
+        out["summary"] = publish_summary(feed, **where)
+    except Exception as exc:        # noqa: BLE001
+        logger.warning("wandb summary write failed (%s), retried with the next feed", exc)
+        out["summary"] = {"written": False, "error": type(exc).__name__}
+    out["history"] = log_feed(feed, short_of=short_of, state_path=state_path, **where)
+    return out
+
+
+__all__ = ["SUMMARY_KEY", "eval_run_ids", "log_feed", "mirror", "new_rows", "publish_summary", "stored_envelope",
+           "target"]

primaryCommitChecks.message:
rent hardening: GPU-type outage cooldown + accurate live-roster phases

Outage cooldown. Host quarantine keeps one machine out of the listings, so a
supply-side outage walked the trainer onto the next dying machine of the same
GPU type: 2026-10-21 19:03 three H100 pods (the era-2593 king + two payer
legs) went unreachable together, the king re-rented an H100 and lost it 13 min
after boot, and only an L40 at 20:07 trained the leg. Pod losses (unreachable
mid-leg) are now recorded per GPU type (provision/sku_outage.py, persisted
like the host quarantine); 2+ distinct pods of a type lost within an hour put
that type in a 3 h cooldown, and _funded_skus_for_rent moves it out while
another type remains. Prefer, never forbid: if only cooling types are offered
they are still rented. Tests isolate the cooldown file via conftest.

Live-roster phases (fix for #375). The phase came from the funded pod ledger,
but a trainer restart rewrites every in-flight row (new rented_at, no pod
uid), so after the 04:22 restart every in-flight leg read "training since
04:22", including one still waiting for a GPU. The phase is now recorded
where it happens: starting (rent intent / each attempt), waiting_gpu (capacity
wait), training (pod ready; an ADOPTED pod after a restart publishes no
"since", the true start being unknown), benching/awaiting_settlement (the
leg thread after training). Entries also carry started_block.

Rent policy + presentational only: no contract, manifest or consensus change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@
+"""GPU-type outage cooldown: correlated pod loss steers rents to other types.
+
+Host quarantine (``record_host_quarantine``) keeps ONE machine out of the
+listings. A supply-side outage takes down many machines of the same type at
+once, and per-host quarantine then just walks the trainer onto the next dying
+machine of that type: 2026-10-21 19:03, three H100 pods (the era-2593 king and
+two payer legs) went unreachable together; the king re-rented an H100 at 19:21
+and lost it 13 min after boot, while an L40 rented at 20:07 trained the full
+leg. This module records pod losses per GPU type and reports a type as
+COOLING once ``MIN_EVENTS`` distinct pods of it were lost inside ``WINDOW``;
+it stays cooling for ``COOL_SECONDS`` after the last loss. Callers PREFER
+other types while one cools (never forbid: if only cooling types are offered
+they are still used — a wait for capacity is worse than a risky rent).
+
+Presentational to consensus: rent policy only, no contract or manifest change.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+SKU_OUTAGE_FILE_ENV = "CASCADE_LIUM_SKU_OUTAGE_FILE"
+WINDOW_SECONDS = 3600.0       # losses this close together are one outage
+MIN_EVENTS = 2                # distinct pods lost inside the window
+COOL_SECONDS = 3 * 3600.0     # prefer other types this long after the last loss
+KEEP_SECONDS = 24 * 3600.0    # events older than this are pruned
+
+
+def sku_outage_path() -> Path:
+    return Path(os.environ.get(
+        SKU_OUTAGE_FILE_ENV, "~/.cache/cascade/lium_sku_outage.json")).expanduser()
+
+
+def _load(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
+    try:
+        raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
+        return []
+    return [e for e in raw if isinstance(e, dict) and "t" in e and "sku" in e] \
+        if isinstance(raw, list) else []
+
+
+def record_pod_loss(sku: str, pod: str, reason: str, *, path: Path | None = None,
+                    now: float | None = None) -> None:
+    """Record that a pod of ``sku`` was lost (unreachable mid-leg)."""
+    sku = str(sku or "").strip()
+    if not sku:
+        return
+    path = path or sku_outage_path()
+    now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
+    try:
+        events = [e for e in _load(path) if now - float(e["t"]) < KEEP_SECONDS]
+        events.append({"t": now, "sku": sku, "pod": str(pod)[:120],
+                       "reason": str(reason)[:200]})
+        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        tmp = path.with_suffix(".json.tmp")
+        tmp.write_text(json.dumps(events), encoding="utf-8")
+        tmp.replace(path)
+        if sku in cooling_skus(path=path, now=now):
+            log.warning("lium: %s pods lost %d+ times within %.0f min — preferring other "
+                        "GPU types for %.1f h (%s)", sku, MIN_EVENTS, WINDOW_SECONDS / 60,
+                        COOL_SECONDS / 3600, reason)
+    except OSError as e:
+        log.warning("lium: could not record %s pod loss: %s", sku, e)
+
+
+def cooling_skus(*, path: Path | None = None, now: float | None = None) -> set[str]:
+    """GPU types with ``MIN_EVENTS`` distinct pod losses inside ``WINDOW_SECONDS``
+    and the last loss less than ``COOL_SECONDS`` ago (case-insensitive keys)."""
+    path = path or sku_outage_path()
+    now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
+    by_sku: dict[str, list[tuple[float, str]]] = {}
+    for e in _load(path):
+        t = float(e["t"])
+        if now - t < KEEP_SECONDS:
+            by_sku.setdefault(str(e["sku"]).lower(), []).append((t, str(e.get("pod", ""))))
+    out: set[str] = set()
+    for sku, evs in by_sku.items():
+        evs.sort()
+        if now - evs[-1][0] >= COOL_SECONDS:
+            continue
+        for i, (t0, _p) in enumerate(evs):
+            pods = {p for t, p in evs[i:] if t - t0 <= WINDOW_SECONDS}
+            if len(pods) >= MIN_EVENTS:
+                out.add(sku)
+                break
+    return out
+
+
+def prefer_healthy(skus: tuple[str, ...], *, path: Path | None = None,
+                   now: float | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
+    """``skus`` without the cooling types — unless that leaves nothing, in
+    which case ``skus`` unchanged (prefer, never forbid)."""
+    cooling = cooling_skus(path=path, now=now)
+    if not cooling:
+        return skus
+    kept = tuple(s for s in skus if s.lower() not in cooling)
+    return kept or skus

@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+"""GPU-type outage cooldown: correlated pod losses steer rents to other types
+(2026-10-21: three H100 pods went dark together; the king re-rented an H100
+and lost it again 13 min in, while an L40 trained the full leg)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from cascade.provision import sku_outage as S
+from cascade.trainer import loop as L
+from cascade.trainer.loop import TrainerRunner
+
+T0 = 1_792_000_000.0
+
+
+def test_two_distinct_losses_in_an_hour_cool_the_type(tmp_path):
+    p = tmp_path / "o.json"
+    S.record_pod_loss("H100", "king-era2593", "pod unreachable", path=p, now=T0)
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0 + 1) == set()          # one loss: no outage
+    S.record_pod_loss("H100", "funded-5fxmxftugkkg", "pod unreachable", path=p, now=T0 + 60)
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0 + 120) == {"h100"}
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0 + 60 + S.COOL_SECONDS + 1) == set()   # expires
+
+
+def test_same_pod_twice_or_losses_far_apart_do_not_cool(tmp_path):
+    p = tmp_path / "o.json"
+    S.record_pod_loss("L40", "king", "x", path=p, now=T0)
+    S.record_pod_loss("L40", "king", "x", path=p, now=T0 + 30)          # same pod
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0 + 60) == set()
+    S.record_pod_loss("L40", "funded-a", "x", path=p, now=T0 + S.WINDOW_SECONDS + 600)
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0 + S.WINDOW_SECONDS + 700) == set()   # > window apart
+
+
+def test_prefer_healthy_never_forbids(tmp_path):
+    p = tmp_path / "o.json"
+    for i in range(2):
+        S.record_pod_loss("H100", f"pod{i}", "x", path=p, now=T0 + i)
+    assert S.prefer_healthy(("RTX4090", "H100", "L40"), path=p, now=T0 + 5) == ("RTX4090", "L40")
+    assert S.prefer_healthy(("H100",), path=p, now=T0 + 5) == ("H100",)       # only option
+    assert S.prefer_healthy(("L40",), path=p, now=T0 + 5) == ("L40",)
+
+
+def test_unreadable_file_is_no_outage(tmp_path):
+    p = tmp_path / "o.json"
+    p.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0) == set()
+    S.record_pod_loss("A6000", "x", "y", path=p, now=T0)              # rewrites cleanly
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0) == set()
+
+
+def _runner(listed=("RTX4090", "H100", "L40")):
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    r = TrainerRunner.__new__(TrainerRunner)
+    r._funded_leg_failures = {}
+    r.cfg = SimpleNamespace(round=SimpleNamespace(funded_pod_skus=tuple(listed),
+                                                  funded_pod_sku=listed[0]))
+    r._sku_per_leg_active = lambda: True
+    return r
+
+
+def test_rent_list_skips_a_cooling_type_and_unreachable_losses_feed_it():
+    r = _runner()
+    assert r._funded_skus_for_rent() == ("RTX4090", "H100", "L40")
+    L._set_leg_phase(r, "5FxMxFTUgKkG6eq", "training", "H100")
+    L._set_leg_phase(r, "5FmuqBcGtX6Scu", "training", "H100")
+    for hk in ("5FxMxFTUgKkG6eq", "5FmuqBcGtX6Scu"):
+        r._record_funded_failure(hk, "remote challenger on funded-x: pod unreachable for 906s",
+                                 miner_fault=False, error_class="infra", burn=False)
+        assert hk not in L._leg_phase_map(r)                    # phase cleared on failure
+    assert r._funded_skus_for_rent() == ("RTX4090", "L40")
+
+
+def test_non_outage_failures_do_not_count():
+    r = _runner()
+    for hk in ("a" * 15, "b" * 15):
+        L._set_leg_phase(r, hk, "training", "H100")
+        r._record_funded_failure(hk, "non-finite loss at step 3", miner_fault=True,
+                                 error_class="generator", burn=False)

+
+def test_leg_phase_keeps_its_original_since():
+    r = _runner()

@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@
+"""GPU-type outage cooldown: correlated pod loss steers rents to other types.
+
+Host quarantine (``record_host_quarantine``) keeps ONE machine out of the
+listings. A supply-side outage takes down many machines of the same type at
+once, and per-host quarantine then just walks the trainer onto the next dying
+machine of that type: 2026-10-21 19:03, three H100 pods (the era-2593 king and
+two payer legs) went unreachable together; the king re-rented an H100 at 19:21
+and lost it 13 min after boot, while an L40 rented at 20:07 trained the full
+leg. This module records pod losses per GPU type and reports a type as
+COOLING once ``MIN_EVENTS`` distinct pods of it were lost inside ``WINDOW``;
+it stays cooling for ``COOL_SECONDS`` after the last loss. Callers PREFER
+other types while one cools (never forbid: if only cooling types are offered
+they are still used — a wait for capacity is worse than a risky rent).
+
+Presentational to consensus: rent policy only, no contract or manifest change.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+SKU_OUTAGE_FILE_ENV = "CASCADE_LIUM_SKU_OUTAGE_FILE"
+WINDOW_SECONDS = 3600.0       # losses this close together are one outage
+MIN_EVENTS = 2                # distinct pods lost inside the window
+COOL_SECONDS = 3 * 3600.0     # prefer other types this long after the last loss
+KEEP_SECONDS = 24 * 3600.0    # events older than this are pruned
+
+
+def sku_outage_path() -> Path:
+    return Path(os.environ.get(
+        SKU_OUTAGE_FILE_ENV, "~/.cache/cascade/lium_sku_outage.json")).expanduser()
+
+
+def _load(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
+    try:
+        raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
+        return []
+    return [e for e in raw if isinstance(e, dict) and "t" in e and "sku" in e] \
+        if isinstance(raw, list) else []
+
+
+def record_pod_loss(sku: str, pod: str, reason: str, *, path: Path | None = None,
+                    now: float | None = None) -> None:
+    """Record that a pod of ``sku`` was lost (unreachable mid-leg)."""
+    sku = str(sku or "").strip()
+    if not sku:
+        return
+    path = path or sku_outage_path()
+    now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
+    try:
+        events = [e for e in _load(path) if now - float(e["t"]) < KEEP_SECONDS]
+        events.append({"t": now, "sku": sku, "pod": str(pod)[:120],
+                       "reason": str(reason)[:200]})
+        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        tmp = path.with_suffix(".json.tmp")
+        tmp.write_text(json.dumps(events), encoding="utf-8")
+        tmp.replace(path)
+        if sku in cooling_skus(path=path, now=now):
+            log.warning("lium: %s pods lost %d+ times within %.0f min — preferring other "
+                        "GPU types for %.1f h (%s)", sku, MIN_EVENTS, WINDOW_SECONDS / 60,
+                        COOL_SECONDS / 3600, reason)
+    except OSError as e:
+        log.warning("lium: could not record %s pod loss: %s", sku, e)
+
+
+def cooling_skus(*, path: Path | None = None, now: float | None = None) -> set[str]:
+    """GPU types with ``MIN_EVENTS`` distinct pod losses inside ``WINDOW_SECONDS``
+    and the last loss less than ``COOL_SECONDS`` ago (case-insensitive keys)."""
+    path = path or sku_outage_path()
+    now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
+    by_sku: dict[str, list[tuple[float, str]]] = {}
+    for e in _load(path):
+        t = float(e["t"])
+        if now - t < KEEP_SECONDS:
+            by_sku.setdefault(str(e["sku"]).lower(), []).append((t, str(e.get("pod", ""))))
+    out: set[str] = set()
+    for sku, evs in by_sku.items():
+        evs.sort()
+        if now - evs[-1][0] >= COOL_SECONDS:
+            continue
+        for i, (t0, _p) in enumerate(evs):
+            pods = {p for t, p in evs[i:] if t - t0 <= WINDOW_SECONDS}
+            if len(pods) >= MIN_EVENTS:
+                out.add(sku)
+                break
+    return out
+
+
+def prefer_healthy(skus: tuple[str, ...], *, path: Path | None = None,
+                   now: float | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
+    """``skus`` without the cooling types — unless that leaves nothing, in
+    which case ``skus`` unchanged (prefer, never forbid)."""
+    cooling = cooling_skus(path=path, now=now)
+    if not cooling:
+        return skus
+    kept = tuple(s for s in skus if s.lower() not in cooling)
+    return kept or skus

+"""GPU-type outage cooldown: correlated pod losses steer rents to other types
+(2026-10-21: three H100 pods went dark together; the king re-rented an H100
+and lost it again 13 min in, while an L40 trained the full leg)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from cascade.provision import sku_outage as S
+from cascade.trainer import loop as L
+from cascade.trainer.loop import TrainerRunner
+
+T0 = 1_792_000_000.0
+
+
+def test_two_distinct_losses_in_an_hour_cool_the_type(tmp_path):
+    p = tmp_path / "o.json"
+    S.record_pod_loss("H100", "king-era2593", "pod unreachable", path=p, now=T0)
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0 + 1) == set()          # one loss: no outage
+    S.record_pod_loss("H100", "funded-5fxmxftugkkg", "pod unreachable", path=p, now=T0 + 60)
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0 + 120) == {"h100"}
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0 + 60 + S.COOL_SECONDS + 1) == set()   # expires
+
+
+def test_same_pod_twice_or_losses_far_apart_do_not_cool(tmp_path):
+    p = tmp_path / "o.json"
+    S.record_pod_loss("L40", "king", "x", path=p, now=T0)
+    S.record_pod_loss("L40", "king", "x", path=p, now=T0 + 30)          # same pod
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0 + 60) == set()
+    S.record_pod_loss("L40", "funded-a", "x", path=p, now=T0 + S.WINDOW_SECONDS + 600)
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0 + S.WINDOW_SECONDS + 700) == set()   # > window apart
+
+
+def test_prefer_healthy_never_forbids(tmp_path):
+    p = tmp_path / "o.json"
+    for i in range(2):
+        S.record_pod_loss("H100", f"pod{i}", "x", path=p, now=T0 + i)
+    assert S.prefer_healthy(("RTX4090", "H100", "L40"), path=p, now=T0 + 5) == ("RTX4090", "L40")
+    assert S.prefer_healthy(("H100",), path=p, now=T0 + 5) == ("H100",)       # only option
+    assert S.prefer_healthy(("L40",), path=p, now=T0 + 5) == ("L40",)
+
+
+def test_unreadable_file_is_no_outage(tmp_path):
+    p = tmp_path / "o.json"
+    p.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0) == set()
+    S.record_pod_loss("A6000", "x", "y", path=p, now=T0)              # rewrites cleanly
+    assert S.cooling_skus(path=p, now=T0) == set()
+
+
+def _runner(listed=("RTX4090", "H100", "L40")):
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    r = TrainerRunner.__new__(TrainerRunner)
+    r._funded_leg_failures = {}
+    r.cfg = SimpleNamespace(round=SimpleNamespace(funded_pod_skus=tuple(listed),
+                                                  funded_pod_sku=listed[0]))
+    r._sku_per_leg_active = lambda: True
+    return r
+
+
+def test_rent_list_skips_a_cooling_type_and_unreachable_losses_feed_it():
+    r = _runner()
+    assert r._funded_skus_for_rent() == ("RTX4090", "H100", "L40")
+    L._set_leg_phase(r, "5FxMxFTUgKkG6eq", "training", "H100")
+    L._set_leg_phase(r, "5FmuqBcGtX6Scu", "training", "H100")
+    for hk in ("5FxMxFTUgKkG6eq", "5FmuqBcGtX6Scu"):
+        r._record_funded_failure(hk, "remote challenger on funded-x: pod unreachable for 906s",
+                                 miner_fault=False, error_class="infra", burn=False)
+        assert hk not in L._leg_phase_map(r)                    # phase cleared on failure
+    assert r._funded_skus_for_rent() == ("RTX4090", "L40")
+
+
+def test_non_outage_failures_do_not_count():
+    r = _runner()
+    for hk in ("a" * 15, "b" * 15):
+        L._set_leg_phase(r, hk, "training", "H100")
+        r._record_funded_failure(hk, "non-finite loss at step 3", miner_fault=True,
+                                 error_class="generator", burn=False)
+    assert r._funded_skus_for_rent() == ("RTX4090", "H100", "L40")
+
+
+def test_leg_phase_keeps_its_original_since():
+    r = _runner()
+    L._set_leg_phase(r, "hk", "waiting_gpu", since=100.0)
+    L._set_leg_phase(r, "hk", "waiting_gpu")                      # repeated poll

fix: never zero a creator day on pricing failure (#178)

* fix: never zero a creator day on pricing failure (fallback source + stale-cache + loud abort)

2026-09-30: a transient CoinGecko 403 zeroed alpha targets platform-wide
for a day; the loss surfaced only when a creator complained (and one
creator's 9/29 payment went out alpha-diluted). Zeroing on pricing failure
is the one failure mode that silently underpays: skipped work is visible,
a zeroed run lies.

- PricingService: CoinGecko -> CoinPaprika fallback (keyless, coin id
  discovered once), then stale-cache with allow_stale=True (weighting and
  publication take a mildly stale price over aborting), then
  PricingUnavailableError.
- _calculate_emission_targets: no more try/except-zeroing. No trustworthy
  price -> the exception propagates and the cycle falls back to the
  visible full-burn path instead of silently paying zero weights.
- _publish_safe: no price -> SKIP publication rather than persist fake
  alpha_target=0 rows into creator-facing history.

Tests: fallback ordering, stale-cache contract (usable for weighting,
refused without allow_stale), publication skip, and the burn-fallback
end-to-end. Suite: 39 passed.

* fix: ruff E501 in _publish_safe (line too long)

-"""Alpha token price and emission-budget lookups for USD -> weight conversion."""
+"""Alpha token price and emission-budget lookups for USD -> weight conversion.
+
+Pricing failures must never silently zero a creator day (2026-09-30: a
+transient CoinGecko 403 zeroed alpha targets platform-wide and the loss was
+only discovered when a creator complained). The rule here is:
+
+- A price from earlier in the process lifetime is better than no price.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,251 @@
+name: PR Review
+
+# Reviews every push to a team pull request, and answers a comment that tags @swarm-reviewer.
+# The review skill and the commands it may run come from the skill repository on every run.
+# The job posts the review with a vote taken from its verdict (approve or request changes); it never merges or pushes.
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, reopened, ready_for_review, synchronize]
+  issue_comment:
+    types: [created]
+
+# A new push replaces a review still running on the same PR; each comment gets its own group.
+concurrency:
+  group: pr-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number }}-${{ github.event.comment.id || 'push' }}
+  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+env:
+  # This repository's settings: the command that installs its packages for tests (empty when CI runs them).
+  REVIEW_SETUP: ""
+
+jobs:
+  review:
+    # Forks get no secrets, so only same-repository PRs; a comment must tag the reviewer.
+    if: >-
+      (github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        && github.event.pull_request.draft == false
+        && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository)
+      || (github.event_name == 'issue_comment'
+        && github.event.issue.pull_request
+        && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@swarm-reviewer'))
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    steps:
+      - name: Token for this repository
+        id: app
+        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
+        with:
+          app-id: ${{ vars.REVIEWER_APP_ID }}
+          private-key: ${{ secrets.REVIEWER_APP_KEY }}
+          permission-contents: read
+          permission-pull-requests: write
+          permission-issues: write
+          permission-checks: read
+          permission-statuses: read
+          permission-actions: read
+
+      - name: Decide whether to review
+        id: gate
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
+          # gh runs before the checkout, so it is told the repository instead of reading it from git.
+          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
+          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
+          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number }}
+          COMMENTER: ${{ github.event.comment.user.login }}
+          COMMENT_URL: ${{ github.event.comment.html_url }}
+        run: |
+          # Anyone can comment on a public PR, so a comment counts only from someone with write access.
+          if [ "$EVENT" = "issue_comment" ]; then
+            level=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$COMMENTER/permission" --jq .permission || echo none)
+            case "$level" in admin|maintain|write) ;; *) echo "Comment from outside the team, skipping"; echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0 ;; esac
+            if [ "$(gh pr view "$PR" --json isCrossRepository --jq .isCrossRepository)" != "false" ]; then
+              echo "PR from a fork or unreadable, skipping"; echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
+            fi
+            kind="the comment at $COMMENT_URL that tags @swarm-reviewer: answer what it asks"
+          elif [ "$ACTION" = "synchronize" ]; then
+            kind="a new push to the pull request: run a follow-up review"
+          else
+            kind="the pull request being opened or marked ready: run a full review"
+          fi
+          sha=$(gh pr view "$PR" --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)
+          if [ -z "$sha" ]; then echo "Could not read the PR head" >&2; exit 1; fi
+          {
+            echo "run=true"
+            echo "pr=$PR"
+            echo "sha=$sha"
+            echo "kind=$kind"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      - name: Assign the author
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
+          PR: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.pr }}
+          AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
+        run: gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$PR/assignees" -f "assignees[]=$AUTHOR" --silent || echo "Could not assign $AUTHOR"
+
+      # An app cannot be requested as a reviewer, so a one-word review puts it in the Reviewers list.
+      - name: Show the review has started
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
+          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+          PR: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.pr }}
+        run: |
+          # A follow-up needs no marker: the reviewer is already in the list from its earlier review.
+          reviewed=$(gh api "repos/$GH_REPO/pulls/$PR/reviews" --jq '[.[] | select(.user.login == "swarm-reviewer[bot]")] | length' || echo 0)
+          if [ "$reviewed" = "0" ]; then
+            gh pr review "$PR" --comment --body "Reviewing" || echo "Could not post the start marker"
+          fi
+
+      - name: Check out the pull request
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.sha }}
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Token for the skill repository
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        id: skill-token
+        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
+        with:
+          app-id: ${{ vars.REVIEWER_APP_ID }}
+          private-key: ${{ secrets.REVIEWER_APP_KEY }}
+          repositories: ${{ vars.REVIEW_SKILL_REPO }}
+          permission-contents: read
+
+      - name: Fetch the review skill
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          repository: ${{ github.repository_owner }}/${{ vars.REVIEW_SKILL_REPO }}
+          ref: ${{ vars.REVIEW_SKILL_REF }}
+          token: ${{ steps.skill-token.outputs.token }}
+          path: .review-skill
+          sparse-checkout: skills/pr-review
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Install the skill and read its settings
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        id: skill
+        run: |
+          skill="$HOME/.claude/skills/pr-review"
+          mkdir -p "$HOME/.claude/skills"
+          mv .review-skill/skills/pr-review "$skill"
+          rm -rf .review-skill
+          rules() { grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$1" | jq -R . | jq -s .; }
+          jq -n --argjson allow "$(rules "$skill/config/ci-allow.txt")" --argjson deny "$(rules "$skill/config/ci-deny.txt")" \
+            '{permissions: {defaultMode: "dontAsk", allow: $allow, deny: $deny}}' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/review-settings.json"
+          {
+            echo "dir=$skill"
+            echo "uv=$(sed -n 's/^uv==//p' "$skill/config/ci-tools.txt")"
+            echo "tools-hash=$(sha256sum "$skill/config/ci-tools.txt" | cut -c1-16)"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      - name: Set up uv
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.3.0
+        with:
+          version: ${{ steps.skill.outputs.uv }}
+
+      - name: Restore the review tools
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        uses: actions/cache@v6
+        with:
+          path: |
+            ~/.local/share/uv/tools
+            ~/.local/share/claude
+            ~/.local/bin
+            ~/.cache/pre-commit
+          key: review-tools-${{ steps.skill.outputs.tools-hash }}-${{ hashFiles('.pre-commit-config.yaml') }}
+          restore-keys: review-tools-${{ steps.skill.outputs.tools-hash }}-
+
+      # A cache hit leaves every tool at its pinned version, so each install below is skipped.
+      - name: Install the review tools
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        id: tools
+        run: |
+          bin="$HOME/.local/bin"
+          mkdir -p "$bin"
+          grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)|^uv==' "${{ steps.skill.outputs.dir }}/config/ci-tools.txt" \
+            | while IFS='=' read -r name _ version; do
+                case "$name" in
+                  claude-code)
+                    "$bin/claude" --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^$version " \
+                      || curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash -s "$version" ;;
+                  age)
+                    "$bin/age" --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^v$version$" \
+                      || curl -fsSL "https://github.com/FiloSottile/age/releases/download/v$version/age-v$version-linux-amd64.tar.gz" \
+                        | tar -xz -C "$bin" --strip-components=1 age/age ;;
+                  *)
+                    uv tool list 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^$name v$version$" || uv tool install --quiet "$name==$version" ;;
+                esac
+              done
+          echo "claude=$bin/claude" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          if [ -n "$REVIEW_SETUP" ]; then eval "$REVIEW_SETUP"; fi
+
+      - name: Review
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        id: review
+        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
+        with:
+          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
+          github_token: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
+          settings: ${{ runner.temp }}/review-settings.json
+          path_to_claude_code_executable: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.claude }}
+          prompt: |
+            Review pull request #${{ steps.gate.outputs.pr }} in ${{ github.repository }} at commit ${{ steps.gate.outputs.sha }}.
+            Use the pr-review skill and follow its CI mode (references/ci-mode.md) from start to finish.
+            The skill is installed at ${{ steps.skill.outputs.dir }}; its scripts are in ${{ steps.skill.outputs.dir }}/scripts.
+            This run was started by ${{ steps.gate.outputs.kind }}.
+          claude_args: |
+            --model claude-opus-5-5
+            --max-turns 120
+            --add-dir ${{ steps.skill.outputs.dir }}
+            --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"verdict":{"type":"string","enum":["approve","approve-with-nits","request-changes"]},"risk":{"type":"string","enum":["low","medium","high"]}},"required":["verdict","risk"]}'
+
+      # The vote comes from the verdict here, never from the reviewer, so PR text cannot talk it into one.
+      - name: Post the review with its vote
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && steps.review.outputs.structured_output != ''
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
+          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+          PR: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.pr }}
+          VERDICT: ${{ fromJSON(steps.review.outputs.structured_output).verdict }}
+        run: |
+          report=/tmp/pr-review/report.md
+          if [ ! -s "$report" ]; then echo "The reviewer wrote no report" >&2; exit 1; fi
+          case "$VERDICT" in
+            approve|approve-with-nits) vote=--approve ;;
+            request-changes) vote=--request-changes ;;
+            *) echo "Unknown verdict: $VERDICT" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+          esac
+          gh pr review "$PR" "$vote" --body-file "$report"
+
+      - name: Encrypt the transcript
+        id: encrypt
+        if: always() && steps.review.outputs.execution_file != '' && vars.REVIEW_LOG_KEY != ''
+        env:
+          TRANSCRIPT: ${{ steps.review.outputs.execution_file }}
+          LOG_KEY: ${{ vars.REVIEW_LOG_KEY }}
+        run: |
+          # Logs on a public repository are public, so the transcript is saved only encrypted.
+          age="$HOME/.local/bin/age"
+          [ -x "$age" ] || { sudo apt-get install -y -qq age > /dev/null; age=age; }
+          "$age" -r "$LOG_KEY" -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/transcript.json.age" "$TRANSCRIPT"
+
+      - name: Save the transcript
+        if: always() && steps.encrypt.outcome == 'success'
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
+        with:
+          name: review-transcript-${{ steps.gate.outputs.pr }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/transcript.json.age
+          retention-days: 90

+            level=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$COMMENTER/permission" --jq .permission || echo none)
+            case "$level" in admin|maintain|write) ;; *) echo "Comment from outside the team, skipping"; echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0 ;; esac
+            if [ "$(gh pr view "$PR" --json isCrossRepository --jq .isCrossRepository)" != "false" ]; then
+              echo "PR from a fork or unreadable, skipping"; echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
+            fi
+            kind="the comment at $COMMENT_URL that tags @swarm-reviewer: answer what it asks"
+          elif [ "$ACTION" = "synchronize" ]; then
+            kind="a new push to the pull request: run a follow-up review"
+          else
+            kind="the pull request being opened or marked ready: run a full review"
+          fi
+          sha=$(gh pr view "$PR" --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)
+          if [ -z "$sha" ]; then echo "Could not read the PR head" >&2; exit 1; fi
+          {
+            echo "run=true"
+            echo "pr=$PR"
+            echo "sha=$sha"
+            echo "kind=$kind"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      - name: Assign the author
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
+          PR: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.pr }}
+          AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
+        run: gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$PR/assignees" -f "assignees[]=$AUTHOR" --silent || echo "Could not assign $AUTHOR"
+
+      # An app cannot be requested as a reviewer, so a one-word review puts it in the Reviewers list.
+      - name: Show the review has started
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
+          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+          PR: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.pr }}
+        run: |
+          # A follow-up needs no marker: the reviewer is already in the list from its earlier review.
+          reviewed=$(gh api "repos/$GH_REPO/pulls/$PR/reviews" --jq '[.[] | select(.user.login == "swarm-reviewer[bot]")] | length' || echo 0)
+          if [ "$reviewed" = "0" ]; then
+            gh pr review "$PR" --comment --body "Reviewing" || echo "Could not post the start marker"
+          fi
+
+      - name: Check out the pull request
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.sha }}
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Token for the skill repository
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        id: skill-token
+        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
+        with:
+          app-id: ${{ vars.REVIEWER_APP_ID }}
+          private-key: ${{ secrets.REVIEWER_APP_KEY }}
+          repositories: ${{ vars.REVIEW_SKILL_REPO }}
+          permission-contents: read
+
+      - name: Fetch the review skill
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          repository: ${{ github.repository_owner }}/${{ vars.REVIEW_SKILL_REPO }}
+          ref: ${{ vars.REVIEW_SKILL_REF }}
+          token: ${{ steps.skill-token.outputs.token }}
+          path: .review-skill
+          sparse-checkout: skills/pr-review
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Install the skill and read its settings
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        id: skill
+        run: |
+          skill="$HOME/.claude/skills/pr-review"
+          mkdir -p "$HOME/.claude/skills"
+          mv .review-skill/skills/pr-review "$skill"
+          rm -rf .review-skill
+          rules() { grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$1" | jq -R . | jq -s .; }
+          jq -n --argjson allow "$(rules "$skill/config/ci-allow.txt")" --argjson deny "$(rules "$skill/config/ci-deny.txt")" \
+            '{permissions: {defaultMode: "dontAsk", allow: $allow, deny: $deny}}' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/review-settings.json"
+          {
+            echo "dir=$skill"
+            echo "uv=$(sed -n 's/^uv==//p' "$skill/config/ci-tools.txt")"
+            echo "tools-hash=$(sha256sum "$skill/config/ci-tools.txt" | cut -c1-16)"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      - name: Set up uv
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.3.0
+        with:
+          version: ${{ steps.skill.outputs.uv }}
+
+      - name: Restore the review tools
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        uses: actions/cache@v6
+        with:
+          path: |
+            ~/.local/share/uv/tools
+            ~/.local/share/claude
+            ~/.local/bin
+            ~/.cache/pre-commit
+          key: review-tools-${{ steps.skill.outputs.tools-hash }}-${{ hashFiles('.pre-commit-config.yaml') }}
+          restore-keys: review-tools-${{ steps.skill.outputs.tools-hash }}-
+
+      # A cache hit leaves every tool at its pinned version, so each install below is skipped.
+      - name: Install the review tools
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        id: tools
+        run: |
+          bin="$HOME/.local/bin"
+          mkdir -p "$bin"
+          grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)|^uv==' "${{ steps.skill.outputs.dir }}/config/ci-tools.txt" \
+            | while IFS='=' read -r name _ version; do
+                case "$name" in
+                  claude-code)
+                    "$bin/claude" --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^$version " \
+                      || curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash -s "$version" ;;
+                  age)
+                    "$bin/age" --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^v$version$" \
+                      || curl -fsSL "https://github.com/FiloSottile/age/releases/download/v$version/age-v$version-linux-amd64.tar.gz" \
+                        | tar -xz -C "$bin" --strip-components=1 age/age ;;
+                  *)
+                    uv tool list 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^$name v$version$" || uv tool install --quiet "$name==$version" ;;
+                esac
+              done
+          echo "claude=$bin/claude" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          if [ -n "$REVIEW_SETUP" ]; then eval "$REVIEW_SETUP"; fi
+
+      - name: Review
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
+        id: review
+        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
+        with:
+          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
+          github_token: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
+          settings: ${{ runner.temp }}/review-settings.json
+          path_to_claude_code_executable: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.claude }}
+          prompt: |
+            Review pull request #${{ steps.gate.outputs.pr }} in ${{ github.repository }} at commit ${{ steps.gate.outputs.sha }}.
+            Use the pr-review skill and follow its CI mode (references/ci-mode.md) from start to finish.
+            The skill is installed at ${{ steps.skill.outputs.dir }}; its scripts are in ${{ steps.skill.outputs.dir }}/scripts.
+            This run was started by ${{ steps.gate.outputs.kind }}.
+          claude_args: |
+            --model claude-opus-5-5
+            --max-turns 120
+            --add-dir ${{ steps.skill.outputs.dir }}
+            --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"verdict":{"type":"string","enum":["approve","approve-with-nits","request-changes"]},"risk":{"type":"string","enum":["low","medium","high"]}},"required":["verdict","risk"]}'
+
+      # The vote comes from the verdict here, never from the reviewer, so PR text cannot talk it into one.
+      - name: Post the review with its vote
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && steps.review.outputs.structured_output != ''
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
+          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+          PR: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.pr }}
+          VERDICT: ${{ fromJSON(steps.review.outputs.structured_output).verdict }}
+        run: |
+          report=/tmp/pr-review/report.md
+          if [ ! -s "$report" ]; then echo "The reviewer wrote no report" >&2; exit 1; fi
+          case "$VERDICT" in
+            approve|approve-with-nits) vote=--approve ;;
+            request-changes) vote=--request-changes ;;
+            *) echo "Unknown verdict: $VERDICT" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+          esac
+          gh pr review "$PR" "$vote" --body-file "$report"
+
+      - name: Encrypt the transcript
+        id: encrypt
+        if: always() && steps.review.outputs.execution_file != '' && vars.REVIEW_LOG_KEY != ''
+        env:
+          TRANSCRIPT: ${{ steps.review.outputs.execution_file }}
+          LOG_KEY: ${{ vars.REVIEW_LOG_KEY }}
+        run: |
+          # Logs on a public repository are public, so the transcript is saved only encrypted.
+          age="$HOME/.local/bin/age"
+          [ -x "$age" ] || { sudo apt-get install -y -qq age > /dev/null; age=age; }
+          "$age" -r "$LOG_KEY" -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/transcript.json.age" "$TRANSCRIPT"
+
+      - name: Save the transcript
+        if: always() && steps.encrypt.outcome == 'success'
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
+        with:
+          name: review-transcript-${{ steps.gate.outputs.pr }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/transcript.json.age
+          retention-days: 90

@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
+# More models from existing providers
+
+Reviewed 2026-10-22 for v0.7.1. These source additions are included in the CLI
+release but are not an admitted production worker or live model rollout.
+Existing keys, discounts, authorizations and deployments remain unchanged.
+No additional provider account type is introduced.
+
+| Provider | Added models | Initial contract |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| MiniMax | Hailuo 02 | Text to video, 6s, 1080p, 16:9 |
+| BFL | FLUX.2 Max, Flex, Klein 4B, Klein 9B | One 1024×1024 PNG |
+| Replicate | FLUX.2 Pro | One 1024×1024 PNG |
+| Runway | Veo 3.1, Veo 3.1 Fast | Text to video, 4s, 720p, 16:9, audio |
+| Luma | Ray 2 Flash | Text to video, 5s, 720p, 16:9 |
+| ElevenLabs | Eleven v4, v4 Turbo, v3, Flash v2.5 | Rachel voice, MP3 44.1 kHz/128 kbps, up to 500 characters |
+| OpenRouter | Veo 3.1 Fast, Veo 3.1 Lite | Text to video, 4s, 720p, 16:9, audio |
+
+These are 15 additional fixed contracts, not every upstream mode. Reference
+images, arbitrary voices, portrait formats and alternate durations are not
+enabled by these contracts. Existing flexible Studio contracts stay separate.
+FLUX.2 image models are not FLUX 3 Max video.
+
+## Miner setup
+
+Use the existing provider key setup, for example:
+
+```sh
+everycli set-api-keys --provider bfl
+everycli set-api-keys --provider elevenlabs
+everycli offers
+```
+
+Do not replace working keys just to add a model. Key presence is not proof of
+account entitlement or funds. Existing provider balance checks remain in use;
+a model addition does not create a separate balance or turn a web subscription
+into API credits. Read the actual offer/readiness state before enabling bids.
+
+## Implementation and release boundaries
+
+- `config/provider-expansion.json` adds new IDs without changing the 47 existing
+  base registry entries or their signed request hashes.
+- The additions use the existing provider adapters, submission-deadline guards,
+  terminal-state handling, receipt binding and media validation.
+- Luma downloads additionally allow its documented `storage.cdn-luma.com` host,
+  without credentials or redirects. Arbitrary hosts remain prohibited.
+- Coordinator discovery includes each addition once, without widening a signed
+  allowlist or enabling an unpriced offer. No price is copied from Fal or an
+  older model. The CLI/UI use that authenticated catalog.
+- Ambiguous paid submissions are not retried. Synchronous speech is input-bound
+  and is not silently regenerated after a worker restart.
+- OpenRouter failures with a null model field now report a terminal failure,
+  matching its documented early-failure response, rather than a model mismatch.
+- Before live routing: review provider-specific prices, run funded paid tests,
+  validate real outputs, build the final immutable worker and verify TEE
+  admission, then publish the signed worker/model allowlist.
+- Updating everycli alone does not activate these models on deployed workers.
+  Worker updates and existing automatic-update opt-in requirements still apply.
+
+## Upstream evidence
+
+Local verification on 2026-10-22: the full Rust release-profile suite passed
+299 tests (including 33 focused provider/protocol/catalog/packaging tests), with
+two intentionally ignored live probes requiring dedicated authorization
+(hotkey identity and paid provider tests).
+The full companion coordinator suite passed 316 tests. Pinned-toolchain Clippy
+with warnings denied, formatting and diff checks passed. Provider HTTP is
+mocked in these suites; public documentation, BFL schemas and the authenticated
+OpenRouter video catalog were checked read-only. The native Linux release build
+passed. One approved live OpenRouter test submission was rejected with HTTP 402;
+the account balance check confirmed insufficient funds. No video was generated
+and no submission was retried. No successful real-media/TEE canary, Docker
+build or production deployment was performed during that local validation. The
+CLI publication workflow separately gates on native CI and container checks. See
+[release checklist](RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v0.7.1.md) for the remaining gates.
+
+- [MiniMax video API](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-t2v)
+- [BFL OpenAPI](https://api.bfl.ai/openapi.json): all four endpoints and their fields were checked directly.
+- [Replicate schema](https://replicate.com/black-forest-labs/flux-2-pro/api/schema)
+- [Runway official SDK schema](https://github.com/runwayml/sdk-node/blob/main/src/resources/text-to-video.ts)
+- [Luma video API](https://docs.lumalabs.ai/docs/video-generation)
+- [ElevenLabs models](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/models) and [speech API](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert)
+- [OpenRouter video API](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/multimodal/video-generation), [Fast](https://openrouter.ai/google/veo-3.1-fast) and [Lite](https://openrouter.ai/google/veo-3.1-lite). Both IDs were also present in the public catalog on 2026-10-22.
+
+Google Imagen is excluded: its [current documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/imagen)
+says it is shut down. Additional Gemini API Veo previews are also excluded:
+the [video guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/video) announces their
+2026-10-22 shutdown. New Gemini image/video APIs need a separately reviewed
+adapter rather than the legacy Veo adapter. Historical contracts are preserved;
+this does not assert that OpenRouter/Runway's separate Veo routes are shut down.

@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+# v0.7.1 release checks
+
+Updated 2026-10-22. This checklist separates CLI publication from production
+worker admission. See GitHub Actions and the release page for publication status.
+
+## Scope
+
+15 new fixed contracts across seven existing providers; see
+[PROVIDER-EXPANSION.md](PROVIDER-EXPANSION.md). Existing contracts, signed
+authorizations, pricing and customer routing are unchanged.
+
+## Verified
+
+- 33 focused Rust tests passed, including historical request hash compatibility,
+  all-provider mock submission/polling, expired deadlines, uncertain submission
+  handling and updater packaging.
+- Companion coordinator: 316 tests passed, including exact registry parity and
+  rejection of unpriced/unauthorized new offers.
+- Final Rust release-profile suite on pinned toolchain 1.97.1: 299 passed,
+  zero failures, two intentionally ignored live probes (dedicated hotkey and
+  paid provider tests). This includes the 33 focused tests above.
+- Release-profile Clippy passed for all targets with warnings denied.
+- Pinned-toolchain formatting and whitespace checks passed.
+- Linux x86_64 release build passed for all three native binaries before the
+  version bump. The publication workflow tests the versioned source again.
+- Authenticated read-only OpenRouter video catalog returned HTTP 200 and listed
+  `google/veo-3.1-fast` and `google/veo-3.1-lite`. This does not prove generation
+  access, funds or valid delivered output.
+
+## CLI publication gates
+
+- Four-platform build/CI and final worker/updater container checks.
+- Branch PR, merge, matching version tag, checksums and installer verification.
+
+## Separate live-mining activation gates
+
+- Funded provider access and paid output validation for the new contracts.
+- Provider-specific reviewed pricing and coordinator quote tests.
+- Final immutable worker image and real TEE admission canary.
+- Scoped coordinator deployment and signed worker/model policy publication.
+
+Those gates are not completed by publishing the CLI. New contracts must remain
+unavailable for routing until their production activation is independently
+verified. Public source does not grant provider entitlements or signed admission.
+
+### Live attempt and current blocker
+
+The Rust adapter submitted one labeled Veo Fast test. OpenRouter rejected it
+with HTTP 402; no accepted job reference was returned. The harness stopped
+without retrying or submitting Veo Lite. Funded provider tests remain incomplete.
+
+No temporary VM was created. No video was delivered, no production routing or
+signed worker policy changed during this validation. CLI publication is separate
+from funded generation tests, final image verification and TEE admission.
+
+The opt-in `tests/live_provider_expansion.rs` harness uses the actual Rust
+adapter, a create-new submission journal and output media checks. It is ignored
+by default; it cannot reuse an existing submission intent. Its first local
+setup attempt rejected an unsupported seed field before any HTTP submission;
+that harness input was corrected before the single HTTP 402 attempt. Clippy
+also passed for the new harness.
+
+## Pricing review notes
+
+Public list prices are evidence for review, not active miner reward quotes or
+proof of the account's actual charge. Taxes, account terms and future provider
+price changes are not included.
+
+| New contract | Published unit rate | Derived fixed-job estimate |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| OpenRouter Veo 3.1 Fast, 4s with audio | $0.10/second | $0.40 |
+| OpenRouter Veo 3.1 Lite, 4s with audio | $0.05/second | $0.20 |
+| Runway Veo 3.1, 4s with audio | 40 credits/second, $0.01/credit | $1.60 |
+| Runway Veo 3.1 Fast, 4s with audio | 15 credits/second, $0.01/credit | $0.60 |
+
+Sources checked on 2026-10-22:
+[OpenRouter Fast](https://openrouter.ai/google/veo-3.1-fast),
+[OpenRouter Lite](https://openrouter.ai/google/veo-3.1-lite), and
+[Runway pricing](https://docs.dev.runwayml.com/guides/pricing/).
+Do not reuse one provider's rate for another provider's endpoint.
+
+BFL's [pricing documentation](https://docs.bfl.ai/quick_start/pricing) confirms
+resolution-dependent FLUX.2 pricing, but the fetched table omitted numeric
+rates. Exact BFL quotes, and the remaining provider prices, still need review;
+no missing rate should be guessed or inherited from an older model.
+
+## Rollout safety
+
+Publish no new routable model until its price, permission and admitted worker
+are all verified. Keep paid tests labeled as tests, do not retry ambiguous
+submissions, and delete a temporary worker and storage after an approved canary.
+CLI installation alone must not silently activate these contracts or opt an
+existing miner into automatic worker updates.

@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+# everycli v0.7.1 — More models from existing providers
+
+This release expands the source model registry and improves provider handling.
+**CLI/source release only: the 15 new model contracts are not yet enabled for
+live mining.** Existing workers, bids, credentials and automatic-update opt-in
+settings are unchanged.
+
+## Added model contracts
+
+- MiniMax: Hailuo 02.
+- BFL: FLUX.2 Max, Flex, Klein 4B and Klein 9B.
+- Replicate: FLUX.2 Pro.
+- Runway: Veo 3.1 and Veo 3.1 Fast.
+- Luma: Ray 2 Flash.
+- ElevenLabs: Eleven v4, v4 Turbo, v3 and Flash v2.5 with the fixed Rachel voice.
+- OpenRouter: Veo 3.1 Fast and Veo 3.1 Lite.
+
+These are fixed text-input contracts, not every upstream format or reference
+mode. The original 47 base contracts and their request hashes are preserved.
+See [supported contract limits](PROVIDER-EXPANSION.md).
+
+## Fixes and verification
+
+- Recognizes terminal OpenRouter video failures even when the provider has not
+  assigned a model field yet; request identity checks remain enforced.
+- Accepts Luma's documented `storage.cdn-luma.com` output host without sending
+  provider credentials to it or allowing arbitrary redirects.
+- Includes the expanded registry in the worker/updater build context.
+- Adds deadline, uncertain-submission, contract-preservation and speech-recovery
+  regressions, plus an explicitly opt-in paid output test harness.
+- Local Rust suite: 299 passed; two live probes intentionally ignored. Companion
+  coordinator suite: 316 passed. These are not proof of funded provider access
+  or final worker attestation. Publication also requires native CI and container
+  build/smoke checks.
+
+## Updating
+
+```sh
+everycli update
+```
+
+This updates the CLI, not the deployed worker. Run `everycli offers` to inspect
+actual model availability. Do not redeploy, bypass attestation or replace keys
+just to enable a registry entry. New models require independently reviewed
+pricing, funded generation/output tests and a compatible signed worker release.
+
+No new production worker or offline-updater bootstrap is published with this
+release. Existing manual worker-update behavior remains unchanged. Kling 4.0
+is not part of v0.7.1.

files.name: PROVIDER-EXPANSION.md
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
+# More models from existing providers
+
+Reviewed 2026-10-22 for v0.7.1. These source additions are included in the CLI
+release but are not an admitted production worker or live model rollout.
+Existing keys, discounts, authorizations and deployments remain unchanged.
+No additional provider account type is introduced.
+
+| Provider | Added models | Initial contract |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| MiniMax | Hailuo 02 | Text to video, 6s, 1080p, 16:9 |
+| BFL | FLUX.2 Max, Flex, Klein 4B, Klein 9B | One 1024×1024 PNG |
+| Replicate | FLUX.2 Pro | One 1024×1024 PNG |
+| Runway | Veo 3.1, Veo 3.1 Fast | Text to video, 4s, 720p, 16:9, audio |
+| Luma | Ray 2 Flash | Text to video, 5s, 720p, 16:9 |
+| ElevenLabs | Eleven v4, v4 Turbo, v3, Flash v2.5 | Rachel voice, MP3 44.1 kHz/128 kbps, up to 500 characters |
+| OpenRouter | Veo 3.1 Fast, Veo 3.1 Lite | Text to video, 4s, 720p, 16:9, audio |
+
+These are 15 additional fixed contracts, not every upstream mode. Reference
+images, arbitrary voices, portrait formats and alternate durations are not
+enabled by these contracts. Existing flexible Studio contracts stay separate.
+FLUX.2 image models are not FLUX 3 Max video.
+
+## Miner setup
+
+Use the existing provider key setup, for example:
+
+```sh
+everycli set-api-keys --provider bfl
+everycli set-api-keys --provider elevenlabs
+everycli offers
+```
+
+Do not replace working keys just to add a model. Key presence is not proof of
+account entitlement or funds. Existing provider balance checks remain in use;
+a model addition does not create a separate balance or turn a web subscription
+into API credits. Read the actual offer/readiness state before enabling bids.
+
+## Implementation and release boundaries
+
+- `config/provider-expansion.json` adds new IDs without changing the 47 existing
+  base registry entries or their signed request hashes.
+- The additions use the existing provider adapters, submission-deadline guards,
+  terminal-state handling, receipt binding and media validation.
+- Luma downloads additionally allow its documented `storage.cdn-luma.com` host,
+  without credentials or redirects. Arbitrary hosts remain prohibited.
+- Coordinator discovery includes each addition once, without widening a signed
+  allowlist or enabling an unpriced offer. No price is copied from Fal or an
+  older model. The CLI/UI use that authenticated catalog.
+- Ambiguous paid submissions are not retried. Synchronous speech is input-bound
+  and is not silently regenerated after a worker restart.
+- OpenRouter failures with a null model field now report a terminal failure,
+  matching its documented early-failure response, rather than a model mismatch.
+- Before live routing: review provider-specific prices, run funded paid tests,
+  validate real outputs, build the final immutable worker and verify TEE
+  admission, then publish the signed worker/model allowlist.
+- Updating everycli alone does not activate these models on deployed workers.
+  Worker updates and existing automatic-update opt-in requirements still apply.
+
+## Upstream evidence
+
+Local verification on 2026-10-22: the full Rust release-profile suite passed
+299 tests (including 33 focused provider/protocol/catalog/packaging tests), with
+two intentionally ignored live probes requiring dedicated authorization
+(hotkey identity and paid provider tests).
+The full companion coordinator suite passed 316 tests. Pinned-toolchain Clippy
+with warnings denied, formatting and diff checks passed. Provider HTTP is
+mocked in these suites; public documentation, BFL schemas and the authenticated
+OpenRouter video catalog were checked read-only. The native Linux release build
+passed. One approved live OpenRouter test submission was rejected with HTTP 402;
+the account balance check confirmed insufficient funds. No video was generated
+and no submission was retried. No successful real-media/TEE canary, Docker
+build or production deployment was performed during that local validation. The
+CLI publication workflow separately gates on native CI and container checks. See
+[release checklist](RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v0.7.1.md) for the remaining gates.
+
+- [MiniMax video API](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-t2v)
+- [BFL OpenAPI](https://api.bfl.ai/openapi.json): all four endpoints and their fields were checked directly.
+- [Replicate schema](https://replicate.com/black-forest-labs/flux-2-pro/api/schema)
+- [Runway official SDK schema](https://github.com/runwayml/sdk-node/blob/main/src/resources/text-to-video.ts)
+- [Luma video API](https://docs.lumalabs.ai/docs/video-generation)
+- [ElevenLabs models](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/models) and [speech API](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert)
+- [OpenRouter video API](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/multimodal/video-generation), [Fast](https://openrouter.ai/google/veo-3.1-fast) and [Lite](https://openrouter.ai/google/veo-3.1-lite). Both IDs were also present in the public catalog on 2026-10-22.
+
+Google Imagen is excluded: its [current documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/imagen)
+says it is shut down. Additional Gemini API Veo previews are also excluded:
+the [video guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/video) announces their
+2026-10-22 shutdown. New Gemini image/video APIs need a separately reviewed
+adapter rather than the legacy Veo adapter. Historical contracts are preserved;
+this does not assert that OpenRouter/Runway's separate Veo routes are shut down.

@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+# v0.7.1 release checks
+
+Updated 2026-10-22. This checklist separates CLI publication from production
+worker admission. See GitHub Actions and the release page for publication status.
+
+## Scope
+
+15 new fixed contracts across seven existing providers; see
+[PROVIDER-EXPANSION.md](PROVIDER-EXPANSION.md). Existing contracts, signed
+authorizations, pricing and customer routing are unchanged.
+
+## Verified
+
+- 33 focused Rust tests passed, including historical request hash compatibility,
+  all-provider mock submission/polling, expired deadlines, uncertain submission
+  handling and updater packaging.
+- Companion coordinator: 316 tests passed, including exact registry parity and
+  rejection of unpriced/unauthorized new offers.
+- Final Rust release-profile suite on pinned toolchain 1.97.1: 299 passed,
+  zero failures, two intentionally ignored live probes (dedicated hotkey and
+  paid provider tests). This includes the 33 focused tests above.
+- Release-profile Clippy passed for all targets with warnings denied.
+- Pinned-toolchain formatting and whitespace checks passed.
+- Linux x86_64 release build passed for all three native binaries before the
+  version bump. The publication workflow tests the versioned source again.
+- Authenticated read-only OpenRouter video catalog returned HTTP 200 and listed
+  `google/veo-3.1-fast` and `google/veo-3.1-lite`. This does not prove generation
+  access, funds or valid delivered output.
+
+## CLI publication gates
+
+- Four-platform build/CI and final worker/updater container checks.
+- Branch PR, merge, matching version tag, checksums and installer verification.
+
+## Separate live-mining activation gates
+
+- Funded provider access and paid output validation for the new contracts.
+- Provider-specific reviewed pricing and coordinator quote tests.
+- Final immutable worker image and real TEE admission canary.
+- Scoped coordinator deployment and signed worker/model policy publication.
+
+Those gates are not completed by publishing the CLI. New contracts must remain
+unavailable for routing until their production activation is independently
+verified. Public source does not grant provider entitlements or signed admission.
+
+### Live attempt and current blocker
+
+The Rust adapter submitted one labeled Veo Fast test. OpenRouter rejected it
+with HTTP 402; no accepted job reference was returned. The harness stopped
+without retrying or submitting Veo Lite. Funded provider tests remain incomplete.
+
+No temporary VM was created. No video was delivered, no production routing or
+signed worker policy changed during this validation. CLI publication is separate
+from funded generation tests, final image verification and TEE admission.
+
+The opt-in `tests/live_provider_expansion.rs` harness uses the actual Rust
+adapter, a create-new submission journal and output media checks. It is ignored
+by default; it cannot reuse an existing submission intent. Its first local
+setup attempt rejected an unsupported seed field before any HTTP submission;
+that harness input was corrected before the single HTTP 402 attempt. Clippy
+also passed for the new harness.
+
+## Pricing review notes
+
+Public list prices are evidence for review, not active miner reward quotes or
+proof of the account's actual charge. Taxes, account terms and future provider
+price changes are not included.
+
+| New contract | Published unit rate | Derived fixed-job estimate |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| OpenRouter Veo 3.1 Fast, 4s with audio | $0.10/second | $0.40 |
+| OpenRouter Veo 3.1 Lite, 4s with audio | $0.05/second | $0.20 |
+| Runway Veo 3.1, 4s with audio | 40 credits/second, $0.01/credit | $1.60 |
+| Runway Veo 3.1 Fast, 4s with audio | 15 credits/second, $0.01/credit | $0.60 |
+
+Sources checked on 2026-10-22:
+[OpenRouter Fast](https://openrouter.ai/google/veo-3.1-fast),
+[OpenRouter Lite](https://openrouter.ai/google/veo-3.1-lite), and
+[Runway pricing](https://docs.dev.runwayml.com/guides/pricing/).
+Do not reuse one provider's rate for another provider's endpoint.
+
+BFL's [pricing documentation](https://docs.bfl.ai/quick_start/pricing) confirms
+resolution-dependent FLUX.2 pricing, but the fetched table omitted numeric
+rates. Exact BFL quotes, and the remaining provider prices, still need review;
+no missing rate should be guessed or inherited from an older model.
+
+## Rollout safety
+
+Publish no new routable model until its price, permission and admitted worker
+are all verified. Keep paid tests labeled as tests, do not retry ambiguous
+submissions, and delete a temporary worker and storage after an approved canary.
+CLI installation alone must not silently activate these contracts or opt an
+existing miner into automatic worker updates.

@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+# everycli v0.7.1 — More models from existing providers
+
+This release expands the source model registry and improves provider handling.
+**CLI/source release only: the 15 new model contracts are not yet enabled for
+live mining.** Existing workers, bids, credentials and automatic-update opt-in
+settings are unchanged.
+
+## Added model contracts
+
+- MiniMax: Hailuo 02.
+- BFL: FLUX.2 Max, Flex, Klein 4B and Klein 9B.
+- Replicate: FLUX.2 Pro.
+- Runway: Veo 3.1 and Veo 3.1 Fast.
+- Luma: Ray 2 Flash.
+- ElevenLabs: Eleven v4, v4 Turbo, v3 and Flash v2.5 with the fixed Rachel voice.
+- OpenRouter: Veo 3.1 Fast and Veo 3.1 Lite.
+
+These are fixed text-input contracts, not every upstream format or reference
+mode. The original 47 base contracts and their request hashes are preserved.
+See [supported contract limits](PROVIDER-EXPANSION.md).
+
+## Fixes and verification
+
+- Recognizes terminal OpenRouter video failures even when the provider has not
+  assigned a model field yet; request identity checks remain enforced.
+- Accepts Luma's documented `storage.cdn-luma.com` output host without sending
+  provider credentials to it or allowing arbitrary redirects.
+- Includes the expanded registry in the worker/updater build context.
+- Adds deadline, uncertain-submission, contract-preservation and speech-recovery
+  regressions, plus an explicitly opt-in paid output test harness.
+- Local Rust suite: 299 passed; two live probes intentionally ignored. Companion
+  coordinator suite: 316 passed. These are not proof of funded provider access
+  or final worker attestation. Publication also requires native CI and container
+  build/smoke checks.
+
+## Updating
+
+```sh
+everycli update
+```
+
+This updates the CLI, not the deployed worker. Run `everycli offers` to inspect
+actual model availability. Do not redeploy, bypass attestation or replace keys
+just to enable a registry entry. New models require independently reviewed
+pricing, funded generation/output tests and a compatible signed worker release.
+
+No new production worker or offline-updater bootstrap is published with this
+release. Existing manual worker-update behavior remains unchanged. Kling 4.0
+is not part of v0.7.1.

+    path = tmp_path / "invite.txt"

+    path.chmod(mode)
+    return path
+
+
+@respx.mock
+def test_drives_join_reads_the_invite_from_a_file(
+    env: dict[str, str], tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    url = _mock_join(monkeypatch)
+    result = run(["drives", "join", "--invite-file", str(_invite_file(tmp_path, url))], env)
+    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
+    assert f"owner        {OWNER}" in result.output
+    assert "role         writer" in result.output
+    assert url.split("#")[1][2:] not in result.output
+
+

+def test_drives_join_reads_stdin_and_emits_json(
+    env: dict[str, str], monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    url = _mock_join(monkeypatch, path_prefix="Work")
+    result = CliRunner().invoke(
+        main, ["drives", "join", "--invite-file", "-", "--json"], input=url, env=env
+    )
+    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
+    row = json.loads(result.output)
+    assert row == {
+        "owner_ss58": OWNER,
+        "folder_hash": FOLDER,
+        "role": "writer",
+        "path_prefix": "Work",
+        "already_owner": False,
+    }
+
+
+@respx.mock
+def test_drives_join_reads_the_environment(
+    env: dict[str, str], monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    url = _mock_join(monkeypatch)
+    result = run(["drives", "join"], {**env, "HIPPIUS_INVITE_URL": url})
+    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
+
+
+def test_drives_join_needs_exactly_one_invite_source(env: dict[str, str], tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    missing = run(["drives", "join"], env)
+    assert missing.exit_code != 0
+    assert "--invite-file" in missing.output
+    path = _invite_file(tmp_path, "https://x.io/invite/t#k=" + "A" * 43)
+    both = run(["drives", "join", "--invite-file", str(path)], {**env, "HIPPIUS_INVITE_URL": "x"})
+    assert both.exit_code != 0
+    assert "once" in both.output
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(os.name != "posix", reason="POSIX file modes")
+def test_drives_join_refuses_an_invite_file_others_can_read(
+    env: dict[str, str], tmp_path: Path
+) -> None:
+    path = _invite_file(tmp_path, "https://x.io/invite/t#k=" + "A" * 43, mode=0o644)
+    result = run(["drives", "join", "--invite-file", str(path)], env)
+    assert result.exit_code != 0
+    assert "chmod 600" in result.output
+
